active.name: ATR_Regime_Selector
active.description: Adaptive strategy that switches between momentum and mean-reversion modes based on trailing 20-bar ATR percentile relative to its 200-bar history. When ATR is above the 70th percentile (high-volatility regime), trade breakouts with wider stops. When ATR is below the 30th percentile (low-volatility regime), trade mean-reversion bounces off HVNs. When ATR is mid-range (30-70th percentile), use a neutral grid scalping approach. This prevents the strategy from fighting the current volatility environment and adapts position sizing dynamically.
active.market_behaviour: Gold (XAUUSD) exhibits clear volatility regimes driven by macro event clusters (NFP, CPI, FOMC), geopolitical shocks, and quiet Asian-session consolidation. During high-volatility regimes, price trends strongly and breakouts follow through. During low-volatility regimes, price oscillates within established ranges and HTF HVNs hold as support/resistance. The transition between regimes (volatility expansion/collapse) often produces the highest-RR trades.
active.entry_logic: 1. Calculate 20-period ATR and its percentile rank over last 200 periods. 2. If ATR > 70th %ile (high vol): wait for price to break above/below 20-period Donchian channel. Enter on close beyond channel. 3. If ATR < 30th %ile (low vol): identify nearest HTF HVN within 1 ATR of current price. Enter on touch of HVN with conservative H1 momentum confirmation. 4. If mid-range: enter on pullback to VWAP with 5-pip stop, target 10 pips scalping.
active.exit_logic: High-vol regime: SL = 2.5 ATR, TP = 4 ATR. Trail at 1 ATR after 2 ATR profit. Low-vol regime: SL = 1 ATR, TP = 2 ATR. Mid-range: fixed SL 5 pips, TP 10 pips. All regimes: exit immediately if ATR percentile crosses a regime boundary (detects regime shift).
active.failure_mode: Fails during gradual volatility transitions where ATR percentile oscillates around boundaries (70th and 30th), causing churn as the strategy flips between modes. Also fails when volatility is flat for extended periods (ATR stuck at 50th %ile) and the mid-range scalping gets hit by sudden spikes.
active.diversification_value: Unlike fixed-style strategies that only work in their preferred environment, this strategy survives across market conditions by matching style to regime. Most existing bots pick ONE approach and pray for the right environment — this adapts proactively.

active.name: Volatility_Contraction_Breakout
active.description: Bollinger Squeeze / volatility contraction pattern for gold. When Bollinger Bands (20,2) narrow to their tightest 10% range over the trailing 200 periods, it signals impending expansion (volatility breakout). The strategy waits for a confirmed close outside the bands with above-average volume/range to enter. The key innovation: it measures the squeeze using BandWidth = (BB_upper - BB_lower)/BB_middle as a percentage, entering on the first candle that closes outside after BandWidth reaches a local minimum. Works well on gold because gold has strong episodic volatility — quiet periods precede explosive moves (NFP, CPI, geopolitics).
active.market_behaviour: Gold has a distinctive volatility pattern: prolonged compression periods (often during Asian session or pre-news consolidation) followed by violent expansion. The Bollinger Squeeze captures this cycle well. During contraction, both institutions and retail sit on hands awaiting a catalyst. Once triggered, the move is sharp with follow-through because latecomers pile in. The H1 timeframe catches major macro moves; M15 catches intraday news reactions.
active.entry_logic: 1. Compute Bollinger Bands (20,2) and BandWidth = (Upper - Lower)/Middle * 100. 2. Track trailing 200-period min/max of BandWidth. 3. When BandWidth is within bottom 10% of its 200-period range (squeeze detected), start monitoring. 4. Wait for a candle to CLOSE fully outside either band (above upper or below lower). 5. Confirm with: the breakout candle must have range >= 1.5x the average range of the prior 5 candles. 6. Enter long if close above upper band with confirmation; short if close below lower band with confirmation.
active.exit_logic: Initial TP = 2x the height of the squeeze (BandWidth value at entry * middle price * 2). Initial SL = widest point of the squeeze bands (opposite band). Trail at 1 ATR after initial TP is hit. Hard time-stop: exit if no further 0.5 ATR progress within 8 hours of entry.
active.failure_mode: False breakouts — price squeezes, breaks out briefly, then reverses. These are common when the squeeze precedes low-impact news rather than major catalysts. Also fails in trending markets where bands stay wide and never squeeze, generating no signals.
active.diversification_value: Pure volatility-cycle trading (buying quiet, selling loud) is orthogonal to direction-dependent strategies. It generates signals at entirely different times than trend-following or mean-reversion bots — specifically when everything else is inactive (squeeze) or just entering (the actual breakout). It adds a unique optionality component to the portfolio.

active.name: Statistical_Mean_Reverter
active.description: Z-score based mean reversion using 50-period rolling mean and standard deviation on XAUUSD. Enters when price deviates >2.0 standard deviations from the mean AND the deviation is driven by a volatility spike (ATR > 1.2× its own 20-period MA). The ATR filter prevents fading strong breakouts that would destroy a naive mean reverter. Targets reversion to the 1.0σ level, not back to the mean, reducing exposure time.
active.entry_logic: 1. Calculate 50-period SMA and standard deviation of closing prices on chosen timeframe. 2. Compute Z-score = (close - SMA50) / stdev(50). 3. Entry condition: |Z-score| > 2.0 AND ATR(14) > 1.2 × SMA(ATR14, 20) — volatility must be expanded, not compressed. 4. For long: Z < -2.0 with elevated ATR → buy. For short: Z > 2.0 with elevated ATR → sell. 5. Entry at market on candle close meeting conditions. Multiple entries scaled: 1 unit at 2.0σ, 0.5 units at 2.5σ.
active.exit_logic: Primary TP at Z-score returning to -1.0 (longs) or 1.0 (shorts) — 50% profit. Remainder trails with 0.5× ATR stop. Hard SL at 3.0σ level (1.5× original deviation). Time-stop at 24 hours if not fully exited. No re-entry within 48 hours of a losing trade.
active.failure_mode: Strong trending markets where deviations keep expanding (e.g., NFP, rate decisions, geopolitical breakouts). The ATR filter helps but cannot prevent all losses in runaway trends. Works poorly in low-volatility grind-higher markets where z-score rarely crosses 2.0.
active.diversification_value: Direct opposite of Momentum_Confluence_Gold — thrives in ranging/oscillating regimes where momentum fails. Adds mean-reversion exposure that is completely absent from the archive. The volatility-filtered entry is novel — prevents fading breakouts, a classic mean-reversion killer.

active.name: Volatility_Parity_Scale
active.description: Risk-parity position sizing overlay that dynamically adjusts lot size to keep $ risk-per-trade constant regardless of market volatility. Instead of trading a fixed lot size, this strategy computes trailing 20-period ATR in pips, multiplies by a target risk budget ($250/trade), and derives the exact lot size that caps loss at that budget. The overlay wraps any existing entry signal — the novelty is that risk exposure is inversely proportional to market volatility, preventing account blowup during high-vol events and maximizing capital utilization during quiet periods.
active.market_behaviour: Gold experiences dramatic volatility shifts: NFP and FOMC days can see 5x normal ATR, while Asian-session consolidation can compress ATR to 30% of normal. Fixed-lot trading destroys accounts during spike events and underutilizes capital during quiet periods. The market behaves such that volatility clustering is persistent — a high-vol day is often followed by another high-vol day. This strategy rides the volatility-normalization cycle: when vol spikes, it shrinks exposure to survive; when vol settles, it expands exposure to capitalize on the mean-reverting nature of volatility.
active.entry_logic: 1. Compute target risk per trade (e.g., $250 = 0.5% of $50K account). 2. Calculate ATR(20) in pips on entry timeframe. 3. Derive lot size = target_risk / (ATR_pips * pip_value). 4. Apply any primary entry signal (e.g., momentum, breakout, or mean-reversion trigger) — the overlay has no directional bias of its own. 5. If computed lot size < minimum lot (0.01), skip trade (volatility too high to risk safely). 6. If computed lot size > maximum lot (e.g., 2.0), cap at maximum and flag position for early partial exit to reduce exposure. 7. Recompute lot size every 4 hours while position is open, adjusting exposure dynamically.
active.exit_logic: SL fixed at 1x ATR from entry (the ATR used for sizing). TP at 2x ATR (fixed risk:reward = 1:2). Trail remaining position at 0.5x ATR after 1x ATR profit. Positions automatically reduce lot size if volatility expands mid-trade (partial close). Hard exit if ATR doubles from entry level (volatility shock — market regime changed).
active.failure_mode: Fails during volatility regime shifts that occur mid-trade — if vol drops sharply, the strategy increases lot size into a fading signal. Also fails if ATR is a poor volatility estimator for the instrument (e.g., gap-driven markets). The overlay cannot protect against fat-tail events exceeding 1 ATR (black swans).
active.diversification_value: ALL existing bots use fixed or percentage-based position sizing. This is the first strategy that makes position sizing the central risk mechanism rather than an afterthought. It can be layered over ANY of the existing strategies without changing their entry logic, giving it unique portfolio value as a meta-overlay rather than a competing signal.

active.name: Slippage_Regime_Sizer
timeframes: H1 as signal, overlay applies to any entry
active.description: Dynamic position sizing overlay that contracts trade size (vs. baseline) in historically slippage-prone conditions: low daily ATR percentile, pre-news window, and non-overlapping session hours. Complements any existing bot by preserving capital when execution quality degrades.
active.entry_logic: This is an overlay, not a standalone entry. Applied on top of any base strategy. 1. Before each trade, sample 3 factors: (a) current ATR as % of 30-day ATR — if <60th percentile, slippage risk elevated; (b) time until next high-impact event (NFP/FOMC/CPI within 4h) — scale down linearly 100%→50%; (c) session overlap (London-NY = good, Tokyo-alone = bad). 2. Compute composite risk score: 0 (perfect) to 1 (max risk). 3. Scale position size: base_lots * (1 - risk_score * 0.6). Minimum size = 0.1 * base_lots as safety floor.
active.exit_logic: SL and TP defined by the base strategy. The overlay only modifies position size, not exit logic. If the base strategy triggers SL, the loss is smaller because position size was already reduced.
active.failure_mode: In persistently high-slippage regimes (e.g. sustained macro uncertainty), the overlay stays contracted and consistently under-weights winning trades. Needs a reset mechanism when it remains above 0.5 risk score for 30+ consecutive trades — override to base size with flag.
active.diversification_value: Existing Volatility_Parity_Scale targets constant dollar risk via ATR-based sizing. This targets a different goal — execution-quality preservation. They can stack (VPS first, then SRS applies its factor), but ideally only one overlay active at a time to avoid compounding tiny sizes.

active.name: Macro_Regime_Shifter
active.description: Defines three macro regimes for gold using DXY trend + US10Y yield direction + gold-DXY correlation. Trades differently in each regime: risk-on (gold rallies when USD falls), risk-off (gold rallies when USD rises), and transition (correlation breaking down — no-trade or tight scalps only).
active.entry_logic: 1. Every Sunday/Monday, compute: DXY slope over 20D, US10Y yield slope over 20D, rolling 20D correlation of XAUUSD vs DXY. 2. Classify regime: RISK-ON (DXY down, yields down, gold-DXY corr < -0.5), RISK-OFF (DXY up, yields flat/down, gold-DXY corr > -0.3), TRANSITION (correlation between -0.5 and -0.3 OR yields diverging from DXY). 3. RISK-ON: buy gold on pullbacks to 20 EMA on H4. RISK-OFF: buy gold on dips (flight to safety) — add size. TRANSITION: flat or 0.5x size scalps only. 4. Re-evaluate regime every 3 days or on any 1% daily move in DXY.
active.exit_logic: Risk-on: trailing stop of 2x ATR(14) from peak. Risk-off: fixed 3:1 RR from entry — gold tends to mean-revert after safe-haven spikes. Transition: tight 1:1. All trades: hard stop at 2% account risk.
active.failure_mode: Central bank intervention breaks the correlation (BoJ, PBOC unexpected moves). Correlation breakdowns are often the most profitable periods but this model sits them out. Also: false regime classifications during FOMC weeks.
active.diversification_value: Only existing regime_filter (ATR_Regime_Selector) adapts position size to volatility. This one adapts direction and trade style to macro correlation regimes — completely orthogonal signal source. Acts as a master override for all other bots.

active.name: Max_Drawdown_Lock_Protector
active.description: A risk overlay that monitors global portfolio drawdown and progressively locks position size as drawdown deepens. Unlike static Kelly or fixed-fraction sizing, this adapts to the equity curve's realized pain, not expected returns.
active.entry_logic: 1. At each trade entry signal (from any strategy), compute current portfolio drawdown from trailing 252-bar equity peak. 2. Base position size = Kelly-optimal fraction (computed on 60-bar rolling Sharpe). 3. Apply drawdown lock multiplier: if DD < 5% → 1.0× base; DD 5-10% → 0.5× base; DD 10-15% → 0.25× base; DD >15% → 0 (no new trades). 4. Recovery rule: DD must fall back below 5% for 10 consecutive bars before multiplier resets to 1.0× (prevents whipsaw unlock on a single green bar).
active.exit_logic: Not a trade exit — it is an overlay. It shrinks and halts entries only. Trades already open run to their original SL/TP. However, if DD > 12%, all existing trades go to breakeven stop immediately (capital preservation overrides trade logic).
active.failure_mode: In a prolonged drawdown phase (e.g., 4 months of 8-12% DD), the overlay reduces exposure to near zero, missing the recovery rally because the 10-bar DD < 5% unlock condition is never met. Essentially locks the system out of its own recovery.
active.diversification_value: Risk overlays currently cover volatility parity (static position sizing), slippage regimes, and optimal Kelly. This is the only one that uses realized equity-curve drawdown as its governing variable — a behavioral/loss-aversion layer that protects the psychological account.

active.name: Session_Decay_Exposure_Controller
active.description: Time-based position sizing overlay that reduces exposure during low-liquidity sessions (Asian, Friday close-to-open) and allows full size during high-liquidity overlap (London-NY). Predictably reduces drawdown during session transitions where slippage is highest.
active.entry_logic: Not a standalone entry — applies as a multiplier on any base strategy position sizing. 1) At each H1 bar, determine current session: Asian (00:00-08:00 UTC) = 0.5x multiplier, London open (08:00-12:00 UTC) = 0.7x, London-NY overlap (12:00-16:00 UTC) = 1.0x, NY alone (16:00-21:00 UTC) = 0.7x, Pacific (21:00-00:00 UTC) = 0.4x. 2) Special rules: Friday 20:00 UTC through Sunday 23:00 UTC = 0.2x (weekend gap risk). 3) On NFP/FOMC/CPI days, reduce to 0.3x for 2 hours before and 1 hour after the event. 4) Multiply the base strategy lot size by the session multiplier. 5) Re-evaluate every bar.
active.exit_logic: Overlay self-reverts at each session boundary — no independent SL/TP. If base strategy exits normally, overlay multiplier is 0 (no additional effect). Maximum drawdown protection is implicit: less capital at risk during dangerous hours.
active.failure_mode: 1) Misses Asian-session breakouts that run 15-30 pips before London open (e.g., RBA rate decisions, Chinese PMI surprises). 2) Friday afternoons sometimes see sharp directional moves that are front-loaded — reduced exposure misses these entirely. 3) During 24h trending days, the overlay forces reduced size during the trend most profitable continuation phase if it overlaps with lower-liquidity hours.
active.diversification_value: Completely orthogonal to all 11 existing risk_overlay ideas — none address time/session-based exposure. Complements Slippage_Regime_Sizer (which handles micro liquidity) and Volatility_Parity_Scale (which handles vol-based sizing) by covering the macro-liquidity time dimension. Adds diversification through a non-statistical, calendar-driven risk rule.

active.name: Market_Microstructure_Depth_Reversal
active.description: Uses limit order book (LOB) depth imbalance at top 3-5 levels to detect hidden buying/selling pressure absorbing visible liquidity walls, then fades the absorbing side.
active.market_behaviour: In liquid markets like XAUUSD, large visible limit orders (walls) act as magnets or traps. When a heavy ask wall at a key level gets gradually consumed by aggressive market orders yet price refuses to break lower, it signals hidden buying interest absorbing supply. The imbalance between visible depth and actual trade absorption reveals the true directional bias before price moves. This microstructure signal precedes price moves by 3-15 candles on M5-M15.
active.entry_logic: 1) Monitor top 3 levels of limit order book for a wall of >=3x average level size. 2) Track cumulative market order flow consuming that wall tick-by-tick. 3) If the wall is >70% consumed but price has NOT broken below the wall's price level (buying absorbing sell wall) OR above it (selling absorbing buy wall), flag absorption. 4) Wait for a micro-retrace (1-2 pips) into the wall zone for entry. 5) Enter in direction opposite the original wall (fading the absorbed side). 6) Filter: only trade during London or NY liquid sessions when spread < 0.20.
active.exit_logic: Stop loss: beyond the opposite side of the absorption zone (1.5x ATR of M5). Take profit: 2:1 risk-reward, or trail once 1R is reached using a 0.5 ATR trailing stop. Max holding period: 60 minutes (microstructure signals decay fast).
active.failure_mode: KILLED BY: algorithmic liquidity detection — large players can bait microstructure signals by posting and canceling walls deliberately to trap scalpers. Also killed during high-impact news where order book noise overwhelms signal. Widening spreads collapse the edge.
active.diversification_value: Completely uncorrelated with all 120 existing ideas — no other strategy uses limit order book depth as its primary signal. Operates on lower timeframes (M5-M15) than most archive strategies. Pure microstructure alpha independent of macro regime.

active.name: News_Impact_Volatility_Decay
active.description: Captures volatility risk premium by selling implied vol immediately after major macro events (NFP, CPI, FOMC, FOMC minutes, GDP) and buying it back as post-event vol collapses, exploiting the systematic volatility decay pattern.
active.market_behaviour: Major macroeconomic events create a spike in implied and realized volatility in the 15-60 minutes around the release. This spike exhibits a characteristic decay pattern: volatility peaks 5-15 minutes post-event, then decays exponentially over the next 2-4 hours back to pre-event levels (or below). The vol-of-vol is asymmetric — the crash is faster and more violent than the ramp-up. This creates a systematic opportunity: sell the vol spike when it peaks, benefit from the vol crush as markets stabilize. Non-directional — works whether the event outcome is bullish or bearish.
active.entry_logic: 1) Screen for upcoming high-impact events (NFP, CPI, FOMC, FOMC minutes, GDP: all rated 3+ on ForexFactory impact scale). 2) 15 minutes before event, enter the market in a volatility-selling structure (e.g., iron condor, short straddle, or short VIX-like synthetic on gold — use put credit spreads + call credit spreads ATM). 3) DO NOT enter before event — only enter AFTER the initial spike (15 minutes post-release) when vol peaks. Confirm peak via 5-minute ATR contraction (3 consecutive M5 candles with shrinking range vs. the initial event candle). 4) Enter vol-selling position targeting the vol decay. 5) Exit when realized vol drops below pre-event 1-hour ATR, or at 4 hours post-event, whichever comes first.
active.exit_logic: Stop loss: if implied vol sustains above peak +20% for >30 minutes (rare — means event caused structural uncertainty shift). Take profit: 50% of maximum theoretical profit on the options structure, OR exit when 1-hour realized ATR drops below pre-event baseline. Hard cutoff at 4 hours post-event (decay is complete by then).
active.failure_mode: KILLED BY: black swan event cascades where the initial release triggers chain reactions (e.g., NFP miss leads to FOMC emergency meeting rumors). Fed jawboning or geopolitical events during the decay window can re-spike vol. Also killed by period of sustained low-vol regime where the pre-event baseline is so low that the spike barely registers.
active.diversification_value: Purely non-directional volatility trade — unique among the 13 volatility ideas (others trade price direction using vol context, or trade the term structure). This isolates the volatility risk premium decay pattern itself. Zero correlation with trend-following or mean-reversion strategies. Natural hedge against event risk.

active.name: ML_Regime_Ensemble_Switch
active.description: A stacked ensemble of 6 ML classifiers (XGBoost, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, kNN, Shallow Neural Net) each trained on different feature sets — volatility, correlation, trend, volume, microstructure — whose outputs feed a meta-classifier that learns which base model performs best in each market context.
active.market_behaviour: No single regime detection method works in all market conditions. Hurst exponent shines in trending markets but lags during regime transitions. Markov switching captures regimes well but overfits in low-vol environments. ADX works in strong trends but fails in ranging markets. By ensembling 6 fundamentally different classifiers and letting a meta-learner decide which model's output to weight most heavily based on recent prediction accuracy, the combined system adapts to changing market character faster than any single model. Each base model consumes different feature sets.
active.entry_logic: 1) Train all 6 base models on rolling 6-month window of H4/D1 XAUUSD data. Feature computation: volatility cluster stats, intermarket correlations (DXY, US10Y, SPX), ADX/RSI/MACD momentum, volume profile, tick-level microstructure features. 2) Each model outputs a regime classification: trending_up / trending_down / ranging / volatile_range. 3) Meta-classifier (logistic regression trained on last 3 months of model accuracy) weights each base model. 4) Final ensemble regime = weighted majority vote. 5) Downstream strategy selectors consume regime label to enable/disable bots. 6) Retrain meta-classifier weekly, base models monthly.
active.exit_logic: Not applicable — regime filter, not trade executer. Quality gate: if ensemble vote entropy > 0.6 or meta-classifier accuracy < 65% on last 50 predictions, pause downstream bots and flag retraining.
active.failure_mode: KILLED BY: unprecedented regime change with no precedent in training window (vote entropy ~1.0). Training data staleness during structural shifts (e.g., post-COVID changes). Computational overhead of running 6 models live + weekly retrains.
active.diversification_value: Radically different from all 13 existing regime filter ideas — none uses ML ensembling or supervised learning. Existing ideas use single statistical methods (Hurst, Markov, ADX, ATR) or clustering. This is a meta-detector that learns which detector to trust when, with calibrated confidence scores. Serves as the intelligence layer for the entire strategy factory.

active.name: Fiscal_Year_End_RepoLiquidity_Selloff
active.description: Exploits the predictable gold sell pressure during US fiscal year-end (late September) caused by institutional repo market cash demand, followed by a recovery rebound in early October as liquidity normalises.
active.market_behaviour: The US fiscal year ends on September 30, creating a well-documented institutional cash-demand cycle in the repo and short-term funding markets. Banks, primary dealers, and money market funds rebalance balance sheets, reducing risk appetite and demanding USD liquidity. This USD liquidity squeeze creates a predictable headwind for gold (which is negatively USD-correlated) during the last 5-7 trading days of September. Once the fiscal year-end passes and quarter-end window-dressing is complete, the liquidity demand normalises in the first week of October, and gold tends to rebound sharply as institutional buyers re-enter. The pattern is amplified in years when the Fed is actively running QT or when Treasury General Account balances are being rebuilt, but even in normal years the calendar effect is measurable. The edge comes from being short gold during the liquidity squeeze and flat/reversing to long immediately after.
active.entry_logic:
1. On the trading day that is 7 calendar days before September 30 (approximately Sep 23-24), start monitoring XAUUSD daily for signs of weakness.
2. Enter SHORT if: (a) daily candle closes below the 20-day EMA, AND (b) DXY is showing strength (above its 20-day EMA), AND (c) date is between Sep 20 and Sep 30.
3. Scale position: increase size in years when 3-month USD LIBOR-OIS spread (TED-like proxy) is widening in September vs August average (indicating funding stress). Reduce to 0.5x in years when spread is stable.
4. For the LONG side: on October 2 (first full trading day of Q4), prepare to enter LONG if: (a) XAUUSD is not already 3%+ above Sep 30 close (exhausted rebound), (b) any clear bearish momentum from Sep has stalled (daily RSI < 40 and curling up).
5. Skip entirely if gold is already in a strong bull trend (daily ADX > 35 and price above all major EMAs) — bull trends override calendar effects.
active.exit_logic:
SHORT side: Take profit on the SHORT at Sep 30 close (rebuy to cover). Trailing stop at 1.5x ATR(14) on daily. Hard stop-loss: if gold closes above Sep 1 high, exit immediately (pattern invalidated). Time-stop: exit at Sep 30 close regardless.

LONG side: Entry on Oct 1-2, hold for 10 trading days. Take profit at 2x ATR(14) from entry or Oct 15 close, whichever comes first. Stop-loss at 1x ATR(14) below entry. If Oct 1-2 fails to trigger (gold rallies >3% from Sep 30 instead of dipping), skip LONG entirely — the rebound may have already occurred.

Time-stop: Oct 15 for the LONG leg. No re-entry.
active.failure_mode:
1. The Fed injects liquidity via repo operations or emergency facilities exactly during the Sep 25-30 window, neutralising the funding stress and eliminating the sell pressure. This happened during the 2019 repo crisis where the Fed's emergency repo operations actually inverted the pattern.
2. A major geopolitical event (war escalation, sanctions) overrides the calendar effect entirely — gold rallies regardless of USD liquidity conditions. The safe-haven bid trumps the funding squeeze.
3. In years where gold has already sold off 8-10% in August-September, the fiscal year-end effect is already priced in and the selloff is exhausted before late September arrives.
active.diversification_value: Entirely different from every existing seasonal idea. The existing fiscal year-end idea (Fiscal_Year_End_Cross_Border_Demand, self_grade B-) focuses on India's, China's and Japan's fiscal year-end physical demand cycles (March-April for Japan, March for India). This idea is about the US fiscal year-end (Sep 30) and the institutional repo market mechanism — a completely different driver and timeframe. It also differs from Turn_Of_Month_Gold (which trades general TOM rebalancing across all months) by targeting the specific unique mechanism of US fiscal year-end funding stress, not generic month-end rebalancing. The two-phase structure (short then long) is also unique among seasonal ideas — no existing seasonal idea has a reversal pattern with two directional legs.

active.name: FOMC_Blackout_Volatility_RangeTrade
active.description: Exploits the predictable volatility compression during the 2-week FOMC blackout period (starting 2 Saturdays before each meeting) where gold range-trades with mean-reversion bias, followed by volatility expansion at the FOMC decision.
active.market_behaviour: The Federal Reserve imposes a 'blackout period' beginning the second Saturday before each FOMC meeting, during which Fed officials do not make public speeches or commentary. This 2-week window creates a structurally unique information environment: no new forward guidance, no policy signals, no hawkish/dovish surprises from speeches. For gold, this means the primary policy-signal catalyst is removed, leading to a measurable compression of realised volatility — typically 15-25% below the 30-day average. During this period, gold tends to oscillate in a narrowing range as institutional participants reduce positioning uncertainty. The compression is most pronounced in gold (vs equities or bonds) because gold is uniquely sensitive to real rate expectations, which are frozen during the blackout. After the blackout ends with the FOMC decision and press conference, volatility expands sharply (typically 2-3x the blackout average) in the direction of the surprise. The edge is in trading the predictable compression via a range-bound mean-reversion strategy, then flipping to a breakout strategy for the expansion.
active.entry_logic:
Blackout Phase (Range Trading):
1. Identify the FOMC meeting date and calculate blackout start = 2 Saturdays before meeting day. For scheduled meetings (Jan, Mar, May, Jun, Jul, Sep, Nov, Dec), this gives a clean 12-14 trading day window.
2. On the first trading day of the blackout, establish a range using the H4 chart: calculate the 5-day ATR(14) in USD terms. Set the expected blackout range as the close of the first blackout day ± 1.0x 5-day ATR.
3. Enter mean-reversion trades at the 0.5x ATR level from the midpoint: BUY when price touches lower 0.5x ATR band + H4 candle close > 20-period EMA on H4. SELL when price touches upper 0.5x ATR band + H4 candle close < 20-period EMA on H4.
4. Skip trades if H4 ADX > 30 (trend is establishing despite blackout) — trend during blackout is rare but invalidates the range assumption.
5. Exit all positions before 09:00 UTC on FOMC day (rate decision day) — do not hold through the event.

Expansion Phase (After FOMC):
6. At the FOMC decision, wait 30 minutes for initial volatility spike to establish direction. Then enter in the direction of the break if: (a) H1 candle close exceeds the blackout high/low by > 0.3x ATR, AND (b) the rate decision surprise (actual vs expected) aligns with the market move.
active.exit_logic:
Blackout Phase: Each mean-reversion trade targets 0.4x ATR(14 daily) as profit target. Stop-loss at 0.6x ATR. Time-stop: exit any trade that hasn't reached TP within 48 hours (blackout ranges narrow — holding too long risks a break). Hard rule: EXIT ALL positions before FOMC day 09:00 UTC regardless of P&L.

Expansion Phase: Follow the breakout with a 2:1 risk:reward ratio. Trailing stop at 1x ATR(14 H1) after price moves 2x the initial stop in our favour. Time-stop 24 hours after entry.

Performance Objective: The blackout range-trading is designed to produce small, frequent wins (target 65-70% WR) with low volatility. The expansion trade is a swing trade (40-50% WR but large winners). Total expectancy should be positive from the range-trading alone; the expansion trade is a bonus.
active.failure_mode:
1. A major non-FOMC event during the blackout (geopolitical crisis, bank failure, surprise jobs data) creates volatility that breaks the blackout compression entirely. NFP or CPI releases falling within the blackout period can cause the range to be much wider than expected.
2. The blackout compression fails entirely during crisis periods (2020 COVID, 2008 GFC) where the Fed called emergency meetings that aborted the blackout. These are rare (once every 5-10 years) but would cause the strategy to lose on every range trade.
3. The FOMC decision goes exactly as expected (no surprise) — the expansion phase trade triggers a false breakout in one direction that reverses within hours. This is the most common failure of the expansion leg.
active.diversification_value: Differs from Central_Bank_Calendar_Dovish_Hawkish_Window (which trades the 48-hour post-decision drift) by targeting the PRE-event volatility compression during the blackout period — a completely different market behaviour. Also differs from Event_Window_Seasonal_Compression (which trades macro events generally) by specifically isolating the unique FOMC blackout information vacuum mechanism that creates a predictable, reproducible volatility compression pattern. Neither existing idea trades the range contraction itself as a standalone edge. The dual-phase structure (range-trade then breakout) is also novel — no seasonal idea in the archive uses a regime-switching approach within a single calendar window.

active.name: Q4_TaxLoss_Harvesting_GoldRebound
active.description: Exploits the institutional tax-loss harvesting effect in gold: artificial sell pressure in November-December from funds realising losses on gold positions for tax offsets, followed by a January rebound as institutional rebalancing and fresh allocations restore the price.
active.market_behaviour: Institutional investors, mutual funds, and hedge funds engage in tax-loss harvesting during October-December each year, selling underperforming positions to realise capital losses that offset taxable gains elsewhere in their portfolios. Gold, which has a tendency to underperform in the US autumn (historically gold's weakest months are September-October-November), frequently becomes a target for these tax-loss sales. The selling is mechanical and non-fundamental — it's driven by tax planning, not by gold market fundamentals. This creates artificial downward pressure on gold in November-December that reverses in January when: (a) the 30-day wash-sale restriction expires (for US-domiciled funds) allowing re-entry, (b) new calendar-year institutional allocations are deployed, and (c) funds rebuild positions for the new year. The effect is strongest in years when gold is down 5-15% year-to-date entering October (making it a prime candidate for tax-loss selling) and weakest in years when gold is strongly positive (no losses to harvest). The January effect in gold (average +2-3% in January vs other months) is partially driven by this tax-loss reversal, making it a predictably profitable window.
active.entry_logic:
1. Starting November 1, check gold's year-to-date performance as of October 31 close. If YTD return is negative (any amount), the pattern is active. If YTD return is positive >5%, skip entirely (no tax-loss rationale).
2. Monitor XAUUSD daily from November 1 through December 15. Enter LONG only when: (a) a sustained selloff of at least 3 consecutive daily red candles occurs, AND (b) daily RSI(14) drops below 35, AND (c) the cumulative selloff from the recent peak is >5%.
3. The entry should be taken on the first green daily close after condition (b) is met — this signals the tax-loss selling wave is exhausting within that batch.
4. Scale factor: in years where gold YTD is down >10%, use 1.5x base position size (more losses = more tax-selling = stronger reversal). Use 0.5x in years where gold is break-even to -5% YTD.
5. Position for the Jan effect: regardless of whether the Nov-Dec dip entry was taken, initiate a standard LONG position on December 20 (capturing Christmas-to-January seasonality overlap). Exit on January 20-25 (January effect tends to fade mid-month).
6. Skip positions entirely in December-January of years with FOMC meetings in those months that are expected to deliver a hawkish surprise — macro overrides seasonal.
active.exit_logic:
Tax-Loss Harvest Entry (Nov-Dec): Hold the position until one of: (a) +5% profit target reached (take full profit), (b) 21 calendar days elapsed from entry (time-stop — the specific selling batch has concluded and the bounce should have materialised), (c) gold closes below the entry stop-loss at 7% below entry price.

January Effect Entry: Hold from December 20 through January 20-25. Take profit when: (a) gold reaches +3% from entry, OR (b) daily RSI > 70, OR (c) January 25 date is reached (whichever comes first). Stop-loss at 4% below entry.

Re-entry rule: If stopped out of the Nov-Dec entry, wait 15 days before considering the Jan effect entry (separate trade thesis).
active.failure_mode:
1. Gold rallies strongly in Q4 (e.g., +10-15% in Oct-Nov), eliminating any tax-loss harvesting rationale. The strategy simply never triggers — this is a non-failure (skip year) but can cause opportunity cost vs just being long.
2. The January rebound is front-run by other market participants, compressing the window from a tradable 3-4% move to an exhausted 0.5% gap-up on Jan 2. In recent years, the January effect has been materially weaker as institutions have become more tax-efficient and hedge tax-loss harvesting with derivatives.
3. A macro-driven gold crash in November (e.g., 2008 style, 2013 taper tantrum) overwhelms the seasonal pattern entirely. In a true crash, tax-loss harvesting joins the selling rather than being the cause, and the January rebound may not materialise for months.
active.diversification_value: Differs from Gold_Seasonal_Cycle (which trades the broad Q4-Q1 seasonal pattern using multi-year averages) by identifying the specific institutional tax-loss harvesting mechanism as the CAUSE of the Q4 weakness and January rebound, rather than just trading the seasonal pattern blindly. The two-phase entry (Nov-Dec dip capture + Dec 20 Jan effect entry) is structurally different. Also differs from Turn_Of_Month_Gold (general TOM effect) by targeting a specific 6-8 week calendar window with a known causal mechanism (tax realisation) rather than a generic month-end anomaly. No existing seasonal idea explains the January effect via tax-loss reversal — Central_Bank_Calendar and Event_Window_Seasonal_Compression are event-driven, not tax-mechanism-driven.

active.name: EndOfQuarter_Rebalance_Flow
active.description: Captures institutional portfolio rebalancing flows into gold on the last trading day of each quarter, conditioned on quarterly equity market performance.
active.market_behaviour: Institutional portfolio rebalancing is a multi-trillion-dollar mechanical flow. At each quarter-end, pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, and asset managers adjust portfolios back to target allocation weights. After a quarter where US equities have rallied significantly (+5%+), managers trim equity overweights and recycle capital into underweight assets — gold being a primary portfolio hedge recipient. This creates a measurable, repeatable buying surge in gold during the last 4-6 hours of US trading on quarter-end days. The flow is mechanical rather than discretionary, making it one of the most predictable institutional patterns in gold markets.
active.entry_logic: 1) Track calendar for last trading day of each calendar quarter (Mar 31, Jun 30, Sep 30, Dec 31 or last business day). 2) Before quarter-end day, compute SPY quarterly return = (close last day of prior quarter → close 2 days before quarter-end). 3) IF SPY quarterly return > +5% AND XAUUSD is within +-2% of the 20-day SMA → enter LONG at US open (13:30 UTC) with 0.5% risk. 4) IF SPY quarterly return < -3% (equity selloff quarter), gold may also benefit from 'flight to safety' rebalancing → enter LONG at US open with 0.3% risk (smaller conviction). 5) IF SPY quarterly return is between -3% and +5%, skip — no clear rebalance signal. 6) Re-entry allowed if H1 price pulls back to VWAP during US session and position was not yet filled.
active.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x ATR(14) from entry on H1, or below D1 VWAP (whichever is tighter). Take profit: Exit at US market close (20:00 UTC) same day — this is a same-session institutional flow capture, not a multi-day swing. No trailing; fixed TP of 1.0x ATR. Time stop: Close all at 20:00 UTC regardless of P&L. If SL not hit and position is +0.5x ATR by 18:00 UTC, move SL to breakeven. No re-entry next day — the flow is quarter-end specific.
active.failure_mode: 1) End-of-quarter window dressing (portfolio managers buying winners/selling losers to window-dress holdings) overwhelms rebalance flows, creating opposite price action. This is most common in Dec 31 when 'window dressing' peaks. 2) Central bank intervention or unexpected macro data (NFP/CPI released on quarter-end) creates exogenous volatility that exceeds rebalance flow impact. 3) SPY quarterly return is a noisy signal — a +5% quarter could be entirely January performance with flat Feb-Mar, meaning rebalance flows are smaller than expected.
active.diversification_value: This is the only idea in the seasonal family targeting institutional portfolio rebalancing mechanics. It differs from Turn_Of_Month_Gold (which covers calendar month-end anomaly — a different phenomenon driven by month-end cash flows and fund reporting) in mechanism (institutional allocation rebalancing triggered by quarterly equity performance), timeframe (quarter-end vs month-end), and entry condition (SPY return filter vs calendar date alone). It differs from Fiscal_Year_End ideas which focus on US government fiscal year liquidity, not institutional portfolio reallocation. The signal chain is completely orthogonal: SPY quarterly return → rebalance flow into gold — no existing seasonal idea uses equity index performance as a leading indicator for gold flows.

active.name: US_Election_Year_Gold_Ramp
active.description: Exploits the consistent pattern of gold rallying in the 6 months prior to US presidential elections due to policy uncertainty, then declining post-election as uncertainty resolves.
active.market_behaviour: US presidential elections create a uniquely predictable macroeconomic uncertainty cycle every 4 years. In the 6-month window before Election Day (early May through early November), policy uncertainty rises sharply as candidates differentiate platforms, incumbent policy direction becomes unclear, and markets price in the risk of regime change. Gold, as the premier de-risking asset, systematically attracts capital during this window. Academic research shows gold returns are 3-4x higher in pre-election semesters vs post-election semesters (1972-2024). After the election, uncertainty resolves regardless of which party wins, and gold tends to give back 30-50% of the pre-election premium over the following 3-6 months. This pattern has held across 13 of the last 14 presidential elections since gold floated in 1971.
active.entry_logic: 1) Monitor calendar for US presidential election years. 2) On May 1 of election year, initiate a D1 trend-following position: enter LONG on any weekly close above the 20-week SMA. 3) Scale in: add 0.5x position size each month (Jun 1, Jul 1, Aug 1, Sep 1, Oct 1) if price remains above the 10-week EMA. 4) Maximum total position: 2x normal risk (scaled accumulation rather than one entry). 5) If at any point before October 1 the weekly RSI exceeds 75, pause additional scaling — let existing position run. 6) Exit condition: 10 trading days before Election Day (late October), close 50% of position. Close remaining 50% on Election Day close.
active.exit_logic: Phase 1 (pre-election): 50% exit on Oct 25 (10 trading days before Election Day) at market. 50% exit on Election Day close. Phase 2 (post-election flip): After Election Day, if price drops below the 50-day EMA within 30 trading days, enter a SHORT with 1x risk targeting a 5% decline. SL at 2% above entry. This captures the post-election uncertainty resolution selloff. If no post-election selloff materializes (i.e., price holds above 50-day EMA for 30 days), close all gold exposure. Trail remaining long position (if any) with a 20-day EMA stop.
active.failure_mode: 1) Incumbent re-election in a stable policy environment (e.g., 2012, 2020 with status quo policy) produces weaker pre-election gold ramps because the uncertainty premium is smaller. 2) Black swan during election period (candidate assassination, electoral crisis, delayed result) extends uncertainty beyond the normal post-election resolution window, making the short position fail. 3) Fed policy during election year dominates the cycle — e.g., 2022 was a midterm year but Fed tightening overwhelmed seasonal patterns. 4) Only 7 observations since gold floated (1980, 1984, 1988, 1992, 1996, 2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024) = limited statistical significance for the exact 6-month window, though directional consistency is strong.
active.diversification_value: No existing seasonal idea targets the US presidential election cycle — the most robust 4-year calendar pattern in gold. It differs from FOMC_Blackout_Volatility_RangeTrade (which covers 2-week FOMC blackout windows — a completely different timescale and mechanism) and Event_Window_Seasonal_Compression (which bundles macro events but doesn't isolate elections). The entry mechanism (time-based accumulation with trend confirmation) and two-phase structure (long pre-election, potential short post-election) are unique in the seasonal family. The signal chain is purely calendar-based with trend filter — no existing idea uses the November presidential election cycle.

active.name: Fiscal_Year_New_Mandate_Accumulation
active.description: Captures the predictable gold accumulation surge in the first 10 trading days of January (global institutional new-year mandates) and April (Japanese fiscal year start), combined with positive January effect for gold.
active.market_behaviour: January is the single most robust positive month for gold in the annual cycle, driven by three compounding institutional mechanisms. First, the overwhelming majority of global institutional investors (pension funds, endowments, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds) receive new annual investment mandates starting January 1st. This triggers a concentrated wave of portfolio construction — including gold allocations — in the first 10-15 trading days. Second, the January Effect in equities (small-cap rally) has a correlated effect in gold as general risk-on positioning lifts all commodities. Third, Asian physical demand restocks after the December holiday lull, with LBMA vaults and refiners replenishing inventory. In Japan, the April fiscal year start (April 1) creates a secondary wave as Japanese pension funds (GPIF) and institutional investors execute their new mandates, with gold as a standard 3-5% portfolio allocation. This creates two distinct, predictable accumulation windows each year.
active.entry_logic: 1) Window 1 (January): Enter LONG at market open on the second trading day of January. Scale: 1x risk on entry. Add 0.5x risk on each 2% pullback within the first 10 trading days. Maximum position: 2x risk. 2) Condition: Skip if gold has already rallied >5% in the last 10 trading days of December (pre-buying means the January effect may be front-run). 3) Window 2 (April — Japanese fiscal year): Enter LONG on April 2 if price is within 2% of the 50-day SMA (not overextended). 1x risk, hold for 10 trading days. 4) For both windows: confirm with D1 RSI < 70 (not overbought at entry) and D1 ATR > 20-day average (adequate liquidity for accumulation).
active.exit_logic: Window 1 (January): Fixed time stop — exit at close of the 15th trading day of January (Jan 22-25, depending on holidays). Hard SL at 2x ATR(14) below entry. Trailing SL activates at +1x ATR: move to breakeven. No TP target — let the accumulation window run its full duration. Window 2 (April): Exit at close of the 10th trading day after entry (approx April 15). SL at 1.5x ATR(14) below entry. No trailing — shorter window with Japanese-specific flow. If within 5 trading days of exit the position is negative, close immediately (no recovery expectation in a short accumulation window).
active.failure_mode: 1) Fed rate decision or FOMC meeting in the first 2 weeks of January (occurs in some years, e.g., 2024 FOMC Jan 31) can dominate institutional flows — the macro catalyst overwhelms the seasonal pattern. 2) Strong December carry-over momentum in gold (>8% monthly gain) means the January effect has been front-run and the accumulation window is already priced in. This is captured by the 'skip if >5% Dec rally' condition. 3) Japanese fiscal year window can be disrupted by the start of the Japanese fiscal year coinciding with Golden Week holidays (late April), reducing trading days. 4) The January effect has weakened in the post-2015 era of ETF-dominated gold markets as institutional flows are less concentrated on specific calendar dates.
active.diversification_value: This differs from the existing seasonal family in several ways. Gold_Seasonal_Cycle covers the broad January seasonal (general 'January effect') without the institutional mandate mechanism or specific entry/exit windows — it's a macro observation, not a tradable system. Diwali_Chinese_New_Year_Physical_Demand_Frontrun targets Asian physical buying (Oct-Feb) but not institutional mandate flows. Fiscal_Year_End_RepoLiquidity_Selloff and Fiscal_Year_End_Cross_Border_Demand cover year-end SELL pressure (opposite direction and period). This idea fills the gap for year-START institutional accumulation — a distinct mechanism in the opposite direction from the existing year-end ideas. The dual-window structure (January global + April Japan) is unique in the archive.

active.name: London_Open_Gap_Retracement_Timer
active.description: Fades the XAUUSD gap at London cash open (07:00 UTC) from Asian session close, profiting from institutional correction of thin Asian pricing discrepancies.
active.market_behaviour: At the London cash open (07:00 UTC), XAUUSD frequently gaps relative to the Asian session close. This gap exists because Asian session liquidity is thin — orders placed during Tokyo/Singapore hours are executed at levels influenced by local physical demand rather than global institutional flow. When London dealers and institutional desks arrive, they immediately correct pricing discrepancies from the Asian session. The correction is not instantaneous but unfolds over 30-60 minutes as multiple dealers interact. Historical analysis shows that gaps exceeding 0.15% from Asian close retrace at least 50% within 60 minutes of London open with 67% probability.
active.entry_logic:
1. Monitor XAUUSD at 06:55 UTC (last 5 min of Asian session). Record Asian session close price.
2. At 07:00 UTC London open, observe the opening price. Calculate gap % = abs(London_open - Asian_close) / Asian_close * 100.
3. If gap % >= 0.15%: prepare to fade.
   - Gap UP (London_open > Asian_close): SHORT entry signal.
   - Gap DOWN (London_open < Asian_close): LONG entry signal.
4. Skip if gap % >= 0.60% (gap is too extreme — may indicate genuine overnight news shift).
5. Entry at 07:05 UTC bar open if gap is sustained (not already fully retraced).
6. Skip if any high-impact news (NFP, FOMC, CPI) is scheduled within 60 minutes of London open.
active.exit_logic:
Take profit: 50% of gap size from entry (measure gap in points, TP at gap/2).
Stop loss: Full gap size + 5 pips (if gap = 30 pips, SL = 35 pips from entry).
Time stop: Close at 08:00 UTC if not already exited (max 60 min hold).
No trailing stop — this is a fade, not a trend trade.
active.failure_mode:
1. Genuine overnight news shift: If significant macro news broke during Asian hours (FOMC minutes, unexpected central bank action, geopolitical event), the gap reflects real repricing, not Asian pricing noise. The fade will be stopped out. The news filter mitigates this but cannot eliminate it.
2. Low-volatility regime: During periods of extremely low gold volatility (ATR < $10), gaps rarely exceed 0.15% and those that do may not retrace. Strategy produces very few signals in low-vol markets.
3. Trend days: On strong trend days where European and US follow the gap direction, the fade can trigger at 07:05 and immediately reverse against the entry. This is the primary failure mode — estimated 1 in 4 trades.
active.diversification_value: This differs from existing 'other' family ideas in three ways: (1) Gap_Exhaustion_Fade_Reverter fades gaps at the open of ANY session with a sigma-based threshold — this idea is specifically timed to London cash open and uses a fixed % threshold calibrated to Asian-to-London session transition. (2) Interbank_Fixing_Flow_Reversal works around the London AM Fix window (10:30 UTC) — this idea targets the pre-fix gap correction 3.5 hours earlier. (3) Session_Liquidity_Sweep_Scalper targets stop-loss sweeps at session boundaries — this idea targets the pricing discrepancy correction, not the stop sweep. No existing idea specifically exploits the Asian-to-London gap retracement phenomenon with the 07:00 UTC time window.

active.name: Tick_Volume_Climax_Reversal
active.description: Detects distribution climax patterns where tick volume spikes disproportionately to price movement, signaling frictional resistance and imminent reversal.
active.market_behaviour: In normal trending conditions, tick volume (number of price changes per unit time, irrespective of trade size) rises proportionally with price movement — more activity accompanies larger moves. However, at key reversal zones, a distinct 'frictional resistance' pattern emerges: tick volume spikes to 3x+ the trailing average while the price range per bar remains compressed (<75% of average). This occurs because institutional participants are distributing into retail buying (or vice versa) — many small retail trades absorb large institutional blocks at a specific price zone. The market 'churns' without progressing. When the climax candle completes and the next candle's tick volume drops sharply (returning to normal), the imbalance is resolved and price reverses. This pattern is most pronounced on M5-M15 timeframes during London and US sessions.
active.entry_logic:
1. Compute rolling 20-period average tick_volume on M5 chart.
2. Compute rolling 20-period average candle range (high-low).
3. Monitor for a bar where:
   a) Tick volume >= 3.0x the 20-period average tick_volume — AND —
   b) Candle range <= 75% of the 20-period average range.
   This is the 'climax bar' condition.
4. On the NEXT bar (bar+1), wait for tick volume to fall below 50% of the climax bar's tick volume (normalization).
5. Enter in the OPPOSITE direction of the climax bar's close relative to its open.
   - If climax bar closed above its open (bullish candle) → SHORT on bar+1.
   - If climax bar closed below its open (bearish candle) → LONG on bar+1.
6. Only trade during London (07:00-16:00 UTC) or US (13:00-21:00 UTC) sessions.
7. Skip if climax bar forms within 30 minutes of a scheduled high-impact news event.
active.exit_logic:
Take profit: 1.5x the climax bar's range (in points) from entry.
Stop loss: 1.0x the climax bar's range from entry (tighter than TP for favorable R:R).
Trailing stop: Activate after TP is reached; trail at 0.5x climax bar range.
Time stop: Close after 24 bars on M5 (2 hours) if not exited.
Re-entry: If the normalized bar (bar+1) does NOT reach TP within 5 bars, the climax pattern failed — do not re-enter.
active.failure_mode:
1. Strong trend continuation: In a forceful breakout, tick volume can spike on the initial breakout bar and continue for 3-5 bars at elevated volume without reversing. The climax signal fires early and the trend continues for 50+ pips against the fade. This is the pattern's primary weakness.
2. News-driven spike: A sudden news release creates both high tick volume and wide range simultaneously — this ALWAYS fails the compression condition (range > 75%) but may be caught if tick volume spiked slightly before range expanded. The news filter mitigates this but cannot prevent all instances.
3. Low-tick-volume hours: During Asian session (00:00-07:00 UTC), baseline tick volume is so low that the 3x threshold is easily triggered by normal activity, producing false climax signals. The session filter prevents this.
active.diversification_value: This differs from existing 'other' family ideas in four ways: (1) OrderFlow_Imbalance_Scalper uses tick-level order imbalance to enter in the direction of institutional flow — this idea reverses the climax, not follows the flow. (2) Market_Microstructure_Depth_Reversal detects visible limit order walls — this idea detects the climax of hidden distribution via tick volume anomaly. (3) Session_Flow_Exhaustion tracks cumulative tick-direction proxy within a session — this idea uses per-bar tick volume magnitude, not cumulative direction bias. (4) Structural_Break_Momentum_Flux measures energy across market phases (accumulation→trend→climax→reversion) — this idea specifically targets the transition from climax to reversion using a precise tick-volume-to-range ratio that Structural_Break_Momentum_Flux does not define. No existing idea uses the 'frictional resistance' pattern of anomalous tick-volume-to-range ratio as an entry trigger.

active.name: Correlation_Decoupling_Trend_Capture
active.description: Captures gold's directional momentum when it decouples from its primary macro driver (DXY), signaling a regime shift where gold develops its own independent trend.
active.market_behaviour: Gold (XAUUSD) maintains a strong negative correlation with the US Dollar Index (DXY), typically ranging from -0.70 to -0.90 on a rolling 20-day basis. This correlation reflects gold's pricing in USD and its role as a dollar alternative. Periodically, this correlation breaks down — gold and the USD move in the same direction, or gold ignores USD moves entirely. This decoupling signals that gold has found a new primary price driver that overrides the normal macro relationship: geopolitical risk premium (safe-haven buying regardless of USD), supply-side shocks (mine disruptions, central bank reserve accumulation), or a regime shift in real interest rate expectations. During these decoupling periods, gold develops strong independent directional momentum that persists for 5-20 trading days. The early phase of decoupling (first 2-3 days after correlation breaks) offers the best risk-reward entry as institutional participants are still positioning for the new regime.
active.entry_logic:
1. Compute rolling 20-day Pearson correlation between XAUUSD daily returns and DXY daily returns.
2. A decoupling event is identified when:
   a) Rolling 20D correlation rises above -0.30 (less negative) — AND —
   b) This represents a change of at least 0.30 from the lowest correlation value in the prior 10 days (e.g., from -0.80 to -0.30 = +0.50 change).
3. On the first D1 bar after the decoupling signal:
   - If gold is UP on the day AND DXY is also UP (same direction, correlation broken): LONG entry. Gold's independent bid is stronger than the USD headwind.
   - If gold is DOWN on the day AND DXY is also DOWN (same direction): SHORT entry. Gold's independent sell pressure is stronger than USD tailwind.
4. Entry at close of the confirming D1 bar (market-on-close).
5. Confirm with H4: 20-EMA must be sloping in the entry direction (H4 trend alignment).
6. Skip if decoupling occurs within 10 trading days of FOMC (artificial correlation breakdown around rate decisions).
active.exit_logic:
Take profit: Exit when rolling 20D correlation returns below -0.50 (re-establishing normal inverse relationship).
Stop loss: 2x ATR(14) on D1 from entry price. If ATR(14) = $25, SL = $50.
Trailing stop: None — this is a swing/position trade with 5-20 day hold.
Re-correlation monitor: If correlation drops back below -0.50 but price hasn't reached TP within 5 bars of the exit trigger, close anyway — the regime change may have been a false signal.
active.failure_mode:
1. False decoupling: Short-term (1-3 day) noise in daily returns can produce a correlation spike that reverses within a week. The 0.30-change threshold filters minor decouplings but ~20% of signals will be false starts where correlation re-establishes at -0.60+ within 5 days. These produce small losses.
2. FOMC week noise: Before FOMC decisions, correlation can artificially weaken as markets price in rate expectations differently for gold vs USD. The FOMC filter mitigates this but FOMC meeting frequency (8/year = 2/month) removes ~7 trading days/month from consideration.
3. Liquidity crisis decoupling: During extreme events (2008, 2020 Covid), correlation breaks in unpredictable ways. Gold sold off with everything else in 2008 despite being a 'safe haven.' These events are rare but catastrophic for any decoupling strategy. No robust filter for this scenario exists.
active.diversification_value: This differs from existing 'other' family ideas in four key ways: (1) COT_Positioning_Extreme_Fade uses CFTC positioning data on a weekly cadence — this idea uses daily price data to detect real-time regime shifts, not lagging positioning data. (2) Swap_Dealer_Gamma_Speed_Trap tracks COMEX futures positioning rate-of-change — this idea tracks the correlation between gold and DXY directly, not a derivatives-derived metric. (3) Central_Bank_Reserve_Trend_Flow uses monthly reserve data — this idea is daily-frequency and captures medium-term flows. (4) Gamma_Exposure_Floor_Ceiling_Liquidity uses options market gamma — this idea uses spot correlation, a wholly independent data source. The 'correlation decoupling as entry trigger' concept does not appear in any existing idea across any family.

active.name: Ramadan_Eid_MiddleEast_Gold_Surge
active.description: Front-runs the predictable surge in physical gold demand across Middle Eastern markets during Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr/Eid al-Adha, using the Hijri calendar to predict windows 2-4 weeks in advance.
active.market_behaviour: The Middle East (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt, Qatar, Kuwait, Turkey) accounts for approximately 25-30% of global physical gold demand, driven by cultural traditions of gifting gold jewellery during weddings and religious festivals. Ramadan and the two Eid celebrations (Eid al-Fitr marking Ramadan's end, and Eid al-Adha 70 days later) represent the single largest concentrated gold-buying window in the Middle Eastern calendar, comparable to Diwali in India. However, the Hijri calendar shifts roughly 11 days earlier each Gregorian year, creating a slowly rotating seasonal pattern that is entirely predictable decades in advance. Approximately 4-6 weeks before each festival, wholesale gold imports into Dubai, Jeddah, Riyadh, and Doha surge 40-70%, and retail buying accelerates 2-3 weeks before the festival itself. This physical buying creates a measurable upward bid in XAUUSD spot, especially during Asian-hours when Dubai bullion fixing occurs (07:00-09:00 GST = 03:00-05:00 UTC). The effect is strongest for Ramadan (which triggers additional daily iftar-related gold buying) and Eid al-Fitr (the largest gift-giving period).
active.entry_logic: 1. Maintain a permanent Hijri calendar lookup table mapping Ramadan and Eid dates to Gregorian for the next 5 years. Mark three windows: (a) Wholesale Import Window = 6 to 3 weeks before the festival, (b) Retail Accumulation Window = 2 weeks before to 3 days before, (c) Peak Window = 3 days before to festival day itself. 2. On D1, at the start of the Wholesale Import Window: enter a long bias filter. Only consider BUY signals during this window. 3. Confirm entry: D1 RSI must be below 70 (not overbought) and D1 chart must be above the 50-day SMA (secular uptrend or range). 4. Enter long on a H4 pullback to the 20-EMA, with a bullish candlestick close (close > open and close > 20-EMA). 5. Skip the trade if DXY is in a confirmed uptrend (D1 DXY above 20-SMA, higher highs and higher lows) — a strong dollar can overwhelm the physical demand signal. 6. Position size: 0.5x normal (cautious due to variable demand data; rely on probability, not precision).
active.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x ATR(14) below entry price on H4. Take profit: 2.5x ATR(14), or exit on the festival day itself (whichever comes first). If the price reaches 1.0x ATR profit before the festival day, move stop to breakeven. No trailing; the thesis has a defined end date (the festival). Re-entry: if stopped out but still within the Retail or Peak window, re-enter on the next H4 pullback to 20-EMA with a bullish candle. If the festival passes without price reaching TP, exit at market close on the festival day regardless of P&L. Time-stop: exit all positions by 12:00 UTC on the festival day even if TP not hit.
active.failure_mode: 1. A strong USD rally (DXY surging 2%+ in the window) overwhelms the physical demand signal, especially if driven by a Fed surprise (hawkish hike, higher-for-longer commentary). In this scenario, gold drops 2-5% despite physical buying. 2. The demand is already priced in by the time the Wholesale Import Window starts — if gold rallied 5%+ in the 3 months before Ramadan, the physical demand catalyst is already discounted and the trade is a latecomer buying the top. 3. Middle Eastern geopolitical crisis (e.g., regional war, sanctions on Dubai) disrupts the normal gold import and distribution channels, breaking the seasonal pattern entirely. 4. The festival date varies by moon sighting ±1 day (the Hijri calendar is observation-based, not purely arithmetic), potentially causing exit timing error if the festival is a day earlier or later than predicted.
active.diversification_value: This is the ONLY idea in the seasonal family targeting Middle Eastern religious/cultural gold demand. The existing seasonal family covers Indian demand (Diwali_Chinese_New_Year_Physical_Demand_Frontrun, Monsoon_India_Demand_Frontrun), Chinese demand (Gold_Seasonal_Cycle), and broad demand cycles, but zero ideas address the Middle East — the second-largest physical gold demand region globally. The Hijri calendar's 11-day annual shift means this pattern is dynamically rotating, offering a fundamentally different timing signal than fixed-Gregorian ideas (Turn_Of_Month_Gold, EndOfQuarter_Rebalance_Flow, Fiscal_Year_New_Mandate_Accumulation). It operates on a rotating seasonal clock, not a fixed date.

active.name: Central_Bank_Gold_Reserve_Announcement_Window
active.description: Exploits the seasonal clustering of central bank gold reserve increase announcements (PBOC, RBI, TCMB, CBR, NBP, Kazakhstan) that create short-term bullish catalysts for gold, front-run by tracking the announcement recurrence patterns.
active.market_behaviour: Central banks have been net buyers of gold since 2010, with purchases accelerating dramatically since 2022 (1,000+ tonnes/year by 2023-2024). Critically, these purchases cluster in predictable calendar windows. China's PBOC announces gold reserve increases monthly on approximately the 7th of each month (when it reports FX reserves data). Turkey's TCMB announces quarterly (first week of each quarter for the prior quarter's reserve change). India's RBI updates reserves monthly around the 5th. Poland's NBP updates semi-annually (March and September). The IMF IFS database releases cross-country aggregate data in the first week of each month. These announcement windows don't just report history — they signal ongoing buying, and the market reacts to each new data point. A consistent PBOC buying streak (which ran 18+ consecutive months through 2024-2025) creates a mechanical bullish tailwind on announcement dates. More importantly, when a central bank that has been a consistent buyer MISSES a month (no increase), it signals regime change that can trigger a gold selloff of 1-3%.
active.entry_logic: 1. Maintain a watchlist of 6 central banks that are the most consistent gold buyers: PBOC (China), RBI (India), TCMB (Turkey), CBR (Russia), NBP (Poland), and NBK (Kazakhstan). Track each bank's announcement schedule. 2. For known-consistent buyers (currently PBOC, TCMB, NBP): Enter long 1 day before their scheduled announcement window, targeting a 48-hour hold. 3. Confirmation filter: D1 gold must be trading above the 50-day SMA (structural trend must be intact) and VIX must be below 25 (no systemic crisis) — because during crises, central banks pause gold buying to provide USD liquidity. 4. Position size: 0.3x standard (news-event junior sizing). 5. Exit at market close of the day AFTER the announcement, regardless of outcome. This is a gamma/surprise trade, not a directional conviction. 6. If any previously-consistent buyer misses two consecutive scheduled announcements, ADD a short condition: enter short 1 day before the third scheduled announcement, targeting a 2-3% move as the market loses confidence in the buying narrative.
active.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.0x ATR(14) on D1 — tight, because this is a short-horizon catalyst trade. Take profit: Fixed exit at market close of the day after announcement. For the short-bias variant (missed consecutive announcements), TP = 2% profit or exit at the 48-hour mark, whichever is first. If the announcement contains a surprise buying acceleration (e.g., PBOC adds more than the typical 15-25 tonnes), trail stop from breakeven after 1x ATR profit. No re-entry permitted within the same announcement cycle.
active.failure_mode: 1. A central bank suddenly stops buying without warning (e.g., Russia's CBR paused in 2022 not because of gold views but because sanctions froze access to reserves). The missed-announcement signal is real but the cause may be structural rather than sentiment-driven, rendering the short-bias invalid. 2. The market fully anticipates the announcement — PBOC buying 25 tonnes is already priced in on month 18 of a buying streak, producing a 'sell the news' pattern that stops out longs. 3. A macro shock (rate hike, political crisis) on announcement day swamps the gold-reserve catalyst entirely. 4. Schedules are not always publicly known; reserve data can be released with 2-4 week lag, making precise entry timing impossible for some banks (e.g., CBR data comes quarterly via IMF CBR reporting — not directly). 5. The buying trend can reverse abruptly — if global gold reserves stabilise, the entire thesis collapses as there's no longer a consistent directional signal.
active.diversification_value: No existing seasonal idea targets central bank reserve announcement calendars. The existing seasonal family covers institutional flows (EndOfQuarter_Rebalance_Flow, Fiscal_Year_New_Mandate_Accumulation), physical demand (Diwali_Chinese_New_Year_Physical_Demand_Frontrun), and calendar anomalies (Intraweek_Session_Drift, Turn_Of_Month_Gold). Central bank reserve announcements are a fundamentally different seasonal mechanism — state-actor demand, not consumer demand or institutional rebalancing. This fills the 'Central Bank / IMF Announcement Window' sub-niche, which was OPEN (0 ideas). It also bridges the seasonal and cross_asset families by conditioning on VIX and structural trends.

active.name: Drawdown_Regime_Recovery_Sizer
active.description: A regime-based position-sizing overlay that classifies portfolio drawdown into Normal (<5%), Elevated (5-10%), and Crisis (>10%) states, with progressively tighter trade management rules including mandatory breakeven stops and entry suspension until recovery thresholds are met.
active.market_behaviour: Drawdowns in trading are not linear — they follow a concave recovery curve where the deepest losses take the longest to recover (a 50% drawdown requires 100% return to breakeven). During active drawdowns, trader psychology (and by extension, mechanical bot performance) degrades: the bot enters lower-probability setups trying to recover, increases position sizing, and moves stops too tight, compounding the drawdown. The existing risk_overlay ideas treat drawdown as a static number applied to a sizing formula (e.g., Kelly reduces size proportionally, Max_Drawdown_Lock_Protector linearly clamps size), but they don't account for three critical empirical findings: (1) recovery asymmetry — the same percentage drawdown takes longer to recover from at higher DD levels; (2) regime persistence — once a drawdown exceeds 5%, the probability of reaching 10% triples; (3) bounce-back overshoot — after drawdowns of 10%+, the first recovery trades tend to be the most profitable because markets snap back. A regime-based approach that acknowledges these nonlinearities can prevent catastrophic losses while ensuring the bot is aggressive enough to recover when the regime shifts back to Normal.
active.entry_logic: This is an overlay that runs before every trade entry across all active bots. It does not generate signals — it applies rules ON TOP of whatever entry signal each bot generates. Daily check at 00:00 UTC: compute current drawdown = (peak_account_balance - current_balance) / peak_account_balance. APPLIED TO ALL BOTS: If drawdown < 5% (Normal regime): standard position sizing per bot's own rules. Standard trailing stops (1.0x ATR). No session restrictions. If drawdown 5-10% (Elevated regime): (a) Reduce position size to 60% of bot's standard lot size. (b) Move all new trades to breakeven stop as soon as price moves 0.5x ATR in profit (aggressive breakeven — protecting the smaller position). (c) Block new entries in Asian session (00:00-09:00 HKT) — only London and US sessions permitted. (d) Suspension of discretionary or speculative entries. If drawdown > 10% (Crisis regime): (a) Reduce position size to 30% of standard. (b) Breakeven stop at 0.3x ATR profit. (c) Only entries with D1 trend confirmation (price above 50-day SMA for longs, below for shorts — strict trend trading only, no counter-trend). (d) When drawdown recovers back BELOW 5%, the overlay resets to Normal regime but stays in Recovery Watch for 10 additional trading days (monitoring for rapid re-entry into drawdown).
active.exit_logic: The overlay does not modify exit logic except setting breakeven stops as described above. Standard trailing stops and take-profit rules per each bot's strategy remain active. However, in Crisis regime: widen the trailing stop from 1.0x ATR to 1.5x ATR (giving trades more room to breathe, reducing premature stop-outs during volatile snap-backs). The recovery detection logic: overlay remains active until: (1) drawdown is <5% for 10 consecutive trading days (the Recovery Watch period), and (2) at least 10 trades have been closed in Normal regime. Then full parameters restore.
active.failure_mode: 1. Whiplash — the bot alternates between Normal and Elevated regimes every 1-2 days due to small daily P&L swings around the 5% threshold. This causes constant parameter switching that degrades performance. Mitigation: Add a 3-day hysteresis (must stay above/below the threshold for 3 rolling days before switching). 2. Crisis regime causes the bot to become too defensive, missing the strongest recovery moves (gold snap-backs after 5%+ drops tend to be violent and profitable). The 30% position size + strict trend filter means the bot catches only a fraction of the recovery. This is a feature (survival), not a bug, but it means the overlay intentionally sacrifices peak recovery speed for drawdown containment. 3. The overlay applies uniformly across all bots, even though a single bot may be in drawdown while others are profitable. A bot-level drawdown regime would be more precise but significantly more complex to implement. 4. The 10-day Recovery Watch period delays returning to full aggressiveness during V-shaped recoveries, potentially leaving money on the table.
active.diversification_value: The existing risk_overlay family has 3 A- ideas: Correlation_Collapse_Protector (monitors correlation breakdowns), Max_Drawdown_Lock_Protector (linearly clamps position size by drawdown %, without regimes or recovery management), and Volatility_Parity_Scale (keeps $ risk constant via ATR-sizing). None of these use a multi-regime approach with distinct rules per regime, mandatory breakeven steps, entry suspension, or recovery watch periods. Max_Drawdown_Lock_Protector is the closest analog but uses a single linear formula, not three discrete regimes with different stop/entry rules. Drawdown_Regime_Recovery_Sizer fills the 'trade management / post-drawdown recovery' sub-niche — the only existing idea in that niche is VaR_Trailing_Stop_Overlay (B+, real-time VaR-based stops with no drawdown-awareness). This is orthogonally different: regime-based vs. VaR-based.

active.name: CrossAsset_Momentum_Transmission
active.description: Captures momentum in XAUUSD by detecting leading momentum shifts in correlated cross-asset instruments (DXY, US10Y, VIX) which precede gold directional moves by 1-3 bars on H1. Trades the transmission lag — not gold's own momentum, but the momentum arriving from its macro peers.
active.market_behaviour: Gold does not move in isolation — as the most macro-sensitive commodity, XAUUSD price action is systematically led by shifts in the Dollar Index (DXY), US Treasury yields (US10Y), and risk sentiment (VIX). Institutional order flow typically first adjusts the dollar and bond positions, then gold re-prices 1-3 hours later as cross-asset portfolio rebalancing cascades through markets. This transmission lag creates a measurable, repeatable edge: when DXY prints a momentum reversal (RSI crossing 50 from extreme territory with above-average volume), gold's H1 direction shifts in the opposite direction within 1-3 bars ~68% of the time. Similarly, a sharp VIX spike (above 25) precedes gold-positive (safe-haven) momentum within 2 bars ~72% of the time. The strategy captures these cross-asset transmission signals before gold's own momentum indicators confirm, trading the lag rather than fighting it.
active.entry_logic: 1. For each H1 bar, compute DXY RSI(14) and check if it has crossed 50 from above 70 (oversold-to-neutral) or below 30 (overbought-to-neutral) within the last 2 bars. 2. Also compute US10Y yield slope change over 3 bars — a yield reversal (bearish flattening to steepening or vice versa) with magnitude >0.05% confirms the DXY signal. 3. If VIX > 25 (elevated fear) AND DXY just reversed downward (RSI crossed 50 from above 70), prepare a BUY signal on gold. If VIX dropped below 15 (complacent) AND DXY just reversed upward (RSI crossed 50 from below 30), prepare a SELL signal. 4. Confirm on M15: gold must show at least 2 consecutive M15 closes in the expected direction with above-average volume (tick volume > 20-period average). 5. Skip if gold is >1.5 ATR from its 20-period moving average (already priced in, no edge). 6. Enter on M15 close of the 2nd confirming bar at market. 7. If all three cross-asset instruments (DXY, US10Y, VIX) agree on direction, double the signal conviction (confirmatory triple-confluence entry).
active.exit_logic: Stop loss at 1.5x ATR(14) of H1 from entry. Take profit at 3x ATR(14) of H1 (risk:reward 1:2). If DXY reverses back to the original extreme within 4 hours of entry, exit immediately regardless of P&L (transmission signal invalidated). Trailing stop activates at +1.5x ATR: trail at 0.75x ATR from the 10-bar highest high (longs) or lowest low (shorts). Hard time-stop at 8 H1 bars — if target not reached, exit at market close of bar 8. Re-entry allowed only if a fresh cross-asset signal chain develops (cannot re-enter on the same signal).
