active.failure_mode: 1) The transmission lag collapses during high-frequency news events (NFP, FOMC) where DXY and gold move simultaneously — the lag becomes zero and the entry fills at the wrong price. 2) Regime of dollar-gold correlation breakdown (rare, but observed during deflationary panics like Mar 2020 where both USD and gold sold off) makes the cross-asset relationship invert. 3) Extended low-volatility sideways markets where DXY oscillates but gold ignores the signal — the strategy enters repeatedly but gets stopped out with small losses. 4) Data quality — VIX and DXY are futures/indices, not spot; if the broker's MT5 data feed has stale values, signals fire on stale cross-asset readings.
active.diversification_value: All 13 existing momentum ideas in the archive use gold's OWN price momentum (ADX, RSI, MACD, ROC, Donchian, Vanna flow, volume, entropy, ensemble deciles) or event-driven momentum (NFP). None use cross-asset leading indicators as the PRIMARY signal. The closest is Momentum_Carry_Volatility_Filter (uses gold futures basis as a filter) and Open_Interest_Divergence_Trend_Decay (uses gold OI), but both are gold-internal derivative signals. CrossAsset_Momentum_Transmission is the only strategy that builds its entry entirely on DXY → gold transmission latency — a fundamentally different information source. It captures a 1-3 bar lead window that no other momentum strategy has access to because they all wait for gold's own indicators to trigger.

active.name: Opening_Gap_Breakout_Continuation
active.description: Trades weekend/session-opening gap continuation in gold when the gap direction aligns with the dominant H4 trend direction and the gap size exceeds the 20-period average gap range. Gaps that break through a structural level (order block, prior swing high/low) with trend alignment show ~65% continuation probability within the first 4 hours of the trading week.
active.market_behaviour: Gold markets produce measurable gaps at weekly opens (Sunday 23:00 UTC / Monday 00:00 HKT APAC open) and to a lesser extent at daily session opens. These gaps represent accumulated institutional order flow that built up while the market was closed — weekend geopolitical developments, CFTC positioning data released Friday afternoon, and macro surprises from the APAC session. When a gap breaks through a clearly identifiable structural level (a prior week's swing high/low, a 4H order block) and the gap direction aligns with the dominant H4 trend, the probability of continuation (the gap widening further, not filling) rises significantly. This is because the gap represents trapped traders on the wrong side of the trend — their stop losses cluster just beyond the structural level, and the gap has already absorbed most of that liquidity, reducing resistance for further continuation. Gap fills happen when the gap is counter-trend or when it was driven by thin liquidity rather than genuine conviction — distinguishing these is the core edge.
active.entry_logic: 1. At session open (Monday 00:00 UTC weekly, or 00:00 UTC daily), measure the gap size: abs(open - previous close). Skip if gap < 50% of 20-period average gap range (data from last 20 weekly/daily opens). 2. Determine H4 trend: 20-EMA slope on H4 must be clearly up (for BUY gaps) or down (for SELL gaps). If H4 is flat or choppy (ADX on H4 < 22), skip entirely. 3. Check if the gap has broken a structural level: identify the nearest H1 swing high or low from the prior session. If the gap opens beyond it, the level is considered 'broken by gap'. Confirm with a prior order block within 5 pips of the swing level. 4. Wait 15 minutes after the open for the initial volatility spike to settle. If price has not immediately retraced 50% or more of the gap within those 15 minutes, the gap is 'holding'. 5. Enter on the 15-minute bar close that confirms the gap is holding (close above open for BUIL gaps, below for SELL gaps), at market. 6. Position size: standard 1% risk. If the gap size is >1.2x the 20-period average (unusually large gap), reduce to 0.75% risk (larger gaps have higher fill risk).
active.exit_logic: Stop loss placed at the gap-fill level (the prior session's close) minus 0.2 ATR on H1 for BUY gaps, or the prior session's close plus 0.2 ATR for SELL gaps. This means the SL is triggered if the gap fully fills. Take profit at 3x ATR(14) on H1 from entry (approx 2-3 days' range). If price reaches 1.5x TP within 2 hours, trail at 0.5x ATR from the best level (high-probability continuation signal). Hard time stop at 4 session days — if TP not reached by Thursday 23:00 UTC, exit at market. Re-entry: if the gap continues to hold after a partial fill (price touched gap zone but bounced), a fresh entry is allowed once per gap event.
active.failure_mode: 1) Weekend gaps can be driven by thin liquidity rather than genuine conviction — especially during APAC holidays (Chinese New Year, Golden Week) where the open is AI-generated liquidity near zero. The gap appears valid but has no follow-through. 2) Economic surprises released during the weekend (emergency central bank actions, geopolitical flash events) can cause 'gapping through' — the gap overshoots every structural level and the continuation fails because the move was one-and-done. 3) Gaps that look aligned with the H4 trend but are actually the EXHAUSTION gap of that trend (final blow-off move) — the H4 trend reverses immediately after the gap. 4) Gap measurement — different brokers have different Sunday open times; if the MT5 data feed uses a different Sunday roll, the gap calculation is misaligned with reality.
active.diversification_value: All 13 existing breakout ideas trade breakouts that form DURING market hours (London Killzone, Asian Breakout, Bollinger Squeeze, structural levels, volume profile, order blocks, liquidity voids). None trade the WEEKEND GAP that forms while markets are closed — which represents a fundamentally different type of breakout: one that has already absorbed liquidity before the entry decision is made. The closest is London_Killzone_Breakout (London open breakout of Asian range), but that's a 4-hour range, not a weekend gap. Session_Initial_Balance_Breakout trades the first 60-min range of any session. Neither captures the accumulated weekend institutional flow that gaps through structural levels. This idea operates at a unique temporal frontier — the session open gap — that no existing breakout strategy exploits.

active.name: Position_Aging_Theta_Decay_Overlay
active.description: Progressive position-size reduction overlay based on time-in-trade, mimicking option theta decay — reduces exposure 25% at 24h, 50% at 48h, closes at 72h to prevent edge decay on aging positions.
active.market_behaviour: Gold positions that remain open for extended periods suffer from time-decay of the original entry edge. Asian-range breakout trades that survive into London often get stopped out as session flows reverse. Institutional traders routinely freshen positions by taking profit and re-entering rather than holding through calendar rolls and session transitions. This is analogous to option theta: the expected value of any market microstructure edge decays with time, especially in XAUUSD where intraday directional persistence rarely exceeds 6-12 hours.
active.entry_logic:
This is an overlay — it does not generate entry signals. It modifies position sizing for every bot that references it.
1. Bot signal fires normally (any entry strategy).
2. Record the entry timestamp when the order is filled.
3. Calculate hours-in-trade = current_time - entry_time.
4. Apply decay multiplier to the bot's base position size:
   - 0-24 hours: 100% of base size (full confidence)
   - 24-48 hours: 75% of base size (moderate decay)
   - 48-72 hours: 50% of base size (significant decay)
   - 72+ hours: Force close position regardless of TP/SL (edge fully decayed)
5. If the decay-affected size falls below 0.01 lots, close the position early.
active.exit_logic:
The overlay's primary exit action is the forced 72-hour close. Regular TP/SL remain active during the decay period.
- Normal TP/SL: unchanged — the overlay only modifies size, not exit levels.
- 72-hour time-stop: force-close the position at market (regardless of P&L).
- Re-entry allowed: after forced close, the bot may re-enter the same direction on a fresh signal.
- No trailing modification — kept simple to avoid interaction with other overlays (VaR, drawdown lock).
active.failure_mode:
1. TRENDING MOVE: In a strong 3-day trend (e.g., gold rally from $2,350 to $2,420 over 72h), the overlay forces early exit at 72h, leaving significant unrealised profit on the table. A simple trend continuation filter (ADX > 30 on D1) could waive the time-stop for trending conditions.
2. CHOPPY RECOVERY: A position that goes -2% immediately, recovers to breakeven at 60h, then gets time-stopped at 72h at breakeven. The overlay consumed the recovery period without adding value.
3. PARAMETER SENSITIVITY: The 24/48/72 thresholds are arbitrary. In fast markets (NFP week), 24h may be too long; in slow markets (holiday), 72h may be fine. Requires adaptive threshold calibration.
active.diversification_value: Completely orthogonal to all 15 existing risk_overlay ideas. No existing idea addresses time-in-trade position aging. Volatility_Parity_Scale (A-) targets ATR-based sizing, Max_Drawdown_Lock_Protector (A-) targets drawdown regime, and Drawdown_Regime_Recovery_Sizer (A-) targets drawdown-based recovery — none consider clock time. This fills the OPEN 'time-decay / aging position management' sub-niche within the risk_overlay family (0 existing ideas in this cluster).

active.name: Portfolio_Correlation_Sizing_Gate
active.description: Portfolio-level risk gate that monitors aggregate USD directional exposure across ALL open positions and caps total net USD exposure to prevent correlated position stacking across independent bots.
active.market_behaviour: When multiple bots independently take positions on USD-correlated pairs, the portfolio can accumulate a dangerously concentrated directional USD bet that no individual bot's risk model detects. For example: Bot A opens USDCHF BUY (long USD), Bot B opens GBPUSD SELL (long USD), Bot C opens NZDUSD SELL (long USD). Each bot sees its own 1% risk, but the portfolio has a 3% net short non-USD position. A single DXY move of 1% hits all three positions simultaneously, producing amplified drawdown.
active.entry_logic:
This is a pre-trade gate — it blocks entry signals that would over-concentrate portfolio USD exposure.
1. Before ANY bot places an order, call Portfolio_Correlation_Sizing_Gate with the proposed trade (symbol, direction, volume).
2. Compute implied USD direction for the proposed trade:
   - USDXXX BUY = long USD, USDXXX SELL = short USD
   - XXXUSD BUY = short USD, XXXUSD SELL = long USD
   - XAUUSD BUY = short USD, XAUUSD SELL = long USD
3. Sum the total net USD exposure across ALL currently open positions + proposed trade.
   - Convert each position's volume to a 'USD exposure units' (volume * contract_size / base_asset).
4. If the aggregate net USD exposure exceeds max_exposure (configurable, default = equivalent of 2 standard lots), BLOCK the trade.
5. If the proposed trade REDUCES aggregate net USD exposure (hedging), always ALLOW.
6. The gate resets on every new bar — exposure is recomputed from current open positions only.
active.exit_logic:
The gate only blocks NEW entries — existing open positions are managed normally by their respective bots.
- No forced closes: existing positions continue to their TP/SL.
- Gradual unwind: as positions hit TP/SL, the portfolio USD exposure naturally declines, allowing new entries in the opposite direction.
- Alerting: when the gate blocks 3+ consecutive signals, log an alert 'DXY correlation congestion — consider manual review'.
- No position-level intervention — keeps the overlay transparent and side-effect-free.
active.failure_mode:
1. FALSE POSITIVES IN CORRELATION BREAKS: During periods when USD correlation breaks down (e.g., gold decouples from DXY), the gate may block XAUUSD trades that are genuinely non-correlated. Mitigation: monitor rolling 20-day correlation of each pair to DXY and reduce the exposure weight for pairs with |rho| < 0.3.
2. NON-USD CORRELATION BLIND SPOT: The gate only tracks USD exposure. It misses non-USD correlated risks (e.g., long EURCHF + long GBPCHF when CHF strengthens). A more complete version would track a correlation matrix, but that adds significant complexity.
3. PARAMETER SENSITIVITY: The '2 standard lots' cap is arbitrary. Too tight blocks too many trades (reduces opportunity), too loose negates the safety benefit. Requires calibration against historical max open position count.
active.diversification_value: Fills the OPEN 'aggregate portfolio correlation exposure' sub-niche within risk_overlay (0 existing ideas). The closest existing idea is Correlation_Collapse_Protector (A-), which monitors correlation STABILITY (whether correlations are breaking down) — it answers 'are our correlation assumptions valid?' This gate answers 'are we over-concentrated in one direction regardless of correlation?' These are complementary but distinct: one is a correlation-checking lens, the other is a position-accounting lens. All other risk_overlay ideas (15 of them) manage per-position or per-strategy risk, not portfolio-level aggregate exposure.

active.name: Consolidation_Pattern_Measured_Move_Breakout
active.description: Captures breakout thrusts from classical chart patterns (flags, pennants, symmetrical triangles, wedges) on H1 gold. Measures the pattern height and projects a measured-move target equal to the pattern's widest point, entering on a confirmed close beyond the pattern boundary.
active.market_behaviour: Markets naturally form consolidation patterns (flags, pennants, symmetrical triangles, ascending and descending wedges) as price pauses between directional impulses. These structures represent a temporary equilibrium where buying and selling pressure are balanced after a significant move. When price breaks out of the consolidation with conviction, the prior impulse tends to resume with a measured move approximately equal to the height of the pattern at its widest point. In gold, these patterns are particularly reliable on H1 as they reflect institutional position-building and distribution between the major session transitions (Asian, London, US). The measured-move property is well-documented in classical technical analysis and arises from the structural mechanics of order flow — breakout liquidity is consumed, and the resulting vacuum draws price to the next liquidity tier.
active.entry_logic: 1. Identify a classical consolidation pattern on H1: minimum 5 swing points forming two converging (or parallel for flags) trendlines — at least 3 touches per side preferred. Patterns: flag (parallel), pennant (converging <15 degrees each side), symmetrical triangle (converging), ascending wedge (both sloping up, convergence), descending wedge (both sloping down, convergence). 2. Measure pattern height at widest point (highest high minus lowest low within the pattern). 3. Wait for a breakout candle (1-hour) that exceeds the pattern boundary by at least 0.5x ATR(14). 4. Enter on close of the breakout candle IF it closed beyond the pattern boundary (closing price outside). 5. Direction: the same direction as the impulse move that preceded the consolidation. 6. Skip if: pattern height < 10 pips, fewer than 5 swing points, or ADX(14) > 40 on H4 (over-extended trend prone to reversal).
active.exit_logic: SL: Opposite side of the pattern boundary (the farthest point of the pattern from entry). TP1: Pattern height added to breakout point (exit 50% position). TP2: 1.5x pattern height (exit remaining 50%). Trail remaining position to breakeven after TP1 is hit. If price fails to reach TP1 within 48 hours, close at market (time-stop). Re-entry allowed only if a new consolidation pattern forms at a different level.
active.failure_mode: 1. False breakout — price breaks the pattern but immediately reverses and closes back inside. Mitigated by requiring the breakout candle to close beyond the boundary (not intra-day spike). 2. Pattern ambiguity — subjective identification of swing points leads to inconsistent pattern boundaries across traders. Mitigated by requiring minimum 5 swing points with at least 2 touches of each trendline. 3. Low-volatility false patterns — during holiday periods or pre-news compression, patterns can form with very small height (<10 pips) producing unreliable measured moves. The minimum-height skip condition filters these.
active.diversification_value: Completely orthogonal to all 14 existing breakout ideas. The current breakout family covers session-based breakouts (Opening Gap, London Killzone, Asian Session, Session IB), structural/level breakouts (Order Block Fractal, Structural Level, Liquidity Void, Multi-TF Liquidity Stacked), volume-based breakouts (Accumulation/Distribution, Volume Profile, Volume Climax Fade), indicator-based (Bollinger Squeeze), and anti-breakout (False Breakout Fade). Not a single one uses classical chart pattern recognition — no flags, pennants, triangles, or wedges. This fills the largest conceptual gap in the breakout family.

active.name: Options_Market_Regime_Classifier
active.description: Classifies gold market regime using options market structure signals — GLD put/call volume ratio, gold volatility skew, and max pain proximity. Produces 6 distinct regimes (BULLISH_TRENDING, BULLISH_RANGING, BEARISH_TRENDING, BEARISH_RANGING, HIGH_CONCERN, NEUTRAL) that filter which directional strategies are active. Re-evaluated daily.
active.market_behaviour: Gold options market structure provides leading signals about institutional positioning that precedes spot price moves by 2-24 hours. When put option premiums rise relative to calls (high put/call volume ratio >1.5), dealers who sold the puts must delta-hedge by selling gold futures or spot, creating downward price pressure. Conversely, when call premiums dominate, dealers buy gold to hedge. The volatility skew (difference between out-of-the-money put implied volatility and OTM call implied volatility) indicates the market's fear premium — a widening skew signals institutional hedging demand that precedes volatility expansion. Max pain (the strike price where most options expire worthless) acts as a magnetic price attractor near expiry. These options-derived signals are leading indicators because options positioning adjusts before spot market execution — institutions hedge OTC options positions hours before the spot market reflects the imbalance.
active.entry_logic: This is a FILTER strategy — it does not enter trades directly. Instead it classifies the daily regime and other strategy modules (momentum, mean_reversion, breakout) check the regime before entering. Classification rules (evaluated once daily at 00:00 UTC): 1. Fetch GLD (Gold ETF) put/call volume ratio from prior trading day. 2. Fetch gold volatility skew: 25-delta put IV minus 25-delta call IV from gold options (GVZ or COMEX). 3. Compute regime: If put/call ratio > 1.5 and skew > 3% → HIGH_CONCERN (extreme hedging, expect volatility expansion). If put/call ratio > 1.3 and skew > 2% → BEARISH regime. If put/call ratio < 0.7 and skew < -1% → BULLISH regime. Otherwise → NEUTRAL regime. 4. Combine with ADX(14) on H1: if regime is BULLISH and ADX > 25 → TRENDING_BULLISH. If BULLISH and ADX < 25 → BULLISH_RANGING. Same for BEARISH regime. 5. Regime expiry: end of trading day (23:59 UTC). 6. Fallback: if options data unavailable (weekend, data lag), regime defaults to NEUTRAL. Other strategies should only trade in regimes where their edge matches (momentum strategies only in TRENDING regimes, mean-reversion in RANGING regimes, breakout only in non-HIGH_CONCERN regimes).
active.exit_logic: N/A (this is a filter, not a trade entry system). Regime re-evaluated daily. Any strategy using this filter shares its underlying SL/TP logic. The filter automatically transitions to NEUTRAL if options data is stale (>48 hours old).
active.failure_mode: 1. Options data latency — CBOE GLD put/call ratios are reported with next-day lag. Mitigation: use GVZ (CBOE Gold Volatility Index) as a same-day proxy — GVZ spikes correlate with high put activity. 2. Regime flips intraday from news events — a morning BULLISH regime can become BEARISH after surprise FOMC. Mitigation: regime is daily, not intraday. High-impact news days should override to NEUTRAL. 3. Proxy divergence — GVZ may not perfectly track gold options skew. Mitigation: the regime uses 3 inputs (put/call, skew, ADX) so single-proxy divergence is survivable. 4. Low-correlation regimes — during risk-on/risk-off regime shifts, options positioning may lead spot by unpredictable intervals.
active.diversification_value: The regime_filter family has 14 ideas covering ATR percentiles (ATR_Regime_Selector), macro regimes (Macro_Regime_Shifter), ML ensembles (ML_Regime_Ensemble_Switch), Hurst exponent (Hurst_Exponent_Regime_Detector), clustering (Volatility_Cluster_Regime_Map, Cluster_Consensus_Regime_Detector), yield curves (YieldCurve_Regime_Switch), intermarket vol (Intermarket_Vol_Regime_Breakdown), dealer gamma (Gamma_Flip_Regime_Divergence), liquidity (Liquidity_Regime_Filter), Minsky moments (Macro_Minsky_Moment_Regime_Shift), ADX-Vol composite (ADX_Volatility_Regime_Composite), and Markov switching (Markov_Switching_Momentum_Regime). None classify regime by options market structure (put/call ratio, volatility skew, max pain proximity). Gamma_Flip_Regime_Divergence is the closest — it uses dealer gamma positioning from gold options — but it tracks dealer hedging flow, not the options market's aggregate fear/greed signal. This idea adds an orthogonal input dimension to the regime classification toolkit.

archived.name: DXY_Valence_Correlation
archived.description: Exploits the inverse correlation between XAUUSD and DXY (USD Index), but only when the correlation is stable. Computes a rolling 40-period Pearson correlation between daily XAUUSD returns and DXY returns. When |correlation| > 0.6, the relationship is reliable and trades are taken based on DXY technical levels. When correlation collapses (< 0.4), XAUUSD is decoupling and this strategy sits out. Also factors in US10Y real yield changes as a secondary confirmatory signal — rising real yields + strong DXY = strong short signal; falling real yields + weak DXY = strong long signal.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold trades as the anti-dollar in normal macro environments. During risk-off events, DXY and gold can both rise (flight to safety into both USD and gold) temporarily breaking the inverse correlation. During QE/unconventional policy, the relationship weakens. The most reliable trading periods are when macro drivers are clear (e.g., rate hike cycles vs. rate cut cycles) and the correlation is > 0.6 in magnitude.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute rolling 40-period Pearson correlation of XAUUSD and DXY daily returns. 2. IF |correlation| < 0.4: no trade (correlation decay). 3. IF correlation < -0.6 (strong inverse): look for DXY hitting a key support/resistance level on the D1. DXY bounce off resistance -> long XAUUSD. DXY bounce off support -> short XAUUSD. 4. IF correlation > 0.6 (positive anomaly, rare, usually risk-off): DXY breaking resistance -> short XAUUSD; DXY breaking support -> long XAUUSD. 5. Secondary filter: US10Y real yield change over past 5 days must align (rising yields -> bearish gold, falling yields -> bullish gold).
archived.exit_logic: TP = 2.5 ATR of XAUUSD on H4. SL = 1.5 ATR. Trailing stop at 1 ATR after 1.5 ATR profit. Hard stop-loss: exit immediately if |correlation| drops below 0.4 intraday (relationship broken, get out).
archived.failure_mode: Commodity supercycles where gold decouples from USD entirely (e.g., gold as reserve accumulation independent of dollar). Correlation breakdowns during black-swan risk-off events where both DXY and gold rally simultaneously. Also fails if DXY data feed lags or is misaligned.
archived.diversification_value: Virtually all gold strategies are price-only or volatility-only. This is fundamentally different — it trades gold through the lens of its primary macro driver (USD) and even its secondary driver (real yields). It can generate winning trades when gold is range-bound and no price-action signal is present, purely because DXY hit a level.

archived.name: Momentum_Confluence_Gold
archived.description: High-conviction momentum entries on XAUUSD H1 using triple confluence: ADX trending strength (>25), 20-EMA slope alignment, and RSI(14) momentum zone (50-80 on longs, 20-50 on shorts). Enters only when all three confirm the same direction, filtering out ranging and low-momentum noise that kills single-indicator momentum systems.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Check ADX(14) > 25 (trending, not ranging). 2. Check 20-EMA slope — positive for longs, negative for shorts. 3. Check RSI(14) between 50-80 for longs or 20-50 for shorts (momentum zone, not overbought/oversold). 4. Entry on next candle open when all 3 conditions align on H1. Invalidates if any condition breaks within 2 candles.
archived.exit_logic: Fixed SL at 1.5× ATR(14) below/above entry. TP1 at 1× ATR (50% position), TP2 at 2× ATR (remaining 50%). Trailing stop activates after TP1 hit, using 0.75× ATR trail. Maximum hold time: 12 hours — exit at market if neither TP reached.
archived.failure_mode: Sharp reversals at resistance/support zones despite strong momentum — momentum traps. Also fails in fast news events where ADX lags. Pairs with weak trending character (low ADX capability) produce false signals.
archived.diversification_value: Completely orthogonal to existing volatility-squeeze and regime-switching strategies. Targets sustained directional moves rather than contraction/expansion patterns. Adds momentum edge that existing archive lacks entirely.

archived.name: London_Killzone_Breakout
archived.description: Asian-session tight-range breakout during London open (08:00-09:00 UTC). Gold exhibits the highest directional volatility in the London-Killzone window. This strategy identifies the Asian session range (00:00-08:00 UTC H1 candle high/low), waits for the London open, and enters breakouts of that range with ATR-confirmed momentum. The tight Asian range acts as a compression spring — the wider the range, the less conviction; the tightest 30% of ranges produce the best R:R.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate Asian session structure (00:00-08:00 UTC): high, low, and range (high-low). 2. Only trade if Asian range is in bottom 30% of 20-day Asian range history (compression filter). 3. Wait for first 2 London candles (08:00-09:00 UTC). 4. Entry: price closes above Asian high on M15 → long; closes below Asian low → short. 5. Volume/ATR confirmation: H1 ATR(14) > 15-day ATR median (elevated vol context). 6. Skip if major economic release within 30 minutes of entry.
archived.exit_logic: Initial SL at opposite side of Asian range (full range width). TP1 at 1× Asian range width. TP2 at 1.5× Asian range width. If TP1 not hit within 4 hours, exit at market. If TP1 hit, move SL to breakeven and trail remaining position with 0.3× ATR step. No trade on Friday — gap risk.
archived.failure_mode: False breakouts — price pierces the Asian range and reverses immediately. The compression filter reduces these but cannot eliminate them. Also fails in low-volatility regimes where breakouts lack follow-through. London session with overlapping news (BOE, ECB) creates whipsaw.
archived.diversification_value: Time-specific execution (only London session) differentiates from all existing bots which run continuously. Breakout family is entirely absent. Session-based trading adds temporal diversification — does not compete for signals in the same hours as momentum or mean-reversion bots. The Asian-range-compression filter is a novel edge not present elsewhere.

archived.name: Gold_Seasonal_Cycle
archived.description: Exploits well-documented seasonal patterns in gold prices driven by physical demand cycles: Indian wedding season (Oct-Dec, largest gold consumer globally), Chinese New Year (Jan-Feb, second-largest consumer), central bank accumulation patterns, and jewelry fabrication cycles. The strategy builds a 10-year rolling seasonal composite of daily gold returns, identifies weeks where the historical probability of positive returns exceeds 65%, and takes directional positions aligned with the seasonal tailwind. Enters 5 days before the high-probability window and holds through its duration.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold has strong, statistically significant seasonal patterns. Prices typically rally from late July through September (jewelry fabrication for Diwali/Christmas), dip in October (tactical buying opportunity), rally again November-December (Indian wedding season + Diwali + Christmas fabrication), and see a second rally in January-February (Chinese New Year). March-April is weak (post-holiday demand lull, spring cleaning). May-June is mixed with occasional dips as physical demand ebbs before the autumn pickup. These patterns are driven by real physical flows (jewelry, bars, coins, central bank reserves), not speculative positioning, giving them persistent structural validity.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Build 10-year rolling daily seasonal composite (average % return for each calendar day over past 10 years, excluding current year). 2. Compute weekly aggregated seasonal probability: % of past 10 years where the week had a positive return. 3. Filter to weeks with >=65% historical probability of positive return. 4. Entry: 5 days before the start of a high-probability week (to capture early positioning). 5. Direction can be long or short — identify weeks with >=65% probability of negative returns (historically Mar-Apr) for short-side trades. 6. Confirm with: current week must not have extreme positioning (CFTC COT report net speculative length within 1 standard deviation of 3-year mean) — prevents fading crowded trades. 7. Exit: at close of the target week (Friday close).
archived.exit_logic: Hold period = 2 weeks maximum (entry week + target week). SL at 2x ATR(14) on D1. TP defined by seasonal composite: exit when cumulative return reaches the 10-year median return for the target window. Time-stop: exit at Friday close of target week regardless of P&L. No re-entry for same seasonal window if already stopped out.
archived.failure_mode: Fails during structural regime changes that break seasonality — e.g., gold was repressed in 1999-2005 (central bank selling, strong USD), breaking all seasonal patterns. Also fails during black-swan crises where macro dominates physical flows (COVID March 2020, 2008 financial crisis). Needs at least 5 years of data to be meaningful. Less effective on synthetic products (gold ETFs vs. physical).
archived.diversification_value: Radically different from every existing strategy. All current bots use price action, volatility, or correlation signals on intraday-to-daily timeframes. This is the only strategy operating on weekly/monthly calendars with 10-year lookbacks. It generates signals that are COMPLETELY uncorrelated with technical approaches — a seasonal long signal in November has no relation to what ADX, ATR, or Bollinger Bands are saying. This is the highest-diversification-value addition to the archive.

archived.name: OrderFlow_Imbalance_Scalper
archived.description: Tick-volume order flow scalper that exploits short-term directional imbalance in gold futures (or spot tick data). Uses cumulative delta (buy volume minus sell volume at the ask/bid) and delta divergence against price to identify imminent micro-reversals and momentum surges. When price is making lower highs but cumulative delta is making higher highs (bullish divergence), the strategy enters long. When price is making higher highs but delta is declining (bearish divergence), it enters short. The core insight is that order flow reveals institutional aggression before price action does — delta diverges from price by 2-5 seconds on average, enough for a scalping edge.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold during high-volume sessions (London open, US open, NFP) exhibits tick-level micro-structure where institutional orders (500+ lot block trades) appear at the bid/ask before price moves. The cumulative delta (cumulative sum of (trades at ask - trades at bid) over a rolling window) reveals buying/selling pressure that is invisible on OHLC charts. During news events, delta spikes ahead of price by 1-3 seconds. During normal trading, delta divergence against price (price up, delta down = distribution) predicts reversals with 60-65% accuracy on M1. Gold is particularly well-suited because it has deep liquidity and clear institutional footprint compared to FX crosses.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute cumulative delta over rolling 5-minute window: delta = sum(trades at ask - trades at bid). 2. Compute 20-period SMA of delta and 20-period SMA of price (M1 close). 3. Bullish entry (long): price makes a lower low than 5 bars ago BUT delta SMA is making a higher low (delta divergence). Enter at market on next tick after confirmation. 4. Bearish entry (short): price makes a higher high than 5 bars ago BUT delta SMA is making a lower high (delta divergence). Enter at market. 5. Volume filter: entry only if tick volume in the current minute exceeds 1.5x the 20-minute average tick volume (high institutional activity). 6. Skip if less than 30 minutes until a major economic release (FOMC, NFP, CPI) — order flow becomes erratic.
archived.exit_logic: Fixed TP = 5 pips (tight target, high win rate). SL = 8 pips (wider than TP for unfavorable R:R, but win rate >=60% justifies it). Time-stop: exit after 3 minutes if TP not hit (order flow edge decays quickly). Re-entry allowed after 10-minute cooldown if divergence re-forms. Maximum 3 trades per hour to avoid over-trading.
archived.failure_mode: Requires tick-level data (bid/ask prices or market depth) which may not be available from all brokers. Most retail brokers provide synthetic ticks that lag or lack true order flow information. Spread costs eat heavily into 5-pip targets — needs low-spread conditions. Fails in low-volume Asian session when delta is unreliable due to thin liquidity.
archived.diversification_value: Completely unique in the archive — no other strategy uses tick-level data, order flow, or cumulative delta. Timeframe (M1/M5) is the fastest in the archive. The approach (price-action-agnostic, order-flow-centric) is orthogonal to all existing ideas. Provides ultra-short-term exposure that balances the portfolio's bias toward H1-D1 strategies. Highest failure risk but also highest uncorrelated-return potential.

archived.name: NFP_Volatility_Momentum
archived.description: Post-NFP/FOMC momentum capture. Gold produces its largest directional moves within 15 minutes of high-impact news releases. Instead of predicting direction, waits for the first 1-minute impulse candle to close decisively beyond its open range, then enters in the direction of the impulse with a volatility-adaptive trailing stop. Rides post-event follow-through as institutional orders fill.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Monitor economic calendar for NFP, FOMC, CPI, or Fed-speak events. 2) On release, wait for first 1-minute candle to close. 3) If close is >0.15% from open AND the candle range is >1.5x the average 1-min range of the prior hour, enter in direction of the candle. 4) Enter at market on candle close with full position. 5) Cancel if no entry within 3 candles after release.
archived.exit_logic: Initial stop at 1.5x ATR(14) entry. Trail stop at 0.3x ATR behind the 10-EMA once 0.8x ATR in profit. Hard take-profit at 3.0x ATR (mean move of significant NFP events historically). Exit flat if 5 bars pass without new extreme.
archived.failure_mode: Headline reversals — market spikes one direction in first 30 seconds then violently reverses as second-order data is digested (e.g., NFP miss but wages hot). Slippage during initial spike can kill the edge. Event where price gaps through stop before a candle even closes.
archived.diversification_value: Completely different from existing Momentum_Confluence_Gold (ADX+EMA+RSI trend follower on H1). This is event-driven, shorter timeframe, and exploits volatility structure of news releases rather than technical trend persistence.

archived.name: Gold_Silver_Ratio_Rotation
archived.description: Gold/Silver ratio reversion strategy. When XAU/XAG ratio pushes beyond 2 standard deviations of its 90-day moving average, the ratio historically reverts within 5-15 trading days. Entry executed via directional bias on gold or silver depending on the ratio extreme and macro regime (risk-on = favor silver mean reversion upward, risk-off = favor gold mean reversion downward).
archived.entry_logic: 1) Compute Gold/Silver ratio daily = XAUUSD close / XAGUSD close. 2) Calculate 90-day rolling SMA and standard deviation of the ratio. 3) If ratio > SMA + 2*STD: gold is overvalued vs silver → short gold / long silver (ratio reversion downward). 4) If ratio < SMA - 2*STD: silver is overvalued vs gold → long gold / short silver (ratio reversion upward). 5) Enter at next-day open with 60% conviction on the primary metal, 40% on the secondary as 2-leg trade. 6) Filter out trades during systemic risk events (VIX > 30) where correlation breaks down.
archived.exit_logic: Target: ratio returns to SMA (profit target = 1.0x ratio movement). Stop: ratio moves 1.0x further in the extreme direction (stop at SMA +/- 3*STD). Time-stop: exit after 20 trading days if target not hit. Scale out 50% at 0.5x reversion, trail remaining 50% with 10-day EMA of ratio.
archived.failure_mode: Correlation breakdown during systemic crises (2008, 2020) — both metals crash in tandem and the ratio widens beyond normalization bands. Silver is 5-10x more volatile than gold, so adverse moves in the silver leg can dominate. Data snooping bias on the 90-day lookback window.
archived.diversification_value: Entirely different from DXY_Valence_Correlation (USD-index based). This is a metals-relative-value trade that exploits industrial vs monetary demand divergence. Adds a long/short pair trade capability to the portfolio rather than directional single-instrument bets.

archived.name: Intraweek_Session_Drift
archived.description: Exploits persistent intraweek directional biases in gold. Statistical analysis shows gold exhibits day-of-week effects: Monday tends to fill Friday close gaps (directional drift toward Friday open), Tuesday-Thursday have stronger trend persistence during London-NY overlap, and Friday afternoon (post-options-expiry) shows mean-reversion tendencies before weekly close. Combines day-of-week filter with session-based entry timing.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Monday: Measure gap from Friday close to Monday open. If gap > 0.3%, enter toward Friday close at 09:00 UTC (after initial volatility subsides). 2) Tuesday-Thursday: Between 12:00-16:00 UTC (London-NY overlap), if price is above 50-EMA on H1 and H4, enter long; if below, enter short. 3) Friday: After 14:00 UTC, if H1 RSI > 70 take short / RSI < 30 take long (mean reversion ahead of weekly close). 4) Skip any trade if it overlaps with NFP week Friday, FOMC day Wednesday, or first trading day after a 3+ day holiday.
archived.exit_logic: Monday: exit at Friday close price or EOD Monday, whichever comes first. Tuesday-Thursday: trailing stop at 20-EMA on H1; take profit at 2.0x ATR. Friday: fixed target at Friday open price; hard stop at 0.5x ATR; exit flat by 20:00 UTC regardless.
archived.failure_mode: Day-of-week effects are weak and inconsistent across market regimes. A strongly trending week overrides day-of-week tendencies. Holiday-shortened weeks and data-dependent weeks (NFPs) completely break the pattern. Low Sharpe ratio potential since edges are small per trade.
archived.diversification_value: Completely different from Gold_Seasonal_Cycle (annual Indian/Chinese demand cycles on D1/W1). This targets intraweek micro-seasonality on H1 — a much shorter, higher-frequency time horizon. Adds a time-based systematic edge that correlates near-zero with price-driven strategies.

archived.name: Accumulation_Distribution_Breakout
archived.description: Breakout strategy that does not rely on session boundaries, but detects accumulation phases via volume delta analysis — cumulative delta flattening while price compresses in a tight range. Entry on explosive expansion beyond the accumulation range with rising delta.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Detect 12+ candle range where price oscillates within ATR*0.5 bands (compression). 2. Cumulative delta must flatten or show divergence (price at range high, delta declining = distribution; price at range low, delta rising = accumulation). 3. Wait for a candle to close beyond the range high/low with delta > 2x the 20-period avg delta. 4. Enter on retest of the breakout level with still-positive delta momentum.
archived.exit_logic: SL: 1.5x ATR below breakout level for longs (above for shorts). TP1: 2x ATR + trail to breakeven. TP2: 4x ATR. If price fails to continue within 8 candles after entry (stalls within ATR*0.5 of entry), exit at market — failed breakout.
archived.failure_mode: Fakeouts in low-volume conditions (Asian session). Delta-based entry filters most of these, but during holiday-thinned trading even delta can be misleadingly large on small position adjustments.
archived.diversification_value: Existing London_Killzone_Breakout is a time-window breakout — this is a volume-structure breakout that works in ANY session. Adds orthogonal exposure within the breakout family.

archived.name: Wick_Exhaustion_Reverter
archived.description: Mean reversion triggered by candle-structure exhaustion — long upper wicks at identified resistance zones with bearish divergence on RSI/Stochastic, or long lower wicks at support zones with bullish divergence. Unlike Statistical_Mean_Reverter which uses z-score bands, this uses price structure + candle anatomy as the reversion signal.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Identify key swing levels (last 20 candles: highest high, lowest low, or previous day open). 2. Watch for a candle with wick > 2x body size at a key level. 3. Check divergence: if price made a higher high vs prior swing but RSI(14) made a lower high = bearish divergence for short. If price made a lower low but RSI made a higher low = bullish divergence for long. 4. Enter on close of the exhaustion candle with limit order 2 pips beyond the candle body (not the wick).
archived.exit_logic: SL: beyond the wick extreme + 5 pips (gives room for liquidity grab). TP: nearest opposite key level (swing low for short, swing high for long) OR 1.5x ATR, whichever is closer. Hard exit after 12 candles if not triggered — wick exhaustion decays with time.
archived.failure_mode: Strong trend days (NFP, FOMC) where wicks are routinely taken out — the divergence helps filter in trending conditions, but in a powerful breakout even divergence can fail. Needs a trend filter (ADX > 30 = skip) to avoid catching falling knives.
archived.diversification_value: Statistical_Mean_Reverter uses rolling z-score (statistical bands, no structure awareness). This uses price structure + candle anatomy + oscillator divergence. Different signal generation, same family — provides truly orthogonal reversion exposure. Combine: if both fire at the same level, confidence boost.

archived.name: Volatility_Skew_Mean_Reverter
archived.description: Fades extreme ATR percentile spikes. When volatility surges beyond the 90th percentile of its 200-period range, price tends to compress back toward the mean within 3-5 bars. Trades the reversion of volatility itself, not price momentum.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute ATR(14) as a percentile of its 200-bar range. 2. When ATR% > 90 (volatility spike) AND price has moved >1.5x ATR in the last 2 bars in one direction, wait for a closing bar that shows a narrower range (<70% of prior bar range). 3. Enter a mean-reversion trade opposite the spike direction at market open of the confirming bar. 4. Use H4 for regime context (trend vs range) — only take counter-trend entries if H4 is ranging (ADX < 25).
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x ATR(14) beyond entry. Take profit: 0.5x ATR(14) (tight — this is a volatility contraction scalp). Trail stop to breakeven after 1x ATR in profit. Max hold: 8 H1 bars. If not hit by then, close at market.
archived.failure_mode: Extended trend continuation after a volatility spike (gap-and-go moves, NFP blowouts). The confirming narrow bar may simply be a brief pause before the next leg. Also fails in low-volatility environments where ATR% never reaches 90.
archived.diversification_value: Existing volatility idea (Volatility_Contraction_Breakout) trades expansion. This trades contraction — opposite logic, decorrelated entries, works in different market regimes. Adds a short-vol scalping layer.

archived.name: Session_Flow_Exhaustion
archived.description: Tracks cumulative tick-direction proxy (close vs open of each 1-min bar) within a session. When one side dominates >65% of volume bars by count, the session is imbalanced. A counter-move in the final 60-90 minutes of the session fades the imbalance for a mean-reverting scalp.
archived.entry_logic: 1. At the start of each major session (Asian 00:00, London 08:00, NY 13:00 UTC), begin tracking: count of up-minutes (close > open) vs down-minutes (close < open). 2. When any session has accumulated >65% imbalance in one direction with at least 90 minutes elapsed AND price is >0.3% from session VWAP, flag as exhausted. 3. Wait for a 5-minute bar to close in the opposite direction of the dominant flow. 4. Enter toward session VWAP at market.
archived.exit_logic: Take profit at session VWAP (primary target) or 0.5x ATR(5). Stop loss: 1x ATR(5). Hard exit at session close regardless of P&L. Max 2 trades per session.
archived.failure_mode: Strong trending days (NFP, FOMC, geopolitical) overwhelm the mean-reversion signal — imbalance continues through session end. Spread costs on M5 eat profits in sideways sessions with 50-55% imbalance. Multiple-entry temptation when first trade loses.
archived.diversification_value: Only existing other idea (OrderFlow_Imbalance_Scalper) uses tick-level order flow. This uses a simpler price-derived flow proxy (no tick data needed) and trades session boundaries — different entry timing, different data requirements, complementary coverage.

archived.name: Hurst_Exponent_Regime_Detector
archived.description: Rolling Hurst exponent (R/S analysis on 50-bar window, smoothed with EMA-5) classifies gold as trending (H>0.55), mean-reverting (H<0.45), or random walk. Switches strategy logic in real-time: momentum on trending, mean-reversion on reverting, stand aside on random walk. No macro inputs needed — purely fractal structure detection.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute Hurst exponent over trailing 50 bars using R/S analysis (range/standard deviation of cumulated deviations). 2. Smooth with 5-period EMA. 3. If H>0.55 → trend regime: entry on pullback to 20-EMA with ADX>25 confirmation. 4. If H<0.45 → reversion regime: entry when price deviates >1.5σ from 50-SMA with RSI<30/>70. 5. If 0.45≤H≤0.55 → no trade.
archived.exit_logic: Trend regime: trailing ATR(14)*2 stop, take profit at 3R. Reversion regime: fixed 1:1.5 RR, stop at 1.5×ATR beyond entry. Remove 50% at 1R in reversion mode.
archived.failure_mode: Hurst estimator has high variance on small windows (50 bars). EMA smoothing helps but adds lag — regime transitions may be detected late during fast whipsaw. XAUUSD can switch character mid-bar. Parameter sensitivity over different market vol regimes.
archived.diversification_value: Only existing regime_filter ideas use ATR magnitude (ATR_Regime_Selector) or macro drivers (Macro_Regime_Shifter). This one uses pure fractal math — completely decorrelated signal source. Works in any market, any timeframe. Captures structural transitions macro filters miss.

archived.name: Cross_Asset_Gamma_Flip
archived.description: Gold reacts asymmetrically to risk-on/risk-off moves depending on whether bonds are rising or falling. When SP500 drops AND US10Y yield is falling (rates cut = accommodation) gold rallies as inflation hedge. When SP500 drops AND US10Y yield RISES (rates up = liquidity panic) gold ALSO drops. This allows trading the FLIP — buying gold on equity panic with falling yields, shorting on equity panic with rising yields. Checks all three instruments concurrently.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Detect a 5-bar consecutive decline in SPY/SPX >1.5% (risk-off event). 2. Check US10Y yield direction over same period: if yield falling (>5bp decline) → long XAUUSD; if yield rising (>5bp increase) → short XAUUSD. 3. Confirm DXY is not diverging (>0.5% move against expected correlation). 4. Enter at market on confirmed signal. 5. Only trade between 07:00-17:00 UTC (liquid hours).
archived.exit_logic: Trailing stop at 1× ATR(14) from the highest/lowest attained since entry. Take partial profit 50% at 2R, runner to 4R or until equity recovery (SPX closes above 5-bar low) which negates the panic. Max hold 12 bars.
archived.failure_mode: False signals when the risk-off event is shallow or temporary (V-shaped recovery). Correlation between gold/bond direction is not 100% — gold can rally with both yields rising if it is a stagflation scare. Lag in yield data across instruments. Position sizing complex with multi-asset confirmation.
archived.diversification_value: Existing cross_asset ideas only use gold-silver ratio (Gold_Silver_Ratio_Rotation) and gold-DXY correlation (DXY_Valence_Correlation). This one triangulates THREE instruments (equities + bonds + gold) and captures the non-linear flip behaviour — completely different signal logic. Also has a bearish gold leg, which most existing strategies lack.

archived.name: Optimal_F_Kelly_Sizer
archived.description: Risk overlay that uses a modified Kelly Criterion to size trades based on the strategy's own historical edge. Instead of fixed 1% risk, computes f* = W - (1-W)/(R) where W = historical win rate and R = average win/average loss ratio. Caps at quarter-Kelly (f*/4). Recalculates every 20 closed trades with exponential decay weighting (recent trades weighted 2×). Falls back to fixed 1% when sample <20 trades.
archived.entry_logic: Not an entry strategy — overlay on any existing strategy. After entry signal fires, look up current Kelly fraction. Multiply base position (e.g. 1% risk) by the Kelly multiplier: multiplier = min(f*/0.25, 2.0) clamped to [0.25, 2.0]. Compute lot size = (account_equity * risk_pct * multiplier) / (stop_distance * pip_value).
archived.exit_logic: No exit logic of its own — overlays parent strategy's exits. If Kelly fraction drops below 0.05 (edge eroded), reduce exposure to 25% and flag strategy for review. If no trades for 50 bars with capital deployed, reduce to minimum position.
archived.failure_mode: Kelly assumes stationary distribution of outcomes — strategy edge can evaporate or regime-shift, causing over-betting into a losing run. Exponential decay helps but 20-trade window may be too short for statistical significance. Adapts slowly to sudden drawdown. Self-referential risk: better recent performance → bigger bets → bigger potential loss on next trade.
archived.diversification_value: Existing risk_overlay ideas use volatility parity (Volatility_Parity_Scale) and slippage regimes (Slippage_Regime_Sizer). Neither uses the strategy's own performance statistics to size bets. Kelly optimal f is a mathematically grounded approach that maximizes long-term geometric growth — different philosophy from fixed-fraction or volatility-adjusted sizing. Complements rather than replaces existing overlays.

archived.name: Momentum_Volume_Convergence
archived.description: Volume-weighted momentum strategy that enters longs/shorts only when price momentum and volume momentum converge (both rising or both falling), filtering out low-volume breakouts and fading high-volume reversals. Uses a rolling 20-period correlation between volume % change and price % change.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute 14-period RSI on close. 2. Compute 14-period volume RSI (rank volume bars). 3. LONG if: price RSI > 55 AND volume RSI > 55 AND price above 20 EMA AND current bar volume > 20-period median volume. 4. SHORT if: price RSI < 45 AND volume RSI < 45 AND price below 20 EMA AND current bar volume > 20-period median volume. 5. Skip if price RSI and volume RSI diverge (one above 50, other below 50) — conflicting signals.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x ATR(14) from entry. Take profit: 3x ATR(14) or 3:1 risk-reward. Trail stop: activate at 1x ATR profit, trail at 0.5x ATR. Time stop: close after 48 bars if not in profit.
archived.failure_mode: Low-volume trending markets where momentum is real but volume never confirms — strategy stays flat and misses the move. Also fails in high-volume chop where volume RSI oscillates noisily around 50, generating whipsaw entries.
archived.diversification_value: Unlike Momentum_Confluence_Gold (H1 trend/MACD) and NFP_Volatility_Momentum (M5 event-driven), this uses volume momentum as a required confirmation gate — it only trades when two independent momentum axes agree. Completely different signal source.

archived.name: Bollinger_Squeeze_Momentum_Breakout
archived.description: Captures explosive directional moves following Bollinger Band squeeze contractions. When BB width contracts below its 20-period percentile (squeeze), ADX below 20 confirms low volatility. The strategy goes long/short on the first bar to close outside the bands with ADX > 25 and rising — the squeeze release.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute BB(20,2) and BB width = (upper-lower)/middle. 2. Compute ADX(14). 3. Identify squeeze: BB width < 20th percentile of its 20-period range AND ADX < 20. 4. LONG entry when: close > upper band AND ADX > 25 AND ADX rising from prior bar AND current close = bar high (bullish close). 5. SHORT entry when: close < lower band AND ADX > 25 AND ADX rising AND current close = bar low (bearish close). 6. Cancel if BB width was not in squeeze zone within prior 5 bars.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: below the squeeze low (for longs) or above squeeze high (for shorts) — structural invalidation level. Take profit: 2x ATR(14) fixed target. Alternative: exit when BB width re-expands above its 50th percentile (volatility regime shift complete).
archived.failure_mode: Fakeouts — price pierces the band then immediately reverses. The ADX gate reduces but does not eliminate these. Also fails in strongly trending markets that never squeeze (permanently wide bands) — strategy has extended flat periods.
archived.diversification_value: London_Killzone_Breakout trades time-based Asian/London breaks; Accumulation_Distribution_Breakout trades volume accumulation patterns. This is purely volatility-based: it waits for a volatility contraction (squeeze) followed by an expansion breakout. Completely different trigger mechanism — market microstructure timing vs. volatility regime timing.

archived.name: Turn_Of_Month_Gold
archived.description: Exploits the institutional turn-of-month (TOM) effect in gold — the tendency for systematic rebalancing, option expiry, and fund flows concentrated in the first 3 and last 3 trading days of each month. Combines with VIX/XAU correlation regime to directional-bias entries.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Identify TOM window = last 3 AND first 3 trading days of each calendar month (excluding weekends/holidays). 2. Within TOM window, compute 5-day rate of change (ROC). 3. LONG if ROC < -1% (oversold within window) AND DXY is falling (DXY close < DXY 10 SMA). 4. SHORT if ROC > +1% (overbought within window) AND DXY is rising. 5. If TOM window and no clear ROC signal, trade the previous month-end closing direction: long if last day of prior month closed green, short if red. 6. OUTSIDE TOM window: stay flat.
archived.exit_logic: Time stop: exit at TOM window close (end of last day). Profit target: 2.5% of entry or 2x ATR(14) whichever is smaller. Stop loss: 1x ATR(14). No trailing — strict time-bound exit.
archived.failure_mode: TOM effect may be weak or reversed in strongly trending months — the strategy fights the dominant trend. If gold is in a sustained bull run, shorting a +1% within-TOM spike against the trend is catastrophic. The DXY filter helps but is not foolproof.
archived.diversification_value: Gold_Seasonal_Cycle trades broad annual/monthly seasonal composites on D1. Intraweek_Session_Drift trades day-of-week intraday tendencies. This targets a completely different calendar effect — the precise 6-day window around month-end driven by institutional cash flows, option expiry, and portfolio rebalancing. Higher frequency seasonal (monthly vs yearly) with a defined structural rationale.

archived.name: Volume_Weighted_Mean_Reverter
archived.description: Mean reversion at VWAP envelope extremes with participation-volume confirmation. Uses multi-session VWAP (1H, 4H, daily) to create zones of expected value. Entries only when price deviates >1 standard deviation from the anchor VWAP AND the current 5-minute candle has at least 1.5x typical volume. Exit when price returns to VWAP mean or volume dries up.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold oscillates around its volume-weighted average price during low-volatility sessions (Asian/London overlap) as institutional order flow provides mean-reverting pressure. When volume spikes coincide with extreme VWAP deviations, price almost always snaps back within 5-12 bars on M15 as market-makers and algorithms fade the dislocation.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate VWAP for Daily, H4, and H1 sessions independently. 2. Compute VWAP std deviation bands (1.0, 1.5, 2.0) for each timeframe. 3. When price touches or exceeds the 1.5-std band on any anchor timeframe, wait for the next 5-minute candle to confirm. 4. Confirmation requires: (a) candle volume >= 1.5x the 20-period median volume, (b) candle closes within the 1.0-std band. 5. Enter 2 ticks inside the band on M15 close.
archived.exit_logic: SL: 1.2x ATR(14) from entry (8-12 pips typical on H1). Primary TP: return to VWAP anchor line. Secondary TP: if price reaches VWAP and continues through, tighten to 1:1 risk and exit on H1 close through VWAP. Hard exit at London session end (16:00 UTC).
archived.failure_mode: Fails during strong trend days when VWAP deviations are structural (breakaway gaps, FOMC runs) rather than mean-reverting dislocations. Also fails during ultra-low-volume holiday sessions where the volume confirmation is never met.
archived.diversification_value: Fills mean_reversion with a volume-centric approach distinct from the existing z-score (Statistical_Mean_Reverter) and candle-structure (Wick_Exhaustion_Reverter) strategies.

archived.name: Volatility_Term_Structure_Fade
archived.description: Trades volatility mean-reversion by comparing short-term (10-period) ATR to its medium-term (50-period) and long-term (200-period) history. When the short-term vol ratio exceeds 2.0, volatility is statistically extended and likely to contract. Unlike Volatility_Skew_Mean_Reverter (which fades fixed-percentile extremes), this uses a dynamic term-structure ratio adaptive to the current vol baseline.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold volatility exhibits mean-reverting term structure: a sharp short-term vol spike (from a news event or liquidity shock) is typically followed by a vol contraction over 6-12 hours. The ratio of short-term to long-term ATR is stationary around 1.0, with excursions beyond 2.0 being rare (~8% of hours) and almost always followed by a snap-back below 1.5 within 48 hours.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate ATR(10), median ATR(50), and median ATR(200) on H1. 2. Compute VolRatio_short = ATR(10)/median ATR(50) and VolRatio_long = ATR(10)/median ATR(200). 3. Signal when BOTH ratios exceed 2.0 simultaneously. 4. Entry direction: if next H1 close is >70% of spike body in same direction, trade continuation fade. If close <30%, fade fully against spike. 5. Split entry: 50% market, 50% if price retraces 30% of spike range.
archived.exit_logic: SL: 1.5x ATR(10) of entry candle (15-25 pips). TP1 (50%): when ATR(10) drops below 1.5x median ATR(50). TP2 (50%): when ATR(10) drops below 1.2x median ATR(50). Hard stop on new vol spike or after 48 hours.
archived.failure_mode: Fails during cascading volatility events (consecutive news shocks, war escalations) where short-term vol stays extended for days. Also fails in ultra-quiet markets where ratio never triggers.
archived.diversification_value: Third angle in volatility family: Volatility_Contraction_Breakout (vol expansion), Volatility_Skew_Mean_Reverter (fixed-percentile fade), this (term-structure ratio). Complementary coverage.

archived.name: Session_Liquidity_Sweep_Scalper
archived.description: Exploits programmed stop-loss hunting at session high/low levels. Each major session establishes initial extremes in the first 30 minutes. These levels act as magnetic liquidity zones — algorithms push price through them to trigger stops, then reverse. Enters on the reversal candle after a clean sweep of a session-established extreme.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold exhibits repeatable liquidity-sweep behaviour at session boundaries. First 30 min of each session (Asian 00:00, London 07:00, NY 12:30 GMT) set initial high/low. Price oscillates, then pushes through one extreme to hunt stops, then reverses within 1-3 M5 candles. Cleanest during overlap sessions.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Identify current session and its first 30-min high/low. 2. Mark the 10-pip zone beyond each extreme (stop-hunt zone). 3. When price breaks INTO the stop-hunt zone (3+ consecutive M5 closes beyond the extreme), wait for next M5 candle to close BACK inside original range. 4. Enter on reversal candle close — long on downward sweep, short on upward sweep. 5. Minimum volume: entry candle >= 1.0x 20-period median M5 volume.
archived.exit_logic: SL: 5 pips beyond sweep extreme (10 pips from entry). TP1 (60%): at session midpoint. TP2 (40%): at opposite extreme of initial 30-min range, or session end, whichever first. No trailing.
archived.failure_mode: Fails in strong trend sessions where the sweep is genuine absorption (trend continuation through stop zone) rather than a reversal sweep. Also fails during high-impact news within the first 30 minutes contaminating the initial range.
archived.diversification_value: Fills "other" family with level-based microstructure scalping — entirely different from OrderFlow_Imbalance_Scalper (tick-level imbalance) and Session_Flow_Exhaustion (cumulative directional bias).

archived.name: MultiTimeframe_ADX_Trend_Momentum
archived.description: Trend-following momentum strategy using multi-timeframe ADX alignment. Enters when ADX is trending (>25) on H4 AND D1, and short-term pullback on H1 gives a re-entry in the trend direction. Captures sustained directional moves and avoids choppy sideways markets through ADX trending threshold filtering.
archived.entry_logic: 1) H4 and D1 both show ADX(14) > 25 (trending regime). 2) H1 ADX > 20 but < 40 to avoid exhaustion. 3) For longs: H4 and D1 DI+ > DI- (bullish trend). 4) H1 price pulls back to 20EMA or H1 VWAP (pullback entry). 5) H1 candle closes back above VWAP/EMA with bullish momentum (MACD histogram turning up). 6) For shorts: opposite conditions with DI- dominance.
archived.exit_logic: Stop Loss: 1.5x ATR(14) below/above entry. Take Profit: 1st TP at 2x ATR (50% position), 2nd TP at 4x ATR (remaining 50%). Trail remaining position with 1x ATR chandelier stop once 2nd TP is hit. If H1 ADX drops below 20, exit remaining position immediately (trend fading).
archived.failure_mode: Fails in ranging markets where ADX spikes briefly from noise before reversing. Also fails in very strong trends where pullbacks are shallow or do not reach the EMA - may miss the best entries. Whipsaws when three timeframes are not aligned.
archived.diversification_value: Existing momentum ideas focus on confluence (Momentum_Confluence_Gold), news events (NFP_Volatility_Momentum), and volume (Momentum_Volume_Convergence). None use pure multi-timeframe ADX alignment for trend-following. This fills the directional trend-following gap in the momentum family.

archived.name: Real_Yield_Gold_Inverse_Corr
archived.description: Exploits the well-documented inverse correlation between US real yields (TIPS yields) and gold prices. When real yields fall, gold typically rises (lower opportunity cost of holding gold). When real yields rise, gold falls. Uses weekly TIPS yield data as the primary signal with DXY as a secondary confirmation filter.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Track US 10-year TIPS real yield on weekly timeframe. 2) LONG gold when: Real yield drops >15bp over a rolling 2-week window AND DXY is not in a strong uptrend (below 20-week SMA). 3) SHORT gold when: Real yield rises >15bp over a rolling 2-week window AND DXY confirms (above 20-week SMA). 4) Enter on D1 at market open Monday after weekly signal triggers, using limit orders. 5) Confirm with daily candle close in the signal direction.
archived.exit_logic: Stop Loss: 3x weekly ATR(14) from entry (wide - macro swing). Take Profit: Exit when real yield move reverses by >10bp or after holding 4 weeks (time-stop). If DXY crosses the 20-week SMA against the position, exit immediately (correlation break). Trailing stop: 1.5x weekly ATR once profit exceeds 2x weekly ATR.
archived.failure_mode: Correlation breaks during risk-off flights (e.g., March 2020 when both gold and real yields fell - liquidity crush trumped fundamentals). Slow to react in fast markets due to weekly data. Central bank rate surprises cause violent reversals within days.
archived.diversification_value: Existing cross_asset ideas use DXY correlation (DXY_Valence_Correlation), gold/silver ratio (Gold_Silver_Ratio_Rotation), and multi-asset gamma (Cross_Asset_Gamma_Flip). None target the real yield / gold inverse relationship - the most fundamental gold driver. This is pure macro driver approach complementing the technically-focused existing set.

archived.name: Structural_Level_Breakout_With_Retest
archived.description: Breakout strategy built on market structure levels - swing highs/lows, trendlines, and order blocks. Unlike indicator-based or session-based breakouts, this uses naked price structure: a confirmed swing point (3+ candles with higher highs on each side for resistance, lower lows for support) defines the level. The strategy waits for a clean break AND retest before committing, filtering out trap breakouts.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Identify structural swing high/low on H1: 3+ consecutive candles with higher highs left and right of peak (resistance) or lower lows (support). 2) Price breaks the level by >0.5 ATR(14) on H1 (clean break). 3) No entry on break - wait for retest. 4) LONG: price breaks above resistance, retests it as new support (wick touches or closes within 0.3 ATR of broken level). 5) Entry on retest candle close back above the level. 6) SHORT: opposite for broken support retested as resistance. 7) M15 confirmation: RSI(14) >50 for longs, <50 for shorts on retest candle close.
archived.exit_logic: Stop Loss: 1x ATR(14) below/above the retested structural level. Take Profit: 1st TP at 1.5x ATR (60% position). 2nd TP at 3x ATR (40% position). If next structural swing point is within 3x ATR, use that as TP instead. No trailing - let structure define exits.
archived.failure_mode: Fails in strong trends where price never retests - just runs. Fails in fakeout scenarios where break + retest trigger but price reverses (common at round numbers). High subjectivity in defining "structural" levels.
archived.diversification_value: Existing breakout ideas use session timing (London_Killzone_Breakout), accumulation patterns (Accumulation_Distribution_Breakout), and Bollinger squeeze (Bollinger_Squeeze_Momentum_Breakout). None use pure price structure breakouts with retest - the classic S/R breakout approach. Strategically catches breakouts confirmed as "real" by retest, unlike the others that enter on initial break which can be traps.

archived.name: Volatility_Cluster_Regime_Map
archived.description: Unsupervised rolling clustering of ATR(14), ADX(14), and 20-period correlation to XAUUDNOK to map 4 latent volatility regimes (compressed/expanding/trending/erratic), then trades only in the expanding regime with momentum confirmation.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute ATR(14), ADX(14), and XAUUDNOK 20-period rolling correlation daily at 00:00 UTC. 2. Feed into k-means (k=4) on a 200-bar rolling window to classify current regime. 3. If regime == "expanding" (cluster with highest ADX + rising ATR) AND price > 20-EMA AND RSI(14) between 50-70: enter long. Short mirror: price < 20-EMA, RSI 30-50. 4. Minimum 12 hours since last cluster transition to avoid whipsaw.
archived.exit_logic: SL: 1.5× ATR(14) at entry. TP: 3× ATR(14). Trailing stop activates at 1.5× ATR profit, trails at 0.5× ATR. Regime re-classify every 4 hours; if regime drops to "compressed" or "erratic" mid-trade, tighten SL to breakeven.
archived.failure_mode: K-means produces unstable clusters in sideways churn — regime label flips every 4 hours causing premature exits. Also fails in fast-crash scenarios where all three metrics surge simultaneously and the "erratic" cluster captures the move too late.
archived.diversification_value: No existing regime filter uses unsupervised clustering; the others are deterministic rule-based (ATR thresholds, macro indicators, Hurst exponent). This adds a data-driven adaptive layer with no human bias on regime boundaries.

archived.name: Quarterly_Roll_Effect
archived.description: Exploits the consistent tendency for gold futures rolls (March/June/September/December expiration cycles) and quarterly institutional rebalancing to create predictable 3-5 day directional windows. Entry window: 3 days before first notice day through 2 days after.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate days to COMEX gold futures first notice day (FND) for current contract month. 2. Entry window activates T-3 through T+2 relative to FND. 3. During window: look for a 2-bar compression (ATR < 20-period ATR average) followed by a close above prior day high (long) or below prior day low (short). 4. If FND falls in a historically bullish month (Jan/Feb/Aug/Sep) bias long; bearish months (Mar/Jun/Oct/Nov) bias short; neutral months trade both directions equally.
archived.exit_logic: Hard exit at T+5 regardless of P&L (the edge decays). SL: 1× ATR(14) at entry. TP: 2× ATR(14). If position shows profit at T+2, trail at 1× ATR. No re-entry into same quarterly window.
archived.failure_mode: Central bank interventions or unexpected macro events (rate decisions, NFP) during the 5-day window overwhelm the seasonal edge. Also, some quarters see no roll activity if open interest shifts early — the window is empty.
archived.diversification_value: Existing seasonal ideas cover annual gold cycles, intraweek drift, and turn-of-month. This is the only idea tied to futures contract mechanics and institutional rebalancing flows — a completely different seasonal driver.

archived.name: FVG_Imbalance_Fill
archived.description: Mean reversion into Fair Value Gaps (FVG) from impulsive 3-candle sequences. When rapid directional moves leave unfilled gap zones between candle bodies, price returns to fill ~70% within 5-15 bars on M15. Enters on touch of FVG boundary with candle-structure rejection and RSI extreme confirmation.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold frequently creates Fair Value Gaps (FVG) in fast directional moves - a 3-candle sequence where the wick of the middle candle leaves a gap between the bodies of the surrounding candles. These gaps remain as magnetic zones that price returns to fill ~70% of the time within 5-15 bars on M15. The phenomenon is strongest during London/NY overlap (high liquidity) and weakest during Asian session. Institutional algorithms and market-makers actively trade back to these levels to clear unfilled orders, creating a self-fulfilling mean-reversion pattern.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Detect FVG on M15: 3-candle pattern where candle A low > candle C high (bullish gap) or candle A high < candle C low (bearish gap), with candle B body completely outside neighbors range. 2. Mark FVG boundaries: upper = min(candle A low, candle C high) for bullish gaps; lower = max(candle A high, candle C low) for bearish gaps. 3. Wait 3+ bars after formation (impulse matures). 4. Enter when price touches FVG boundary AND touching candle shows rejection (wick >= 2x body size) on M15. 5. RSI(14) <30 for bullish fill, >70 for bearish fill. 6. Skip if FVG formed 20+ bars ago (decayed), or if ADX > 30 (strong momentum invalidates reversion).
archived.exit_logic: SL: beyond FVG zone + 5 pips. TP: nearest structural swing or 1.5x ATR(14), closer wins. Split 60% at 1x ATR, 40% runner to 1.5x ATR. Time-stop: exit after 15 M15 bars. No re-entry into same FVG.
archived.failure_mode: Fails in strong trending markets (gap-and-go, NFP, geopolitical shocks) where FVGs remain unfilled for extended periods. Multiple overlapping FVGs create ambiguity. Spread-sensitive on M15. RSI filter may cause false negatives on valid fills.
archived.diversification_value: All existing mean_reversion ideas use statistical bands (z-score), candle anatomy (wick exhaustion), or VWAP. FVG fill is pure price-structure reversion targeting unfair-price zones from impulsive moves - a completely different reversion category catching post-impulse snap-backs none of the others target.

archived.name: Volatility_Momentum_Ride
archived.description: Volatility trend-following strategy - the only non-fading volatility approach in the archive. Rides volatility expansion phases by entering when ATR(14) crosses above its 50-SMA by 1.2x, trading in direction of 20-EMA slope. Stays in until ATR(14) contracts back below its 50-SMA, capturing the full expansion wave.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold volatility exhibits momentum itself - once ATR expands, it tends to continue expanding for 6-12 bars before peaking and contracting. During expansion phases, price trends strongly with self-reinforcing dynamics: breakout attracts attention, traders pile in, volume increases, driving more volatility. Gold volatility expansions persist for an average 8 bars on H1, producing strong directional moves. This is the direct opposite of volatility mean-reversion - it is volatility trend-following.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute ATR(14) and 50-period SMA on H1. 2. ATR ratio = ATR(14) / SMA(ATR, 50). 3. Entry when ATR ratio crosses ABOVE 1.2 (vol expansion, not peak). 4. Direction: 20-EMA slope > 0 AND close > 20-EMA -> long; EMA slope < 0 AND close < 20-EMA -> short. 5. H4 must also have ATR ratio > 1.0. 6. Enter at market on H1 close after confirmation. 7. One re-entry if stopped out but ATR ratio still > 1.2 and direction intact.
archived.exit_logic: Primary SL: ATR ratio drops below 1.0 (vol contraction = ride over). Secondary SL: price closes through 20-EMA against position. TP: exit when ATR ratio < 1.0 (full expansion wave captured). Trail at 1x ATR(14) after 2x ATR profit. Hard time-stop at 24h. Single-ticket, no partial exits.
archived.failure_mode: False volatility spikes from short-lived news events (reversing 2-3 bars) produce whipsaw. Gap-heavy environments where ATR jumps and immediately contracts (illiquid after-hours). Extended low-vol regimes where ATR ratio stays < 1.2 for weeks - strategy flat.
archived.diversification_value: ALL existing volatility ideas are mean-reverting (fade). Volatility_Contraction_Breakout trades expansion-from-squeeze then exits. Volatility_Skew_Mean_Reverter and Volatility_Term_Structure_Fade both fade extremes. This is the ONLY vol momentum/trend-following approach - rides the expansion wave instead of betting on contraction. Highest orthogonal value in the volatility family.

archived.name: Pivot_Point_Bounce_Scalper
archived.description: Institutional pivot-point scalper that fades touches of daily pivot levels (R1, R2, S1, S2) on normal-volatility days. Gold bounces off standard pivot levels ~65-70% within 2-3 M15 candles from algorithmic reference-point trading. Enters on candle-structure rejection with volume confirmation, targeting central pivot or next level.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold exhibits strong mean-reverting behavior around standard pivot points (R1, R2, S1, S2, central pivot) during liquid sessions. These levels act as intraday gravity zones because institutional algorithms use them as reference points for stop placement, order entry, and hedging. On normal vol days (non-NFP/non-FOMC), gold bounces off pivot levels 65-70% of the time within 2-3 M15 candles. Strongest at R1/S1, degrades at R2/S2.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute daily pivots before Asian open: P = (H_prev+L_prev+C_prev)/3, R1=2P-L_prev, S1=2P-H_prev, R2=P+(H_prev-L_prev), S2=P-(H_prev-L_prev). 2. Normal day filter: prev day ATR(14) within 0.7-1.3x of 20-day avg. 3. LONG: price touches S1/S2 AND M15 candle shows bullish rejection (close > open, body above pivot level). 4. SHORT: price touches R1/R2 AND bearish rejection (close < open, body below pivot). 5. Volume: entry candle vol > 1.2x 20-period median M15 vol. 6. Skip if same level already bounced once today, or within 30 min of high-impact news.
archived.exit_logic: SL: beyond pivot level by 0.5x ATR(14) on M15 (5-8 pips). TP1 (50%): central pivot for S1/S2 trades, R1/S1 for P trades. TP2 (50%): next pivot level. Time-stop: exit after 3h. Max 3 trades/day.
archived.failure_mode: Fails on trending days (NFP, FOMC, geopolitics) where pivots overrun without reversal - consecutive losing bounces. Extreme low-vol chop where price oscillates between pivots without clean bounces - spread costs dominate. Pivot levels are crowd-sourced and algorithms may fake the bounce to trigger stops then run.
archived.diversification_value: Existing other ideas use tick-level order flow (OrderFlow_Imbalance_Scalper), session cumulative bias (Session_Flow_Exhaustion), and stop-hunt sweeps (Session_Liquidity_Sweep_Scalper). None use intraday pivot points - the most widely-used institutional level framework. Pure mathematical level-based approach targeting 65-70% win rate with tight stops, decorrelated from microstructure and flow-imbalance strategies.

archived.name: COT_Positioning_Extreme_Fade
archived.description: Uses weekly CFTC Commitments of Traders data to identify extreme speculative net long/short positioning in gold futures. When Managed Money net longs hit multi-year percentile extremes (90th+ or 10th-), take a contrarian fade position anticipating reversion as the marginal buyer/seller is exhausted.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Load weekly COT data for Gold futures (Managed Money net positions). 2. Compute z-score of net positioning vs 3-year rolling window. 3. When z-score > +2.0 (extreme long) and price is above 200 EMA (overextended trend), go short. 4. When z-score < -2.0 (extreme short) and price is below 200 EMA, go long. 5. Confirm with bearish/bullish divergence on RSI(14) daily. 6. Enter at next H4 open after COT release (Friday 15:30 ET or Monday open).
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x ATR(14) on D1. Take profit: 50% at 2x ATR(H4), remainder at 1x ATR(D1) or when COT z-score drops below |1.0| (reversion confirmed). Trailing stop after 50% TP hit moves to 1x ATR(H4). Max hold: 10 trading days.
