archived.failure_mode: Extended trend regimes where fundamentals override positioning (e.g., persistent war premium, rate cutting cycles). COT data has 3-day lag — regime can shift before the fade triggers. Low trade frequency (5-8 signals/year).
archived.diversification_value: Solely fundamental/sentiment-driven — zero correlation with any price-action or technical strategy in the archive. Uses weekly institutional flow data, not price action. Acts as a portfolio hedge during sentiment extremes.

archived.name: Structural_MSS_Continuation
archived.description: Captures trend continuation by identifying Market Structure Shifts (MSS/CHOCH — Change of Character) on pullbacks within established trends. After a clear swing high/low break in the opposite direction confirms a trend change, enters in the new trend direction with Order Block mitigation as confluence. Brings SMC/ICT displacement logic to the gold strategy mix.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Identify trend on H1: 50 EMA slope + higher highs/higher lows (uptrend) or lower highs/lower lows (downtrend). 2. Wait for a pullback that breaks the most recent swing point (demand flips to supply or vice versa). 3. Confirm MSS on M15: a clean break of structure with a displacement candle (1.5x average range, close beyond the swing high/low). 4. Mark the last Order Block (the base candle before the displacement move). 5. Enter limit order at 50% retracement of the Order Block + 1 pip. 6. Optional: FVG (fair value gap) in the displacement move adds confluence.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: below the Order Block low (1x ATR buffer). Take profit 1: 1R (50% position). Take profit 2: trail remaining at previous swing high/low. No fixed TP — let the trend run until structure breaks against. Max hold: 48 hours. If price fails to reach entry within 12 hours, cancel.
archived.failure_mode: Ranging/choppy markets where structure constantly flips (false MSS — whipsway). Requires subjective identification of Order Blocks. Performs poorly in news-driven vertical moves that skip mitigation levels. Low win rate in low-volatility regimes.
archived.diversification_value: Only SMC/ICT-structured strategy in the portfolio. All existing momentum ideas use ADX, RSI convergence, or volume — this is purely structure-based (swing points, displacement, order blocks). Negative correlation with mean reversion strategies. Works best when other momentum ideas are struggling (trend consolidation phase vs trend extension).

archived.name: Lunar_Phase_Gold_Cycle
archived.description: Exploits the documented anomaly of lunar phase effects on gold price direction and volatility. Statistical studies show gold tends to exhibit higher volatility and directional bias during new moon and full moon periods, with mean reversion in the following week. Enters on the lunar phase transition and holds through the expected bias window.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Determine current lunar phase via astronomical calendar (new moon, first quarter, full moon, last quarter). 2. At new moon: go LONG if price is above 50-day SMA and VIX < 25 (risk-on environment). Hold for 5 days. 3. At full moon: go SHORT if price is below 50-day SMA or RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Hold for 3 days. 4. At first/last quarter: stay flat unless ATR(14) expands >20% (volatility phase entry). 5. Near-quarter phases: only trade if a confirmed daily SMT divergence (gold vs silver) is present. 6. Filter out events within 3 days of major FOMC/NFP. 7. Enter at market open of the lunar day (00:00 UTC).
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x ATR(14) on D1. Take profit: time-based exit at end of hold period (3-5 days). No price-based scaling — strict time exit. If price hits +2x ATR before hold period ends, move SL to breakeven and let time run. If price hits -1x ATR within 24h of entry, exit immediately (failed signal).
archived.failure_mode: Low signal count (only 12-13 new moons + 12-13 full moons per year = ~25 trade opportunities, most filtered out to ~6-8/year). Lunar anomalies are weakly documented in academic literature for gold specifically. High probability of random noise overwhelming the subtle cyclical signal. Calendar effects erode as algos front-run known dates.
archived.diversification_value: Zero correlation with all existing strategies — no technical indicator, no price action, no volume, no volatility metric. Pure calendar/astronomical cycle. Acts as a non-correlated tail hedge in a portfolio of technical strategies. Also diversifies the seasonal family away from macro calendar (NFP, FOMC, month-end) into an orthogonal cycle.

archived.name: Volume_Profile_Acceptance_Breakout
archived.description: Enter on breakout beyond Volume Profile High Volume Node (HVN) value area, confirmed by acceptance (close beyond VAH/VAL with above-average volume). Retest entry. Uses post-break acceptance filter that traps fakeouts.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate Volume Profile over last 5-10 days. 2. Identify HVN and value area high/low (VAH, VAL). 3. Wait for break outside value area. 4. Confirm acceptance: candle closes beyond VAH/VAL with above-avg volume. 5. Enter on retest of VAH/VAL as new support/resistance.
archived.exit_logic: SL below HVN midpoint for longs, above for shorts. TP1 at 1x ATR, TP2 at 2x ATR. Trail remaining at 1x ATR lock.
archived.failure_mode: Low-volume markets produce unreliable volume profiles. Choppy range-bound markets cause repeated false breaks straddling the value area.
archived.diversification_value: Pure volume-based breakout with acceptance filter. No overlap with existing breakouts (time-based, pattern-based, Bollinger squeeze, structural levels). Adds volume confirmation layer.

archived.name: Volume_Delta_Exhaustion_Reverter
archived.description: Mean reversion using cumulative delta divergence — when price makes a new swing high but aggressive buying volume declines, it reveals institutional absorption and sets up a reversion trade.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate cumulative delta (buy-sell volume) per candle. 2. Identify divergence: price HH / delta LH (bearish) or price LL / delta HL (bullish). 3. Wait for momentum exhaustion candle (smaller body, longer wick, reducing volume). 4. Enter on first retracement candle. 5. Filter: only trade when ADX < 25 (non-trending market).
archived.exit_logic: SL beyond swing high/low where divergence occurred. TP at VWAP or prior HVN. Max hold 8 candles; scratch if not at TP by then.
archived.failure_mode: Strong trend days overwhelm delta divergence for multiple bars. Intraday delta data quality depends on broker feed. ADX filter may cause missed trades in choppy low-vol markets.
archived.diversification_value: Uses cumulative delta divergence — unique signal source among existing MR bots (which use z-score, wick anatomy, volume-weighted MA, FVG fills). Adds order-flow dimension.

archived.name: Implied_Realized_Spread_Compression
archived.description: Trades volatility expansion when implied volatility and realized volatility converge to an unusually tight spread (<15th percentile historical). Entry in direction of the first 2x ATR breakout candle.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate 14-day realized volatility (ATR-based). 2. Estimate implied volatility (proxy via ATR smoothed by Hull MA). 3. Compute spread = |IV - RV| / RV. 4. When spread < 0.15 (15th percentile), enter monitoring mode. 5. On first 2x ATR candle in either direction, enter that direction. 6. Add second unit if price continues same direction for 3 consecutive candles.
archived.exit_logic: SL 1x ATR below entry. TP at 3x ATR. Hard time stop at 12 hours. No trailing — expansion plays held to full resolution.
archived.failure_mode: Extended low-vol regimes where spread stays compressed for weeks (summer doldrums). IV estimation proxy may be noisy. Direction of expansion may oppose longer-term trend.
archived.diversification_value: Unique among vol bots — uses IV/RV spread compression rather than contraction breakout, skew, term structure, or momentum ride. Macro volatility timing complements intraday strategies.

archived.name: Regime_Fractal_Phase_Transition
archived.description: Detects regime shifts by tracking fractal dimension (Hurst exponent) in rolling windows. When fractal dimension crosses its 50-session moving average by more than 1 standard deviation, it signals a phase transition between trending (H<0.4), random (H~0.5), and mean-reverting (H>0.6) regimes. Each regime gets its own dedicated entry module.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute Hurst exponent over 120-period sliding window using R/S analysis on H1 close prices. 2. Smooth with 10-period EMA to get HS. 3. Compute rolling mean and stdev of HS over 50 periods. 4. If HS crosses above mean+1stdev → trending regime → enable momentum entries (pullback to 20-EMA on impulsive volume). 5. If HS crosses below mean-1stdev → mean-reverting regime → enable mean-reversion entries (RSI<30 bounce off Bollinger lower band). 6. If HS stays within ±0.5 stdev → random regime → no entries, wait.
archived.exit_logic: Trailing ATR-based stop (2.5×ATR) in trending regime. Fixed 1:2 R:R in mean-reverting regime. All positions closed immediately if HS flips to random regime mid-trade.
archived.failure_mode: Hurst exponent is noisy on short windows and laggy on long windows. Choppiness in H1 can produce 3-4 false transitions per month. Gold's occasional explosive vertical moves can flip the fractal regime mid-move, causing premature exits.
archived.diversification_value: Only existing regime filter (Hurst_Exponent_Regime_Detector) uses a single binary trending/mean-reverting classification. This introduces a three-state model (trending/random/mean-reverting) with separate entry modules per state and dynamic mid-trade regime monitoring — a fundamentally different approach to regime adaptation.

archived.name: Cross_Asset_Vanna_Flow_Proxy
archived.description: Uses SPX gamma positioning (absolute dealer gamma and zero-G levels) combined with US Treasury yield slope and DXY momentum as a multi-asset composite to predict directional XAUUSD flow. When SPX dealer gamma flips negative (dealers short gamma) AND yield curve steepens >2σ, gold tends to rally on vol-of-vol; the opposite configuration predicts gold selloffs.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Fetch SPX gamma exposure (zero-G level, dealer gamma in ) from end-of-day options data. 2. Calculate US10Y-2Y spread daily change and z-score over 60 days. 3. Calculate DXY 14-period RSI. 4. Entry signal = 1 if (dealer gamma < -Bn) AND (10Y-2Y z-score > 2.0) AND (DXY RSI < 40) → go long XAUUSD. 5. Entry signal = -1 if (dealer gamma < -Bn) AND (10Y-2Y z-score < -2.0) AND (DXY RSI > 60) → go short XAUUSD. 6. If dealer gamma is positive (dealers long gamma), skip — markets are structurally stable.
archived.exit_logic: Take profit at 2×ATR on H4. Stop at 1×ATR. Time-stop: exit on the 3rd daily close in signal direction to avoid stale positioning.
archived.failure_mode: SPX gamma data is not freely available in real-time — requires subscription or delayed daily data. Gamma flips are most predictive during options expiry weeks and lose signal mid-cycle. DXY regimes can overwhelm the composite during central-bank-intervention periods.
archived.diversification_value: Existing cross_asset ideas (DXY_Valence_Correlation, Real_Yield_Gold_Inverse_Corr, Gold_Silver_Ratio_Rotation) use two-asset pairs. This is the first three-asset composite (SPX gamma + yield curve + DXY) and the first to incorporate derivatives positioning data (dealer vanna/gamma). Adds a completely new data source class.

archived.name: Risk_Premium_Chase_Decay
archived.description: Models gold's equity-bond correlation regime (beta-to-risk) as a decaying signal for position sizing. When gold is positively correlated with equities (risk-on regime), trend-following bots get 1.5× base sizing and mean-reversion gets 0.5×. When gold is negatively correlated (safe-haven regime), the ratios flip. The correlation decays exponentially to neutral over 10 days of confirmed regime, forcing the system to harvest premium early and reduce size as the regime ages.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute 30-day rolling correlation of XAUUSD vs SPY daily returns (ρ_eq) and vs TLT daily returns (ρ_bond). 2. Classify regime: RiskOn = (ρ_eq > 0.3 AND ρ_bond < -0.2), SafeHaven = (ρ_eq < -0.3 AND ρ_bond > 0.2), Mixed = everything else. 3. On regime detection, calculate regime_age = days since classification (capped at 10). 4. Decay multiplier = exp(-0.15 × regime_age). 5. Apply size_multiplier = (base_multiplier - 1.0) × decay_multiplier + 1.0, where base_multiplier is 1.5 for the favored strategy class in the detected regime. 6. Recalculate every 3 days.
archived.exit_logic: No direct exits — this is a sizing overlay. It modulates the position sizes of sibling bots. Stop-losses are delegated to each instrument strategy. Overlay resets to 1.0× if the correlation regime flips or becomes ambiguous (mixed classification).
archived.failure_mode: Correlation regimes can flip intraday during news events, lagging the overlay 1-2 days. In Mixed regimes the overlay defaults to 1.0× which is optimal for no signal but misses regime edges. Exponential decay is arbitrary — a different decay curve may work better. Relies on sibling bots having properly set base stops.
archived.diversification_value: Existing risk_overlay ideas (Volatility_Parity_Scale, Slippage_Regime_Sizer, Optimal_F_Kelly_Sizer, Max_Drawdown_Lock_Protector) all size based on volatility, drawdowns, or win-rate metrics. This is the first correlation-regime-based sizing overlay and the first to use exponential decay to age-out premium signals. It also explicitly coordinates with sibling strategies by strategy class rather than acting independently.

archived.name: Asian_Session_Breakout_Continuation
archived.description: Trades the classic Asian-session range breakout at London open. Asian tight range (~00:00-07:00 GMT) sets clear high/low boundaries. London open often breaks this range with directional continuation for 1-3 hours when aligned with H4 trend. Uses retest confirmation and momentum velocity filter.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute Asian session high and low (00:00-07:00 GMT). 2. At London open (07:00-09:00 GMT), monitor for breakout beyond Asian range. 3. Confirm: (a) breakout candle closes beyond Asian Hi/Lo, (b) M15 ATR on breakout candle > 20-period avg (momentum filter), (c) direction aligns with H4 trend (above/below 200 EMA). 4. Enter on retest of breakout level OR 2nd consecutive candle beyond range (whichever comes first).
archived.exit_logic: SL: 1.5x Asian range width beyond breakout. TP1: 1x Asian range extension. TP2: 2x Asian range. Trail to breakeven after TP1 hit. Max hold 4 hours from London open; exit anything still open.
archived.failure_mode: Wide Asian ranges (>50% of prior day ATR) indicate indecision and produce fakeouts. News events near London open (08:30 GMT data prints) destabilise the pattern. Gaps from overnight news events make Asian range meaningless.
archived.diversification_value: Completely orthogonal to existing breakout ideas — no Asian-session pattern, no session-based breakout exists. Current 5 breakouts all use volume/volatility/structural levels during London/NY. This is pure session-range breakout trading, capturing a pattern uncorrelated to all existing strategies.

archived.name: Event_Volatility_Straddle_Reversal
archived.description: Trades scheduled high-impact events (FOMC, NFP, CPI, Core PCE, rate decisions). Deploys a straddle 30min pre-event to capture initial spike, then fades the spike with a reversal leg anticipating the typical 30-50% retrace within 1-2 hours post-release.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Identify next high-impact scheduled event (FOMC, NFP, CPI, Core PCE, BOE/ECB/BOJ rates). 2. 30min before event note current price P. 3. Place long-stop at P + (0.5 x M15 ATR14) and short-stop at P - (0.5 x M15 ATR14). 4. First triggered stop = entry. 5. If triggered, immediately place reversal order at P + (1.0 x ATR) from entry in opposite direction (catching the retrace). 6. If second stop of original straddle not triggered within 30min post-event, close original position and cancel reversal.
archived.exit_logic: Straddle legs: SL at 1.0x ATR from entry, TP at 2.0x ATR. Reversal leg: SL at spike extreme + 0.2 ATR, TP at 1.5x ATR from re-entry. Max 2 trades per event. Total event risk capped at 2% account. Hard stop: exit everything 3 hours post-event.
archived.failure_mode: Extreme events where market gaps through both stops in seconds (surprise rate cuts, unexpected NFP print). Paradigm-shifting data where initial move continues as strong trend with no retrace. Spread/commission costs eat small-ATR moves. Non-standard event timing.
archived.diversification_value: Unique in the volatility family — all 5 existing volatility ideas are technical (contraction/expansion, skew, term structure, momentum, spread). None trade scheduled events. This is pure event-driven volatility with a systematic reversal expectation, making it wholly uncorrelated.

archived.name: DXY_Deviation_Regime_Scalp
archived.description: Short-term intraday divergence scalp exploiting the XAUUSD-DXY inverse correlation (-0.7 to -0.85). When gold makes a counter-trend price move against the DXY direction (positive or negative divergence), the deviation typically resolves within 2-4 hours. Uses z-score of 60-min return correlation to identify statistically significant divergences.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate z-score of XAUUSD/DXY 60-min return correlation over last 40 periods. 2. DXY makes new 4h high while gold flat or ALSO making new 4h high = positive divergence (bearish for gold) → SHORT gold. 3. DXY makes new 4h low while gold flat or ALSO making new 4h low = negative divergence (bullish for gold) → LONG gold. 4. Filter: z-score of divergence > 1.5 (statistically significant). 5. Trade only during London/NY overlap (12:00-16:00 GMT) for liquidity.
archived.exit_logic: SL: 1.0x H1 ATR14 from entry. TP: 1.5x H1 ATR from entry OR when divergence z-score drops below 0.5 (convergence), whichever comes first. Max hold 4 hours; force-exit anything still open.
archived.failure_mode: Gold-DXY correlation breakdowns (QE, fiscal dominance, risk-off flows where both sell). News-event divergences that persist meaningfully. Low-liquidity session noise divergences. Regime changes (e.g. 2008, 2020) where correlation flips.
archived.diversification_value: Entirely different from existing cross-asset ideas — all 5 current ideas are macro/fundamental multi-day (DXY valence, gold-silver ratio, real yields, gamma, vanna). This is the only short-term intraday intermarket-statistical divergence scalp, exploiting the XAUUSD-DXY pair itself at sub-day horizons.

archived.name: YieldCurve_Regime_Switch
archived.description: Uses the US Treasury yield curve slope (2s10s spread) and its rate of change to classify gold into four macro regimes: (1) Inverted/Deepening — recession fear, bullish gold as safe haven; (2) Steepening from Inversion — reflation trade, bullish gold as inflation hedge; (3) Normal Steepening — growth positive, gold range-bound as risk appetite dominates; (4) Flattening from Normal — tightening expectations, bearish gold as real rates rise. Each regime triggers a distinct trading bias and position sizing multiplier.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Calculate daily 2s10s spread = US10Y yield - US02Y yield. 2) Calculate 20-day slope of the spread (linear regression). 3) Classify regime: (a) Spread < -0.20 AND slope negative → REGIME_1 (Deep Inversion) → long bias, 1.5x size; (b) Spread < -0.20 AND slope positive → REGIME_2 (Steepening from Inversion) → long bias, 1.0x size; (c) Spread between -0.20 and +0.50 AND slope positive → REGIME_3 (Normal Expansion) → neutral/sideways, 0.5x size or flat; (d) Spread > +0.50 AND slope negative → REGIME_4 (Tightening Flattening) → short bias, 1.0x size. 4) On D1, if regime is 1 or 2, enter long on a pullback to the 20 EMA with DXY also declining (DXY < 20 SMA). If regime is 4, enter short on a rally to 20 EMA with DXY rising.
archived.exit_logic: Take profit: 2:1 risk-reward on D1 ATR-based targets. Stop loss: 1.5x D1 ATR. No trailing stop — let macro regimes play out. Exit immediately if regime classification changes (e.g., spread flips from -0.15 to -0.05 after being in regime 1). Max holding: 20 bars on D1. Regime overlay also scales position: 1.5x in strong directional regimes, 0.5x in neutral regimes, flat in regime 3.
archived.failure_mode: Central bank intervention (yield curve control, QE) can distort the 2s10s spread signal. During 2020-2021, massive Fed buying flattened the curve artificially, generating false regime signals. Also, gold can sell off during inversion periods if a liquidity crisis forces margin calls (e.g., March 2020). Regime transitions lag price action by days.
archived.diversification_value: No existing bot uses the yield curve as its primary macro regime classifier. All current regime_filter ideas (ATR, Volatility Cluster, Hurst, Fractal Phase, Macro Regime Shifter) use price/volatility internals. This brings genuine macro input from the bond market, orthogonal to price action. Excellent hedge against pure technical strategies.

archived.name: Gold_Oil_Ratio_Extreme_Reverter
archived.description: The Gold-to-Oil ratio (XAUUSD price divided by Brent/CL price) has historically mean-reverted around a long-term equilibrium of ~15-20 barrels of oil per ounce of gold. At extremes — ratio above 25 (gold expensive, oil cheap) or below 10 (gold cheap, oil expensive) — the ratio tends to revert as either gold corrects, oil catches up, or both. The trade is a pure mean reversion bet on the ratio itself, not directional gold or oil. This captures a classic inter-commodity equilibrium dynamic that macro hedge funds have traded for decades.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Calculate Gold-Oil Ratio = XAUUSD price / USOIL price (daily close). 2) Compute 200-day z-score of the ratio. 3) Entry conditions: (a) z-score > +2.0 (ratio extremely high) -> SHORT gold / LONG oil (via pairs sizing). For forex-only implementation: enter SHORT XAUUSD only when ratio > 2.0 z-score AND oil is in a confirmed uptrend (USOIL > 50 SMA on D1). (b) z-score < -2.0 (ratio extremely low) -> LONG XAUUSD only when ratio < -2.0 z-score AND oil is in a confirmed downtrend (USOIL < 50 SMA on D1). 4) Confirm with D1 RSI(14) divergence on gold. 5) Enter at market open after the daily close that triggers the signal.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 2x D1 ATR of XAUUSD. Take profit 1: 50% position at z-score returns to 0 (ratio equilibrium). Take profit 2: 50% position at z-score reaches -1.0 (for short) or +1.0 (for long). Maximum hold: 60 calendar days. If z-score exceeds +3.0 or -3.0 while in trade, tighten stop to breakeven. Exit immediately if the ratio regime changes structurally.
archived.failure_mode: Structural shifts in the gold-oil equilibrium. The 2020 oil crash pushed the ratio to 100+, but the equilibrium had fundamentally changed due to the shale revolution. Central bank gold buying (2022+) and green energy oil demand shifts can create new equilibria. A 200-day z-score assumes stationarity that may not hold. Also, USOIL CFD pricing differs from physical oil benchmarks during contango/backwardation extremes.
archived.diversification_value: No existing strategy in the archive uses a pure inter-commodity ratio mean reversion. This is distinctly different from the Gold-Silver ratio (precious metals only) and from all other mean reversion ideas that are purely price/volume-based on gold alone. It taps into a macro factor (energy vs precious metals) entirely absent from the archive. Long holding period (weeks-months) diversifies against all intraday/scalp strategies.

archived.name: Vanna_Flow_Momentum_Capture
archived.description: Uses proxy indicators of dealer gamma/vanna hedging flows to capture short-term momentum bursts in gold. When gold is near a large option strike concentration (e.g., major round numbers 1900, 2000, 2100) and implied volatility is elevated, dealers delta-hedge gamma exposure, creating self-reinforcing momentum. The strategy identifies these "magnet" levels from option open interest data and enters momentum trades as price approaches and breaches them, riding the dealer hedging cascade.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Track weekly XAUUSD option chain data for high open-interest strike levels (top 5 strikes by OI). These are dealer gamma concentration zones. 2) When price is within 0.5% of a high-OI strike AND IV is above its 20-day median (indicating dealers are actively hedging), prepare for entry. 3) LONG entry: price breaks above the high-OI strike by 0.15% with a bullish engulfing or strong (volume > 20 SMA) M15 candle. SHORT entry: price breaks below the high-OI strike by 0.15% with a bearish engulfing or strong bearish M15 candle. 4) Confirm with H1 RSI > 55 (long) or < 45 (short) to avoid fading the dominant trend. 5) Enter immediately on candle close of the confirmation bar.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 0.5x H1 ATR below/above entry (tight — this is a momentum capture, not a swing trade). Take profit 1: next option strike level (next high-OI zone). Take profit 2: trail by 1x H1 ATR once +1x ATR in profit. Maximum hold: 24 bars on M15 (6 hours). If price stalls within 0.5 ATR of entry after 3 bars, exit for a small loss/small gain — the momentum cascade should fire immediately or it is not happening.
archived.failure_mode: Option OI data is often delayed or unavailable for XAUUSD OTC/spot — depends on broker feed quality. Dealers have changed hedging behavior post-2020 with increased retail options flow. During low-IV environments, hedging flows are minimal and the "magnet" effect is negligible. Also, large macro events (NFP, FOMC, CPI) can overwhelm dealer hedging flows entirely, causing violent breaks through gamma levels.
archived.diversification_value: This is the first strategy in the archive to explicitly model dealer hedging flows as a momentum source. All existing momentum ideas use price/volume/ADX/MSS patterns. This introduces a derivatives-market microstructure angle entirely absent from the current set. Its tight stops and short holding period make it a good complement to the longer-term macro and seasonal strategies. Captures a different category of momentum — flow-driven, not trend-driven.

archived.name: Correlation_Collapse_Protector
archived.description: A risk overlay that monitors rolling correlations between XAUUSD and its three most influential cross-asset peers -- DXY (USD Index), US10Y (10-year Treasury yield), and USDJPY -- and dynamically reduces position size when historical correlation structures break down. When Gold decouples from its normal relationship with the dollar or yields (e.g., gold rallies with a rising dollar, or falls with falling yields), it signals that the fundamental regime has shifted, making risk models unreliable. The overlay caps total exposure at 50% of normal during such regimes and requires a correlation re-convergence signal to reinstate full sizing.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold normally exhibits strong negative correlation with DXY (-0.6 to -0.8) and US10Y real yields, and positive correlation with USDJPY in risk-on environments. These relationships are not constant -- they tighten during trend regimes and fray during shock events (rate surprises, geopolitical flashpoints, liquidity crises). When correlations collapse, standard volatility-based risk models (which assume stable relationships) fail catastrophically because portfolio hedges stop working simultaneously. The market enters a regime of higher tail dependency -- all assets move together in unexpected ways -- precisely when risk models need to be most conservative. This overlay anticipates that breakdown rather than reacting after a drawdown.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute rolling 30-day Pearson correlation of XAUUSD vs DXY, US10Y yield, and USDJPY on H1 data. 2. Compute the 90-day standard deviation of each correlation (the volatility of correlation). 3. Calculate a Correlation Stability Score (CSS) = 1 - (sum of z-scores of the three correlations deviation from their 90-day mean) / 3. 4. Normal range (full exposure): CSS > -1.0. 5. Caution zone (50% exposure): CSS between -1.0 and -2.0. 6. Lockdown zone (25% exposure or no new entries): CSS < -2.0. 7. Recovery: Full sizing resumes only when CSS returns above -0.5 for 3 consecutive days (hysteresis band). Overlay applies at portfolio level, not per-trade.
archived.exit_logic: No per-trade exit -- this is a portfolio-level risk overlay. When CSS enters caution zone, any open positions have their trailing stops tightened to 0.5x normal ATR. When CSS enters lockdown zone, all open positions are reduced by 50% (partial close) and no new entries permitted. Recovery to normal sizing triggers position re-entry only if original entry signal is still valid. Hard override: if any single asset shows a 10-day correlation flip (e.g., DXY correlation from -0.7 to +0.3), immediately enter lockdown regardless of CSS score.
archived.failure_mode: Fails during structurally persistent regime shifts where a new normal correlation takes hold (e.g., the 2022 gold-DXY regime where both rallied together for months) -- the overlay would remain in lockdown indefinitely, starving the portfolio of exposure during a profitable regime. The 90-day lookback window causes slow adaptation. Correlations are fragile estimators: 30-day Pearson can be distorted by a single outlier day. Also fails in zero-correlation environments where the CSS is persistently in caution zone due to noise, not real regime change.
archived.diversification_value: The only overlay in the archive that monitors correlation stability rather than volatility. While Volatility_Parity_Scale adjusts to volatility level, this adjusts to correlation regime -- they are orthogonal risk dimensions. Fills a critical gap: prevents the portfolio from being overexposed precisely when diversification fails (the moment you need protection most). Cannot be replicated by any existing strategy since no current bot monitors cross-asset correlation structures at the portfolio level.

archived.name: Event_Window_Seasonal_Compression
archived.description: Combines seasonal patterns with macro event windows (FOMC, NFP, CPI, ECB, BOJ rate decisions) to exploit the tendency of Gold to compress its seasonal drift into a narrower window around high-impact events. Rather than holding a seasonal position for weeks, this strategy enters 12 hours before a macro event during seasonally favorable months and exits 24 hours after -- capturing the bulk of seasonal movement while avoiding the noise of non-event days. The hypothesis is that large institutional seasonal flows (hedging, central bank rebalancing, physical settlement) are accelerated through event-driven liquidity pools.
archived.market_behaviour: Gold seasonal patterns (Indian wedding demand Oct-Dec, Chinese New Year Jan-Feb, summer lull May-Jul) are well-documented but diffuse -- the total return over a seasonal window is small (1-3%) spread over weeks. However, macro events create liquidity concentration: large orders that would normally dribble in over days are compressed into the hours around FOMC/NFP when depth is highest. The seasonal signal is strongest not on random Tuesdays in November, but in the 36-hour window around high-impact macro events during seasonally favorable periods. The drift provides the directional bias, the event provides the catalyst.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Maintain seasonal calendar: Long-favorable windows (Aug 1 - Sep 15, Oct 15 - Feb 15), Short-favorable windows (Mar 1 - May 1, Jun 15 - Jul 15). 2. Cross-reference with macro event calendar: FOMC (8/year), NFP (12/year), CPI (12/year), ECB rate (8/year), BOJ rate (8/year). 3. Entry condition: A macro event must fall within a seasonally favorable window. 4. Entry timing: 12 hours before the event (e.g., entry Tue 08:00 ET for FOMC Wed 14:00 ET). Direction = seasonal window direction. 5. Position size = 1.5x normal (compressed timeframe justifies higher conviction). 6. Skip if: the event is within 5 days of another same-type event (cluster risk), or if the seasonal window has less than 5 days remaining (insufficient runway).
archived.exit_logic: Primary exit: 24 hours after the event release (captures the post-event continuation drift). Time-stop: exit at Friday 17:00 ET regardless. Hard stop: if the event triggers a >2% daily move against position, exit immediately (event-driven trend rejection). SL: 1.5x ATR(14) on H4 from entry. No TP -- exit is purely time-based. If the same seasonal window contains multiple events, treat each independently: exit position A before entering position B.
archived.failure_mode: Fails when macro events override seasonal patterns entirely (e.g., a hawkish FOMC surprise during the Nov-Feb seasonal rally, or an emergency rate cut during the Apr short window). Event outcomes are binary and fat-tailed -- a single NFP miss can undo months of seasonal drift. Low trade count (only 15-20 events per year fall in seasonal windows). Backtesting requires 10+ years of event timestamps and exact timestamp entry (not OHLC only). Seasonality itself can break in structurally new macro regimes (COVID, 2008).
archived.diversification_value: None of the 5 existing seasonal strategies use macro event windows as the execution catalyst -- they all hold through full calendar windows. This is the first hybrid seasonal+event strategy in the archive. It operates on a fundamentally different timescale (36-hour holds vs. multi-week holds) making it uncorrelated with Gold_Seasonal_Cycle or Turn_Of_Month_Gold. It bridges the gap between seasonal and regime_filter families, a combinatorial space the archive has never explored.

archived.name: Structural_Break_Momentum_Flux
archived.description: Detects structural market breaks using a novel Momentum Flux Index -- the cumulative divergence between price rate-of-change and volume-weighted velocity -- then trades the re-convergence pattern. Unlike standard momentum (which buys strength) or mean-reversion (which fades extremes), this strategy identifies moments when momentum has exhausted its statistical energy but price has not yet reversed, creating a high-probability zone where the direction is about to change. It sits in the uncorrelated middle ground between momentum and mean-reversion -- it neither chases trends nor fades them, but catches the exact inflection.
archived.market_behaviour: Markets transition through distinct phases: accumulation (low energy building), trend (high energy directional), climax (peak energy + exhaustion), and reversion (energy dissipating). Standard momentum strategies buy during trend and fail at climax; mean-reversion strategies buy at climax and succeed at reversion. But both miss the critical edge: the moment between climax and the first bar of reversion. During this flux state, price is range-bound but compressed volatility is about to expand in the opposite direction. Momentum flux (rate of change of momentum, akin to second derivative of price) peaks 1-3 bars before price reverses, providing a leading indicator that neither momentum nor reversion alone can see.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute Momentum Flux Index (MFI): apply a rolling linear regression slope to ATR(14) over 20 bars, then divide by the standard deviation of slope (z-score of ATR acceleration). 2. Compute Price Velocity Divergence (PVD): the angle difference between price ROC(14) and a weighted mid-price (H+L/2) ROC(14). 3. Entry conditions for LONG: (a) MFI z-score > +2.5 AND (b) PVD > +1.5 AND (c) price closed in bottom 30% of the last 5 bars AND (d) RSI(14) > 70. 4. Entry conditions for SHORT: inverse -- MFI z-score < -2.5, PVD < -1.5, price in top 30% of 5 bars, RSI < 30. 5. Entry at next H4 open after all conditions met.
archived.exit_logic: SL: 1.0x ATR(14) on H4 from entry (tight because entry is at the peak of acceleration -- if wrong, price is still accelerating, so a small stop is essential). TP1: 50% at 1x ATR(14) on H4 (scalp the initial reversion). TP2: 30% at 2x ATR(14) on H4 (reversion continuation). Remainder: trail at 0.5x ATR(14) when price reaches 1x ATR profit. Max hold: 5 days. The tight 1x ATR stop is non-negotiable -- this strategy lives and dies on catching the exact inflection, and wrong entries must be cut ruthlessly.
archived.failure_mode: The tight 1x ATR SL causes high strike-rate on non-climax bars (false positives where momentum briefly shows flux but resumes). In strong, uninterrupted trends (e.g., war breakout, rate-cut cycle), the flux signal can fire multiple times and get stopped out each time -- bleeding small losses. Requires tick-level or intra-bar data to compute precise mid-price and acceleration -- standard H4 OHLC may lose signal fidelity. The z-score approach makes it regime-dependent: after a quiet period, even moderate momentum looks extreme.
archived.diversification_value: Conceptually novel -- not momentum, not mean-reversion, but a pure inflection-capture strategy that exploits the second derivative of price. No existing idea in any family uses acceleration z-scores or mid-price velocity divergence. This occupies a unique niche: it would fire at exactly the worst possible entry for both momentum bots (which buy climax) and mean-reversion bots (which require clear reversal bars first). It captures edges that both other families miss because they look at different features (level vs. reversal vs. acceleration). Fills a genuine algorithmic gap.

archived.name: OrderBlock_Fractal_Breakout
archived.description: Combines unmitigated Higher-Timeframe Order Blocks (SMC/ICT) with Williams Fractal confirmation on H1 for high-probability breakouts. Price touching an unmitigated OB on H4 with a completed fractal on H1 signals a directional breakout with a defined invalidation level.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Identify unmitigated buy/sell order blocks on H4 (last 5-7 candles before a strong move). 2) Switch to H1 and wait for price to retrace into the OB zone. 3) Confirm with a completed Williams Fractal (5-candle pattern: middle candle highest/lowest). 4) For a bullish setup: price touches H4 buy OB + bullish fractal forms at OB edge. 5) Enter on break of fractal high/low with 1 ATR stop buffer.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1 ATR below/above the order block edge. Take profit 1: 2x ATR from entry (50% position). Take profit 2: trail remaining position at 2.5 ATR with H1 fractal flip. If price rejects OB without forming a fractal, abort trade completely.
archived.failure_mode: Order blocks lose significance in strong trend when institutional orders are swept aggressively. Also fails in ranging markets where OBs form on both sides simultaneously — fractal signals become noise.
archived.diversification_value: Existing breakout bots use standard S/R, volume profile, Bollinger Bands, or session-specific timing. This is the first to codify Smart Money Concepts (order blocks + fractal confirmation) into a systematic algo rule set, capturing institutional-level orderflow.

archived.name: CRB_Gold_Momentum_Spread
archived.description: Exploits the intermarket rotation between broad commodity indices (CRB) and Gold. When CRB rallies but Gold lags, Gold tends to catch up (safe-haven + inflation hedge demand). When Gold rallies while CRB flat/declining, Gold is overextended relative to the commodity complex. Uses 20-day rate-of-change divergence as the trigger.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Compute 20-day ROC of CRB Index and XAUUSD daily close. 2) Compute spread = ROC_CRB - ROC_GOLD. 3) BUY signal: spread > +8% (CRB outrunning Gold by 8% in 20 days) AND Gold ROC < 5% (lagging). 4) SELL signal: spread < -8% (CRB lagging Gold by 8%) AND Gold ROC > 10% (overextended). 5) Only trade when Gold ATR(14) > 0.8% of price (liquid enough). 6) Additional filter: Gold must be within 1.5 ATR of its 50-day MA (not disconnected from trend).
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 2 ATR(14) from entry. Take profit: when spread compresses to within ±2% (convergence). Hard time stop: 21 trading days. If a major macro event (FOMC, NFP) occurs during the trade, move to breakeven immediately.
archived.failure_mode: During risk-off regimes (2008, 2020), correlations break — everything sells off together regardless of relative momentum. Also fails when Gold is driven by unique factors (central bank buying, geopolitical premium) disconnected from commodity cycles.
archived.diversification_value: No existing bot in the archive uses the broad commodity index (CRB) as a relative momentum signal for Gold. Existing cross-asset bots focus on DXY, yields, silver, and options flow — this adds a genuine macro rotation dimension.

archived.name: Holiday_Liquidity_Vacuum_Rebound
archived.description: Capitalizes on the mechanical microstructure of low-liquidity holiday periods (Christmas, New Year, Thanksgiving week, Easter Friday, US Independence Day, Labor Day) where orderbook depth drops 60-80%. Small institutional flows produce outsized price moves that revert sharply 1-3 sessions post-holiday when liquidity returns. This is a pure structural scalp.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Pre-define holiday windows: 2 sessions before and 1 session after major US/EU holidays (Christmas, New Year, Thanksgiving, Good Friday, July 4, Labor Day, Memorial Day). 2) During holiday window, measure intraday range expansion: if price moves > 1.8x the 10-day average H1 range within a single session, flag as overshoot. 3) Entry: wait for first 15-min candle post-range-expansion that shows wick > 60% of candle body in opposite direction — this is the first sign of liquidity returning. 4) Enter 50% at candle close, 50% on a second confirmation 30 min later. 5) Pre-holiday drift (directional moves entering the holiday) invalidates the setup — only trade range-expansion, not drift.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: entire move retraced (liquidity has fully returned but against you). Take profit 1: 50% of the holiday-range-expansion distance (target the midpoint). Take profit 2: 100% of the holiday-range-expansion distance. Hard exit: end of the first full post-holiday trading session (NY close). Stops trail behind H1 20-EMA after TP1 is hit.
archived.failure_mode: Major macro news during holiday periods (surprise rate decision, geopolitical event) overwhelms microstructure effects. Also fails when multiple holidays overlap (US+EU), as liquidity vanishes entirely for days and no snap-back catalyst exists. Works worst in August (European summer lull is weeks, not days — different regime).
archived.diversification_value: Existing seasonal bots cover monthly turn, quarterly roll, lunar cycles, and event-window compression — none address the specific microstructure vacuum of short holiday periods. This is pure market mechanics (liquidity-dependent price discovery) rather than calendar-based return expectancy.

archived.name: Donchian_Breakout_Momentum_Acceleration
archived.description: Donchian channel breakout filtered by rate-of-change acceleration. Enters on 20-period Donchian breakout only when the 5-period ROC is rising (acceleration) and above its own 14-period SMA, confirming genuine momentum thrust rather than fake breakouts.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate Donchian(20) — upper and lower bands. 2. Price closes above upper Donchian band. 3. ROC(5) > ROC(5) 14-period SMA (i.e., momentum is accelerating, not just level-breaking). 4. ROC(5) is positive. 5. Enter long at market open of next candle. 6. For shorts: price closes below lower band, ROC(5) < 0 and below its SMA (decelerating downside).
archived.exit_logic: Hard SL at 1.5x ATR(14) below entry. TP1 at 2x ATR, TP2 at 3.5x ATR with 50% position each. Trailing stop activates after TP1 hit — trail at 1x ATR. Max hold 20 candles; if neither TP hit, exit at close.
archived.failure_mode: Chopping markets with false Donchian breaks where ROC oscillates erratically. Also fails in strong trend reversals where acceleration plateaus then reverses violently — the SL gets taken before the trailing logic engages.
archived.diversification_value: Existing momentum bots use ADX confluence or volume — this adds rate-of-change acceleration as a higher-frequency momentum filter. It catches breakouts earlier than ADX-based systems and avoids the lag of moving-average crossovers.

archived.name: RSI_Stochastic_Divergence_Reversal
archived.description: Contrarian reversal entries triggered by concurrent RSI and stochastic divergence at key support/resistance zones on lower timeframes. Designed for mean-reversion scalps in ranging conditions.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Identify a swing high (for shorts) or swing low (for longs) on M30 using fractals. 2. Check RSI(14) — price makes higher high but RSI makes lower high (bearish divergence) OR price makes lower low but RSI makes higher low (bullish divergence). 3. Check Stochastic(5,3,3) — must confirm divergence within 1 bar of RSI signal. 4. Price must be within 5 pips of a horizontal S/R level or Fibonacci 0.618-0.786 zone. 5. Enter at market with 10-pip invalidation if price reverses past the divergence pivot.
archived.exit_logic: Fixed TP at 1.2x ATR(14). SL at 1.2x ATR. If price reaches 50% of TP in under 3 candles, trail stop to breakeven. Max hold 12 candles.
archived.failure_mode: Strong trending markets break divergence repeatedly — each divergence triggers a loss as the trend powers through. Divergence on lower timeframes (M15) is notoriously noisy with false signals.
archived.diversification_value: Existing mean-reversion bots use wicks, VWAP, or volume profile. This adds multi-indicator divergence confirmation with an S/R filter, reducing false signals compared to single-indicator divergence strategies.

archived.name: VaR_Trailing_Stop_Overlay
archived.description: Dynamic position-sizing and trailing-stop overlay that adjusts trade parameters based on real-time Value-at-Risk (VaR) estimation at the 95th and 99th percentiles. Designed to plug into any existing directional strategy to replace static SL/TP with volatility-adaptive exits.
archived.entry_logic: Does NOT generate entries — this is an overlay for existing strategies. It takes entry signals from a parent signal feeder (configurable: any existing bot) and calculates: 1. VaR(95) using historical simulation over the last 100 candles. 2. VaR(99) using the same window. 3. Position size = (account_risk / VaR(99)) * correlation_factor — caps single-trade risk at 1% of account. 4. Initial SL = 1.5x VaR(95). 5. Stop is recalculated every 6 candles: if VaR shrinks (volatility declining), trail stop tighter; if VaR expands, widen stop proportionally.
archived.exit_logic: Primary exit: trailing VaR-based stop (1.5x VaR(95) recalculated every 6 candles). Secondary exit: if VaR(99) exceeds 2x entry VaR(99) (volatility explosion), exit immediately at market — protective stop-out regardless of P&L. TP not used; positions ride until stopped or volatility-expelled.
archived.failure_mode: VaR fails spectacularly during black-swan events (gap moves, flash crashes) where historical simulation underestimates tail risk. The 2x VaR(99) volatility-explosion exit itself becomes a loss lock-in mechanism if volatility spikes are mean-reverting rather than persistent.
archived.diversification_value: All existing risk_overlay ideas (Kelly, Vol Parity, Max Drawdown Lock, Correlation Collapse) are static-parameter or parameterized-by-regime overlays. This is the only one that uses real-time VaR estimation to adapt both position size AND stop distance dynamically. Also unique: it self-ejects on volatility explosions rather than holding through them.

archived.name: Volatility_Risk_Premium_Decay
archived.description: Captures the volatility risk premium decay (implied vol minus realized vol compressing) during session transitions on XAUUSD. The premium is widest at Asian open and decays as liquidity returns in London.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate 20-period HV vs ATR-normalized IV proxy. 2. Entry when IV-HV spread > 1.5 std devs above 50-period mean AND within 30min of London open. 3. Confirm ADX < 25. 4. Short the spread - enter at current bid.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x ATR. Take profit: spread compresses to 20-period mean. Trail at 0.5x ATR after 1x ATR profit. Max hold: 8 hours.
archived.failure_mode: Sustained news-driven volatility widens the spread instead of compressing. Crushed in vol expansion regimes.
archived.diversification_value: All existing vol ideas trade price direction or straddles. This is a vol-of-vol premium decay trade, zero-beta to trend and breakout strategies.

archived.name: Intermarket_Vol_Regime_Breakdown
archived.description: Uses rolling correlation of vol across gold, bonds (TNX ATR), and dollar (DXY ATR) to detect regime shifts. Correlation breakdown signals regime change and switches between momentum and mean-reversion modes.
archived.entry_logic: 1. 40-period rolling Pearson correlation of daily ATR changes across XAUUSD/TNX/DXY. 2. Correlation>0.6=synchronized (momentum mode). Correlation<0.3=fragmented (mean-reversion mode). 3. On breakdown signal (crossing 0.6 to 0.3): fade last 10-period move if trending, or breakout if ranging.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 2x ATR. Take profit: 3x ATR. Mode persists until correlation re-enters synchronized zone or 15 bars. Trail 1x ATR after 1.5x ATR profit.
archived.failure_mode: Central bank intervention causes false 1-2 bar correlation breakdowns. 40-period window too slow to filter micro-breakdowns.
archived.diversification_value: Only regime filter spanning three asset classes (gold, bonds, dollar). Complements all single-asset filters.

archived.name: Gap_Exhaustion_Fade_Reverter
archived.description: Fades large XAUUSD gaps (>2 sigma of 20-day avg) at open. Statistical edge: 68% probability of 50%+ retracement within 4 hours as algos fade the emotional open.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Gap = abs(open-prev_close)/(20-period ATR). 2. Trigger when gap > 2.0 std devs above 20-day mean. 3. Fade direction: short if gap up, long if gap down. 4. Reject within 60min of high-impact news. 5. Reject if tick volume below 20-period median.
archived.exit_logic: Stop: 0.8x ATR. Target: 50% gap retracement. Time stop: 4 hours. Trail to breakeven at 40% retracement.
archived.failure_mode: Breakaway gaps from fundamental regime changes (rate decisions, geopolitical surprises) do not retrace. News filter catches scheduled events but not surprise shocks.
archived.diversification_value: No existing idea targets gap exhaustion specifically. Unique behavioral edge on emotional opens with defined expiry.

archived.name: Gld_Put_Call_Skew_Reversal
archived.description: Detects excessive bearish hedging in gold options via put/call implied volatility skew. When OTM put IV exceeds OTM call IV by >25% on a normalized 5-day basis, it signals crowded bearish positioning that historically precedes short-covering rallies in spot gold within 1-3 days.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Calculate rolling 5-day normalized put/call IV skew for GLD options (proxying spot gold). 2. Compute Z-score of skew relative to 60-day mean. 3. When skew Z-score > +2.0 (puts excessively expensive vs calls) AND XAUUSD is at a 5-day low, enter long. 4. Filter: only trade if ADX(14) < 25 (non-trending environment prevents trend-caused skew persistence). 5. Entry at market open of next H4 candle after signal.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x ATR(14) below entry. Take profit: 2.5x ATR(14) or when skew Z-score drops below +0.5 (skew mean-reverted). Trailing stop activates at 1x ATR profit. Max hold: 5 H4 bars. If no target hit, exit at close.
archived.failure_mode: Sustained bear trends where elevated put skew is rational (not excessive) — options market prices in real downside risk. This kills the reversal edge and produces persistent losses. Also fails during extreme macro shocks where skew stays elevated for weeks.
archived.diversification_value: Only strategy in archive using options market pricing data (implied volatility skew). Completely uncorrelated with price-action, volume, or momentum signals. Provides a contrarian volatility edge when most strategies are directionally biased.

archived.name: Central_Bank_Reserve_Trend_Flow
archived.description: Uses monthly central bank gold reserve data (aggregate net purchases from World Gold Council / IMF IFS) as a fundamental regime filter. When top-10 central banks collectively accumulate >50 tonnes net over 2 consecutive months, gold enters a structural-demand regime where every pullback is a buy opportunity and trend-following gets reinforced.
archived.entry_logic: 1. On 1st of each month, load latest central bank net purchase figure (tonnes, 2-month rolling sum). 2. If rolling sum > +50 tonnes: enable structural-bid regime. 3. In structural-bid regime: enter long on any D1 close above 20-day SMA with RSI(14) between 40-60 (pullback entry, not chase). 4. Exit structural-bid mode when rolling 2-month net purchases drop below +20 tonnes. 5. Position size: 1.5x base in structural-bid regime, 0.5x in neutral/zero.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 3x ATR(14) at D1 level (wide — fundamental regime allows noise). Take profit: trail at 20-day SMA after 2x ATR profit. Flat when regime exits structural-bid mode. Max 4 simultaneous positions (each on different pullback legs).
archived.failure_mode: Central bank data is monthly and revised retroactively. Initial release figures can be significantly revised (sometimes 30-50% off). Also: major central banks (Fed, ECB) do not buy gold, only emerging-market CBs drive this — if they pause buying simultaneously, the regime signal vanishes but gold may still trend on other drivers.
archived.diversification_value: Only strategy in archive using fundamental macro data (central bank balance sheets) rather than price/volume/volatility inputs. Provides an independent structural-demand read that persists for weeks-months. Non-correlated with intraday or technical strategies.

archived.name: Gold_Mining_Equity_Leading_Index
archived.description: Exploits the leading-indicator relationship between gold mining equities (GDX ETF) and physical gold (XAUUSD). Gold miners typically lead spot gold by 1-3 days due to lower liquidity, higher beta to gold price changes, and institutional rotation patterns. When GDX breaks out while XAUUSD consolidates, it signals imminent gold movement in the same direction.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Track daily GDX price vs XAUUSD. 2. Detect breakout signal: GDX closes above its 20-day Donchian channel high while XAUUSD has moved less than 0.5x ATR(14) in the last 3 days (consolidating). 3. Enter long XAUUSD at next D1 open if GDX leads up. Short if GDX breaks Donchian low while XAUUSD consolidates. 4. Filter: only trade if GDX-XAUUSD 5-day rolling correlation is >0.6 (relationship intact). 5. Confirm with GDX volume > 1.5x 20-day average.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 2x ATR(14) at D1 level below/above entry. Take profit: 3x ATR(14) or when XAUUSD has caught up (GDX-XAUUSD ratio mean-reverts). Time exit: if XAUUSD hasn't moved within 5 days despite GDX signal, exit at market. Trailing stop after 1.5x ATR profit.
archived.failure_mode: Correlation breakdown periods — during gold market dislocations (flash crashes, liquidity events) miners can diverge from spot gold for weeks. Also fails when miners are driven by equity-market-wide factors (risk-on/risk-off rotation) rather than gold fundamentals. GDX options expiration week can introduce noise.
archived.diversification_value: Only strategy in archive using equities as a leading indicator for a commodity. Uses intermarket lead-lag structure rather than direct price action. Partially correlated with momentum strategies during steady trends but provides early-entry advantage that momentum strategies miss.

archived.name: Liquidity_Void_Breakout_Trap
archived.description: Uses Volume Profile to identify low-volume nodes (liquidity voids) between structure levels. When price breaks a swing high/low into a void zone, retail sees a breakout. Instead of chasing, wait for a retracement back into the void. If the void holds as support/resistance and price breaks the initial level again, this is an institutional liquidity grab - trade the real directional move. Filters out 60%+ of false breakouts.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Identify nearest swing high/low on H1. 2. Overlay Volume Profile (2-week lookback). 3. Locate the low-volume node (LVN) between current price and the swing level. 4. Wait for price to break the swing level but then IMMEDIATELY retrace back into the LVN within 3 bars. 5. On the second attempt to break the swing level, enter long on a 1-bar close above the swing high (or short below swing low). 6. Require H1 candle close confirming direction before entry.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1 ATR below the LVN midpoint (long) or above (short). Take profit 1: 1.5x ATR from entry. Take profit 2: 3x ATR from entry. Trail remaining position at 1 ATR using chandelier exit. Max hold: 24 bars on M15. If not triggered, manual close.
archived.failure_mode: Strong trend days where price never retraces into the void zone - the breakout runs away and the trap never triggers. Also fails in low-volatility range markets where no clear LVN forms. Worst in choppy news-driven sessions where multiple LVNs overlap.
archived.diversification_value: Entirely different from existing breakout bots (Bollinger Squeeze, London Killzone, Asian Session, OrderBlock, Volume Profile Acceptance). This is the only strategy that waits for a FALSE breakout before trading the REAL one - it is a trap fade turned continuation rather than a standard breakout.

archived.name: MultiDecile_Momentum_Ensemble
archived.description: Score each bar across 10 individual momentum signals and normalize each to a 0-100 decile. Only trade when the ensemble score crosses above 70 (long) or below 30 (short) with at least 6 of 10 signals aligned in direction. This ensemble approach filters out the noise of any single oscillator and catches broad-based institutional momentum that no single signal would confirm.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute 10 momentum signals every H1 bar: ROC(5), ROC(10), ROC(20), RSI(14), Aroon Up, DI+ (from ADX), CCI(20), MFI(14), TSV/OBV slope(10), Williams %R(14). 2. Normalize each signal to a 0-100 decile relative to its trailing 50-bar range. 3. Sum all decile scores (range 0-1000) and divide by 10 (range 0-100). 4. LONG entry: ensemble score crosses ABOVE 70 from below 60 AND 6+ of 10 signals are bullish (decile > 50). 5. SHORT entry: ensemble score crosses BELOW 30 from above 40 AND 6+ of 10 signals are bearish (decile < 50). 6. Filter: skip if ensemble score was in extreme zone (70+ or 30-) for fewer than 3 bars - avoids choppy whipsaw entries.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5 ATR from entry (wider than usual because ensemble must actually reverse). Take profit: when ensemble score drops below 60 on a long (or rises above 40 on a short), scale out 50%. Trail remaining 50% with a 1-ATR chandelier stop. Max trade duration: 48 bars. If score drops into neutral (40-60) zone for 10+ bars, close remaining.
archived.failure_mode: Slow-trending markets where momentum oscillates near the threshold without committing - can produce 2-3 small stop-outs before catching a move. Also fails when all 10 signals are directionally aligned but the market reverses sharply (gap reversals on news). Most vulnerable to high-impact event windows where signals lag price action.
archived.diversification_value: All existing momentum ideas use 1-3 indicators (ADX only, Vanna Flow only, MSS, etc.). This is the only ensemble approach that requires 6+ independent momentum signals to agree. It will only fire when momentum is truly broad-based. Also uses decile normalization rather than raw values, making it adaptive to changing volatility.

archived.name: Gamma_Flip_Regime_Divergence
archived.description: Uses dealer gamma positioning (from gold options market - estimated via spot-gamma from GLD options or XAU OTC gamma exposure proxies) to detect when market makers have flipped from long gamma to short gamma. When dealers are short gamma, they cannot fade moves so momentum strategies work. When dealers are long gamma, they fade extremes so mean reversion strategies work. This gamma regime switch precedes price regime changes by 1-3 bars.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Estimate net gamma exposure across dealer books using gamma profile from GLD options chain (daily update, extrapolated to intraday). 2. Compute gamma flip signal: when net gamma crosses from positive to negative (dealers go short gamma), set regime to TRENDING. When from negative to positive (dealers go long gamma), set regime to MEAN-REVERTING. 3. In TRENDING regime: enable momentum entries. 4. In MEAN-REVERTING regime: enable mean reversion entries. 5. Regime switch has a 24-hour minimum lock - no flip-flopping within the same day. 6. Confirm with D1 gamma flip - only trade intraday regime changes aligned with weekly gamma trend.
archived.exit_logic: Not a standalone entry - this is a regime overlay. Risk parameters come from the underlying strategy used. Fail-safe: if gamma flips back within 12 hours of a regime change, close all regime-related positions and wait 24h.
archived.failure_mode: Gamma estimates are imprecise without direct access to OTC dealer books - GLD options provide only a noisy proxy. Works poorly during low-option-volume periods (holidays, pre-NFP summer months). Can also be front-run if gamma flips are widely reported in financial media.
archived.diversification_value: Existing regime filters use price/volatility/macro data (Hurst exponent, yield curves, vol clusters, macro regimes, fractal phases, ATR regimes, intermarket vol). This is the ONLY regime filter based on options market microstructure - it detects regime shifts from the dealer positioning channel, which often leads price-based regime changes by 3-5 bars.

archived.name: Liquidity_Grab_Mean_Reverter
archived.description: Exploits trapped liquidity by entering short when price aggressively sweeps above a recent swing high by 5-10 pips and reverses within 1-2 candles, or long when sweeping below a swing low. Targets the liquidity provider reaction — stop hunts that fail to sustain reveal true order flow direction.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Identify clear swing high and swing low on M15. 2) Mark level at the exact swing extreme. 3) Wait for price to breach level by at least 5 pips (XAUUSD) within 2 candles. 4) Confirm reversal candle: a full-body close back below (for short) or above (for long) the breached level. 5) Enter on close of the confirming candle. 6) Require RSI divergence (price makes new high/low, RSI does not) for higher-conviction entries.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x the distance from entry to the sweeep extreme peak. Take profit 1: 1R (50% position). Take profit 2: 2R (remaining 50%). Trailing stop activated after 1R is hit, using a 0.5R trail. Max hold time: 6 hours — if not hit, exit at market.
archived.failure_mode: Strong trend days where sweep-and-go occurs (price sweeps the level and continues running, not reversing). Most lethal during high-impact news (NFP, FOMC) when liquidity is absorbed by genuine institutional orders rather than retail stops. Also fails in low-liquidity Asian session when stops are too shallow.
archived.diversification_value: Unlike Wick_Exhaustion_Reverter (general wick analysis) or FVG_Imbalance_Fill (gap fills), this targets a specific microstructure pattern — structural stop hunts. It is event-dependent rather than purely statistical, offering a different risk profile that is uncorrelated with standard mean reversion during ranging markets.

archived.name: Intraday_VaR_Regime_Adaptive_Sizer
timeframes: Any — overlay applicable to any entry strategy
archived.description: Dynamic position sizing overlay that computes a 2-hour rolling VaR (95th percentile of intraday range) to classify the current risk regime as quiet, normal, or volatile. Position size scales inversely: full size in quiet, standard size in normal, reduced in volatile. Prevents over-trading in wild markets and under-trading in tame ones.
archived.entry_logic: 1) On each bar close, compute rolling VaR: take absolute returns over the last 120 candles (2h on M1, or equivalent), sort ascending, pick the 95th percentile value. 2) Compare to a rolling 24h median of VaR values. 3) Classify regime: VaR < 0.7x median = QUIET; 0.7x-1.3x median = NORMAL; > 1.3x median = VOLATILE. 4) Scale position size: QUIET=1.2x base, NORMAL=1.0x base, VOLATILE=0.5x base. 5) Apply a 3-candle smoothing filter to regime changes to prevent flip-flopping on single outlier bars. 6) Override to NORMAL during the first 30 minutes of London open (structural volatility).
archived.exit_logic: No direct exits — this is a sizing overlay. It modifies position size of whatever entry strategy it is attached to. The exit belongs to the parent strategy. Implicitly, when VaR spikes sharply (3x+ median), a temporary position reduction or halt is triggered regardless of parent rules, protecting against flash events.
archived.failure_mode: Breaking news where volatility instantly gaps (no intraday range to compute from). VaR lags as it is inherently historical. Also vulnerable to low-volatility regime shifts where VaR says QUIET but a volatility explosion is imminent (e.g., Friday afternoon NFP release). The smoothing filter adds delay to regime changes, which cuts both ways.
archived.diversification_value: Unlike Volatility_Parity_Scale (ATR-based, daily) and VaR_Trailing_Stop_Overlay (uses VaR for stops), this uses intraday VaR specifically for position SIZING with a 3-candle regime smoothing filter. The intraday window (2h vs 24h+ for most VaR approaches) captures micro-regimes that daily measures miss.

archived.name: NFP_Week_Mean_Reversion_Bias
archived.description: Exploits the statistical tendency of gold to over-extend on major US macro releases (NFP, CPI, FOMC) and then mean revert within 12-24 hours as initial liquidity is absorbed. Targets the retracement leg rather than the breakout direction, betting that the fundamental shock is priced in within hours of release.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Monitor US macro calendar for NFP (1st Friday), CPI (mid-month), FOMC decisions. 2) Wait for release. 3) Identify the initial 1-hour spike range (high and low of the first H1 candle after release). 4) If range > 1.5x the average 1H ATR of the past 5 days, mark as high-volatility event. 5) Enter mean reversion 6 hours after the release: if price closed above the 1H spike range midpoint, go SHORT; if below, go LONG. 6) Add RSI confirmation: RSI must be > 70 (short) or < 30 (long) on the H1 at entry time.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x the initial spike range. Take profit: 0.5x the initial spike range (first 50%), 0.75x (remaining 50%). Hard exit: 24 hours after release regardless of PnL — the reversion window closes. If price breaks beyond the initial spike extreme by 1x the spike range, exit immediately (failed hypothesis).
archived.failure_mode: Non-reversion events where the fundamental shock is sustained (e.g., surprise rate hike that changes the macro outlook for weeks). Also fails during risk-off weeks where multiple events compound in the same direction. Most lethal: when the spike range is small (< 1x ATR) and there is no over-extension to revert from.
archived.diversification_value: Unlike Event_Window_Seasonal_Compression (trades the BREAKOUT during compression) and Holiday_Liquidity_Vacuum_Rebound (holiday-specific), this specifically trades the POST-EVENT mean reversion with a fixed 6h entry delay and 24h hard exit. It is a pure contrarian macro play with no directional bias, complementing directional event-driven strategies.

archived.name: Futures_Spot_Convergence_Arbitrage
archived.description: Trades the mean-reverting spread between gold spot (XAUUSD) and the active gold futures contract. During high-volatility events or liquidity dislocations, the futures basis widens far beyond fair carry cost. The strategy fades extreme basis deviations when the spread exceeds 2 standard deviations of its 20-period rolling mean, targeting convergence at the next fixing window or session close.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute basis = futures_price - spot_price (normalized by contract multiplier). 2. Calculate rolling 20-period z-score of basis on H1. 3. When z-score > +2.0 (futures overpriced relative to spot): SHORT futures / LONG spot (via synthetic spread). 4. When z-score < -2.0 (futures underpriced): LONG futures / SHORT spot. 5. Confirmation: basis must have diverged for at least 3 consecutive bars (rejects flash spikes). 6. Enter at market only during London or NY session (highest liquidity, tightest spread execution).
archived.exit_logic: SL: 1.5x ATR(14) of the basis spread itself. TP: z-score returns to 0 (fair value). Trail: if z-score crosses back within +/-1.0, trail at 50% of remaining convergence. Max hold: 24 hours - forced flat at next London fix if unconverged.
archived.failure_mode: Structural regime change in gold market (e.g., backwardation during physical delivery squeeze, or contango blowout during a liquidity crisis). The basis may not converge for weeks during such events. Also: execution slippage on the synthetic spread can destroy the thin edge.
archived.diversification_value: Solely focuses on the futures-spot basis, a pure microstructure/arbitrage dimension untouched by all 8 existing cross_asset ideas (which cover DXY, silver ratio, real yields, gamma, Vanna, CRB, and mining equities). Zero beta to gold directional moves - profit from convergence alone. Near-market-neutral.

archived.name: Interbank_Fixing_Flow_Reversal
archived.description: Exploits the well-documented gold fixing effect: in the 30-minute window before the London AM Fix (10:30 UTC) and PM Fix (15:00 UTC), order flow builds as dealers and central banks queue fix orders. This creates directional pressure that peaks at the fix print. In the 30 minutes post-fix, the artificial flow exhausts and price reverts partially or fully. The strategy enters a fade trade 5 minutes after the fix timestamp, targeting the pre-fix origin.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Identify fix windows: London AM Fix (10:30 UTC), London PM Fix (15:00 UTC). 2. Monitor M5 price action 60 min pre-fix. Measure total bar-to-bar excursion (High-Low sum). 3. Record fix-price at the exact fix minute (timestamp from LBMA or ICE benchmark). 4. Wait 5 minutes after fix for initial volatility to settle. 5. If pre-fix net move >0.3% of spot price: enter counter-directional trade at market. 6. If pre-fix move <0.3%: skip (no significant flow to fade). 7. Check: no high-impact news within +/-15 min of fix (reject if NFP, FOMC, CPI).
archived.exit_logic: SL: pre-fix excursion distance + 0.1% buffer. TP1 (50%): 50% of pre-fix excursion retraced. TP2 (50%): full retrace to pre-fix opening price. Hard stop: London session close - carry no position across NY open. If pre-fix move continues post-fix for 3 consecutive M15 bars, exit at breakeven (flow was sustained, not artificial).
archived.failure_mode: Central bank intervention or large real-money fix orders that overwhelm the fade (e.g., reserve rebalancing at month-end). During extreme macro events, the fix window flow is directional and does not reverse. Low-volatility days produce insufficient excursion to trade.
archived.diversification_value: Existing other-category ideas cover orderflow imbalance, session exhaustion, pivot bounces, COT fades, gap fills, and central bank reserve trends - but none specifically target the gold fixing window microstructure. This is a pure calendar-based event arbitrage that thrives in normal-volatility conditions when other strategies are flat.

archived.name: Open_Interest_Divergence_Trend_Decay
archived.description: Tracks daily Open Interest (OI) changes in gold futures alongside price action to detect structural trend health. Healthy trends see rising OI + rising price (new money entering). Exhausting trends see falling OI + rising price (short covering / distribution). When price makes a new swing high but OI declines vs its 10-day smoothed rate of change, the trend is structurally weak and due for a reversal or sharp pullback. The strategy enters anti-trend on this divergence signal, unlike existing momentum ideas that follow momentum.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Fetch daily GC futures OI data (from CFTC or exchange). 2. Compute OI_ROC = 10-day rate of change of OI. 3. Compute price_ROC = 10-day rate of change of spot price. 4. On H4 chart, identify a swing high (closing price > previous 10 bars). 5. CONFIRMING SIGNAL: price_ROC > +3% AND OI_ROC < -2% (bearish divergence - price up, OI down). 6. OR: swing low with price_ROC < -3% AND OI_ROC > +2% (bullish divergence - price down, OI up). 7. Enter at the close of the H4 bar that prints the divergence. 8. Skip if ATR(14) > 2x its 50-day average (extreme volatility regime pollutes OI signal).
archived.exit_logic: SL: 1.5x ATR(14) on H4 beyond the swing point. TP1 (33%): 1:1 risk/reward. TP2 (33%): OI_ROC crosses back through zero. TP3 (34%): trail at 25-bar EMA on H4. Max hold: 14 calendar days - OI data inherently slow, signal decays after 2 weeks.
archived.failure_mode: Lag: OI data is released with 1-3 day delay (CFTC weekly commitments). For daily exchange OI (CME), still end-of-day only. Intra-week reversals cannot use this. Also: OI divergence can persist for weeks during parabolic blow-off tops - early entry gets crushed.
archived.diversification_value: All 8 existing momentum ideas use price/volume/momentum oscillators (ADX, Donchian, Vanna flow, MSS, decile ensembles). None use Open Interest divergence as a primary signal. This is a structural, slow-frequency momentum-exhaustion detector that complements fast intraday momentum bots. It signals WHEN momentum is about to die, not when to ride it.

archived.name: Central_Bank_Calendar_Dovish_Hawkish_Window
archived.description: Captures the 48-hour directional drift following major central bank rate decisions (FOMC, ECB, BOE, BOJ, SNB). Gold trends sharply in the direction of the real-yield delta for ~2 sessions post-announcement, then mean-reverts. Entry at the first H1 close after the announcement, exit before the 48-hour window closes.
archived.entry_logic: Track upcoming central bank events via economic calendar. At the first H1 candle close after the rate decision (or statement), compute real-yield delta (prevailing yield vs pre-announcement). Enter long if real yields dropped more than 5bps vs expectation; short if real yields rose more than 5bps. Use a 1.5x ATR trailing stop from entry.
archived.exit_logic: Hard exit at 47 hours post-announcement (before reversion sets in). Trailing stop 1.5x ATR. If price reaches 2.5x ATR profit, take 50% partial and move stop to breakeven.
archived.failure_mode: Non-taper-tantrum macro regime where real-yield moves are noisy (e.g., yield curve control, quantitative easing with forward guidance). Also fails in zero-volatility environments where the delta is too small to trade above spread.
archived.diversification_value: No existing seasonal idea targets the 48-hour central-bank decision window specifically — most focus on lunar/calendar/turn-of-month effects. This is event-driven seasonality rather than date-driven seasonality.

archived.name: Sharpe_Ratio_Rotator
archived.description: Dynamic capital allocation overlay that rotates risk budget between all active strategies based on trailing 20-period Sharpe ratios. If a strategy's Sharpe drops below 0.3, its allocation is halved and redistributed to the highest-Sharpe strategy. Prevents capital from sitting in decaying strategies while overweighting regimes where a particular strategy excels.
archived.entry_logic: No direct entry — this is an overlay. At each H1 close, compute rolling 20-period Sharpe ratio for every active bot strategy. Rank strategies by Sharpe. Top-ranked gets +30% of freed capital, 2nd gets +20%, rest split proportionally. Any strategy trailing Sharpe < 0.3 for 40 consecutive periods gets zeroed out until it recovers above 0.5.
archived.exit_logic: Not applicable — permanent overlay. Rebalances every H1 candle. Full rebalance triggered if any strategy hits a trailing 40-period drawdown > 15%.
archived.failure_mode: False signal in strongly trending markets where mean-reversion strategies have negative Sharpe for legitimate reasons (they should be disabled, which is correct behavioral — but catching the re-entry point is noisy). Also suffers from look-ahead bias if backward-looking Sharpe doesn't anticipate regime change.
archived.diversification_value: All existing risk overlays (Kelly, VaR, volatility parity, drawdown lock) are static sizing rules. This is the first dynamic inter-strategy capital allocator in the archive — it treats the strategy suite as a portfolio and optimizes weightings online.

archived.name: VWAP_Vol_Channel_Mean_Drift
archived.description: Price oscillates within VWAP-based volatility channels that expand and contract with ATR. When the channel width (upper VWAP+2σ - lower VWAP-2σ) contracts below its 14-period minimum (a volatility squeeze), the subsequent expansion produces a high-probability directional drift. Entry is in the pre-squeeze trend direction, measured by VWAP slope over the squeeze duration.
archived.entry_logic: Compute VWAP(20) plus dynamic bands: band_width = VWAP ± (2 * ATR(14)). Track channel_width = upper_band - lower_band. When channel_width drops below its 14-period lowest value (squeeze detection), record VWAP slope over the last 5 bars. On the candle that breaks the upper band (if VWAP slope > 0) or lower band (if slope < 0), enter long/short with 0.5% risk of account.
archived.exit_logic: Take profit: 1.5x the pre-squeeze channel width projected upward/downward. Stop loss: 0.75x the pre-squeeze channel width on the opposite side. Trail after price reaches 1x channel width in profit.
archived.failure_mode: Fails in sideways congestion with repeated false squeezes (channel compresses, breaks, then immediately fades). Also fails in high-frequency whip around VWAP during low-liquidity sessions where the squeeze metric oscillates rapidly.
archived.diversification_value: Existing volatility ideas focus on volatility contraction-breakout, skew, term structure, and implied-realized spread. None use VWAP-anchored dynamic band compression as a volatility squeeze trigger. This bridges volatility and trend-following in a unique way.

archived.name: Monsoon_India_Demand_Frontrun
archived.description: Uses real-time Indian monsoon rainfall deviation (IMD cumulative rainfall index vs 50-year normal) as a 2-3 month leading indicator of rural physical gold demand. Poor monsoon (rainfall deficit >10% by mid-season) forces rural India (60%+ of total gold demand) to increase gold buying as an inflation hedge 8-12 weeks ahead of the Oct-Feb wedding season peak. The strategy builds a long position in July-September when monsoon data confirms deficit, targets the seasonal rally Oct-Feb, and closes ahead of March post-wedding lull.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Track IMD cumulative monsoon rainfall index vs 1961-2010 normal daily from June 1 through September 30. 2. At the midpoint of monsoon season (July 31), compute aggregate deviation %. 3. If deviation < -10% (deficit monsoon): initiate a long position at first weekly close >20-week SMA in August, targeting Oct-Feb rally. 4. If deviation > +5% (normal/surplus): no position; skip the season. 5. If DXY is in a confirmed uptrend (above 200-day SMA), reduce position size by 50% to account for USD strength headwind. 6.
