archived.diversification_value: Only HMM-based regime filter in the archive. Completely decorrelated from all existing ADX/ATR/macro regime approaches — captures statistical regime structure rather than deterministic threshold-based regimes. Would have near-zero correlation with any existing bot.

archived.name: Gold_Bitcoin_Divergence_Rotator
archived.description: Gold and Bitcoin increasingly compete as store-of-value / safe-haven assets, but trade on different liquidity channels (gold: institutional, CB reserves; BTC: retail/ETF flows, digital-native). When rolling 30-day correlation exceeds +0.65 (regime of convergence) or drops below -0.20 (divergence), fade the move back toward the 90-day mean correlation of ~0.25. No existing cross_asset idea uses BTC correlation at all.
archived.entry_logic: 1. Compute 30-day Pearson correlation of daily returns (XAUUSD vs BTCUSD). 2. Compute 90-day rolling mean and std of that correlation. 3. IF z-score of current 30-day correlation > 2.0 (unusually high convergence) — expect mean reversion in correlation. Short the stronger asset, long the weaker. 4. IF z-score < -1.5 (unusual divergence) — expect convergence. Long the lagging asset, short the leading. 5. Entry only when both assets have >$50 daily range (avoid low-vol noise). 6. Check DXY direction: if DXY > 20-day EMA, prefer short gold side. 7. Position size: equal notional, 0.5% risk per leg.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x ATR(14) on each leg, or correlation z-score moves another 1.0 in same direction (stop out if divergence continues). Take profit: correlation z-score returns to 0 (neutral). Time stop: exit after 10 bars if not triggered, as correlation regimes have limited persistence. Rebalance daily.
archived.failure_mode: Structural breakdown: if gold and BTC permanently decouple (e.g., CBDCs displace BTC as digital gold), the historical correlation anchor drifts. BTC can gap 10%+ on crypto-native events (exchange hacks, regulatory bans) that leave gold unchanged — the pair correlation becomes meaningless noise during crypto-specific shocks.
archived.diversification_value: Only strategy in the archive using BTC correlation with gold. Cross-asset ideas currently cover DXY, US10Y, TIPS, SPX, XAGUSD, USOIL, GDX, CRB indexes — but zero crypto exposure. This adds a completely orthogonal asset class dimension. Also distinct from pair-trade mean reversion (which is intra-asset-class); this is inter-asset-class correlation rotator.

archived.name: Kalman_Filter_Dynamic_Mean_Reversion
archived.description: Uses a Kalman filter to estimate the dynamic, time-varying mean of gold prices — rather than a fixed moving average or fixed Bollinger band center. When price deviates >1.5x the Kalman prediction error (innovation) on M15, fade aggressively. The Kalman filter adapts to changing volatility and trend components automatically, unlike static Bollinger/MA mean reversion. No existing mean_reversion idea uses Kalman filtering.
archived.entry_logic: 1. State vector: [price_level, trend_slope]. Observation: H1 close. Process noise covariance Q and observation noise R estimated via 5-day rolling MLE. 2. Kalman predict-update cycle yields: predicted price (k_t|t-1), innovation (residual between actual and predicted), and innovation variance S_t. 3. ENTRY CONDITION: |innovation| > 1.5 * sqrt(S_t) AND the innovation is in the opposite direction of the last 3 consecutive 15-min candle direction (divergence confirmation). 4. For long: price significantly below Kalman estimate AND last 3 M15 candles are bearish (exhaustion). 5. For short: symmetric. 6. Filter out entries when Kalman trend_slope > 0.3 ATR/day (too strong trend, don't fade). 7. Enter at market, 0.75% risk.
archived.exit_logic: Stop loss: 0.8x ATR(14) from entry (tight — Kalman reversion tends to be sharp). Take profit 1: 50% at innovation returns to 0 (price re-meets Kalman estimate). Take profit 2: 50% at 1.0x innovation in opposite direction (overshoot the other side). Fail-safe: if Kalman re-estimates such that current price becomes the new mean (innovation shrinks below 0.5x S_t while still in loss), exit at breakeven or -0.3 ATR max loss — the filter is saying the mean has moved.
archived.failure_mode: Kalman filter can take time to converge after structural breaks (gap openings, NFP spikes). During high-vol news events, the innovation threshold is too tight — gets stopped out repeatedly. Process noise parameters chosen by rolling MLE can produce unstable estimates during low-liquidity Asian session. Most dangerous failure: Kalman diverges (filter becomes overconfident in wrong state) during sustained trending moves, causing repeated fade losses.
archived.diversification_value: First Kalman filter-based strategy in the archive. Completely different mathematical foundation from existing mean reversion ideas (which use: z-score of EMA, Bollinger distance, VWAP entropy, FVG fills, order flow exhaustion, COT extremes). Kalman provides a dynamic state-space approach that adapts faster than fixed-period oscillators and handles non-stationary price processes naturally. Should show very low correlation with all 13 existing mean reversion strategies.

archived.name: Breakout_Volume_Climax_Fade
archived.description: Fades breakouts when price reaches a prior resistance-turned-support zone with volume climax divergence. Unlike existing fade strategies that fade failed breakouts generally, this waits for the breakout to actually reach a historical resistance level and then identifies exhaustion via volume spike + delta divergence on that specific candle.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Identify a structural resistance level (at least 2 touches on H1). 2) Price breaks above it cleanly. 3) Price returns to retest the old resistance as new support. 4) On the retest candle, volume spikes 1.8x above 20-period average AND cumulative delta shows divergence (weaker bullish delta on the retest than on the initial breakout). 5) Enter short at the close of the retest candle. 6) Stop loss 1.5x ATR above retest high. Take profit at next structural support below. Trailing stop after 1:1 R:R.
archived.exit_logic: Initial SL: 1.5x ATR above retest high. TP1: next structural support below (50% position, 1:1 R:R). TP2: move SL to breakeven and trail with ATR chandelier stop on remaining 50%. Breach of entry zone after 3 candles invalidates.
archived.failure_mode: Strong trending markets where resistance is continuously overcome (no exhaustion). Delta divergence false positives during news events. Works poorly during high-impact news where volume spikes are non-structural.
archived.diversification_value: Only breakout strategy that specifically fades breakouts REACHING historical levels with volume climax. Complementary to False_Breakout_Trap_Fade (which fades immediate break failures) and Structural_Level_Breakout_With_Retest (which rides the breakout retest long).

archived.name: Fiscal_Year_End_Cross_Border_Demand
archived.description: Capitalises on predictable gold demand surges tied to fiscal year-ends of the three largest gold-consuming nations: India (Mar 31), China (Dec 31), and USA (Sep 30 fiscal, Dec 31 tax). Each creates a distinct 2-4 week window of physical buying pressure as institutions adjust balance sheets.
archived.entry_logic: 1) For each fiscal year-end date, define a 15-day pre-window and 5-day post-window. 2) India (Mar): enter long at Mar 15 close. 3) China (Dec): enter long at Dec 10 close. 4) USA (Sep): enter Sep 15 close. 5) USA (Dec): enter Dec 10 close. 6) Scale position size by historical average return for each window. 7) Use 50-period SMA as trend filter - only go long if price is above SMA.
archived.exit_logic: Fixed exit on window end date. India: exit Apr 5. China: exit Jan 5. USA Sep: exit Oct 5. USA Dec: exit Jan 5. Hard stop at 1.5x ATR below entry. If a major central bank rate decision falls within the window, exit half before the event.
archived.failure_mode: Macro shocks override seasonal patterns entirely. USD strength during India/China windows can negate gold gains. Calendar effects drift as cultural buying habits change.
archived.diversification_value: Only seasonal strategy targeting fiscal year-end institutional flows. Uncorrelated with Diwali_Chinese_New_Year_Physical_Demand_Frontrun (different time windows) and Gold_Seasonal_Cycle (broad annual cycle).

archived.name: Gamma_Exposure_Floor_Ceiling_Liquidity
archived.description: Uses options market gamma exposure data to identify dealer long-gamma zones (stability/mean reversion) vs short-gamma zones (momentum acceleration). When gamma flips at a key level, the market becomes unstable and prone to directional runs. When gamma is strongly positive, price reverts toward max pain.
archived.entry_logic: 1) Load daily GLD/XAUUSD options gamma profile (or proxy via VIX term structure + put/call ratio). 2) Identify high-gamma strike zone (dealers long gamma, expect mean reversion). 3) Identify low/negative gamma zones (dealers short gamma, expect acceleration). 4) When price approaches a high-gamma zone from above: enter long. 5) From below: enter short. 6) If price breaks through a high-gamma zone with speed (1.5x ATR in 2 candles) + delta confirms: abandon mean reversion and enter in breakout direction (gamma flip signal). 7) Scale by gamma concentration.
archived.exit_logic: Mean-reversion mode: exit at high-gamma strike center or after 2:1 R:R with trailing stop. Gamma-flip breakout mode: trail with ATR chandelier (3x ATR). Hard stop at 1x ATR below/above gamma flip candle. If gamma profile shifts significantly intraday, flatten all positions.
archived.failure_mode: Requires reliable options data - not available to all retail traders. Gamma profiles update daily at best. Low-options-volume environments degrade signals. Weekend gaps can violate gamma zones.
archived.diversification_value: Only hypothesis in archive directly using options gamma positioning for spot gold. Complements Gamma_Flip_Regime_Divergence (regime_filter) but at discrete trade entry level. Differs from Swap_Dealer_Gamma_Speed_Trap (expiry-focused).
